# Recursion — the linguistics engine on crystallized forms

Status: consolidated specification with a bound implementation. Written
against `/opt/mycelium-v0.1.0` at a29bba5 (2026-09-05). This text replaces
every earlier version of this file: the earlier versions accreted parts
that amended one another by reference; this one is a single closed form in
which every statement stands where it applies. Companion documents:
`ALPHABET.md`, `MU-ENGINEERING.md`, `MU-ECONOMY.md`, `XSEPTUM.md`.

## How to read this document

Ten parts, fifty chapters, each chapter self-contained enough to
implement and each opening with what it carries from the one before.

| part | what it settles | who reads it first |
|---|---|---|
| I Geometry | what a word, a form, a move, a recursion **is** | everyone |
| II Cohomology | why the moves are sound: cochains, Mayer–Vietoris, Leray, naturality | the auditor; the implementor of the court |
| III Identity and algorithms | the component procedures and master algorithms every key, address, chart, class, comprehension, pivot, and route passes through | the implementor, before writing any code |
| IV Implementation on forms | every move bound to a function at an absolute path and line | the implementor |
| V Migration and exact strings | how the tree changes without stopping the fleet; the literal refusal reasons and log lines | the implementor and the auditor |
| VI Extensions | the two walls and how they come down without changing what a word is | later |
| VII Verification and landing | every test, every cold-boot trace, one landing order, and the theorems the engine proves by running | the auditor |
| VIII Boundaries | what is deliberately absent; relayed statements not adopted | everyone, once |
| IX The mesh under adversaries | time without clocks, threshold identity, receipts and the signed prefix, equivocation, settlement | the implementor of the court and the wire; the auditor |
| X Language formation | the sentence as the unit of speech: construction and deconstruction as adjoint functors, edge transport in the stabilizer, ordered factorization, typed demands, the three seams | the implementor of the voice and the court; the auditor |

**What this document is.** A specification of the implementation at
`/opt/mycelium-v0.1.0`, every statement bound to a function and a path,
never a survey. It began on 2026-09-05 (a6a21a9) as the recursion
specification, was rewritten as moves on crystallized forms (1f2db2d), and
consolidated into one closed form (4e2641d). Its identity ruling (1.5,
88f58e1) stated from the start that identity is re-derived and that
digests are transport only. The algorithms written after it (b6758e5,
9481243) reintroduced digests of canonical forms as keys, and the class
vector, the certificate, and the address were then written the same way.
That drift lost the coordinates the connecting maps and the naturality
squares need, and it is corrected on 2026-09-06 by laws 2, 11 and 12 as
now written and by A21: keys are coordinates, carriages are versors, every
dimension is a proof. Chapter 1.7 states why, once, so that no later
convenience reopens the question. Chapters 12.6, 15.4, 16, 17.2, 18.2, 19,
21, 35 and 47 were rewritten under that correction; a reader of an earlier
revision should not trust its keys. The same day found a second shadow
carried as the carrier: since 04931ab the class vector read the plane form
first and the rotor's conjugacy class as a fallback, so the
two-dimensional projection of a four-dimensional holonomy was primary;
12.6, 15.3, 16.3 and 3.10 now put the rotor first and name the "sheet" as
what it is, the orientation character of a half-turn through a third
axis. **What the drift cost.** Every class key, certificate and tape
written between 04931ab and de6fa58 was keyed by digests and is not
comparable with anything after 38ee193; the soak readings of Cut B before
38ee193 are void; the identity recut cost one landing (38ee193) and one
residue commit (75e26eb) before any new chapter could land. The task list
keeps a dated backtrack ledger so this is not paid twice.

## The laws this document is written under

These are not restated in each chapter; every chapter assumes them.

1. **Geometry, not trigonometry or calculus.** A rotation is an exact rotor
   over ℚ; its angle is never formed. No norms or roots beyond an exact
   rational square root that refuses when inexact. No limits, series,
   derivatives, or probabilities. Termination is by an integer measure or
   a `Budget`. Nothing is scored; things are equal, or they are not, and
   a reading of two lane vectors says per lane which fell, held or rose.
2. **Identity is content, never bytes and never a digest of content.** Two
   words are equal when their rotors are projectively equal. A key is the
   canonical coordinates of an exact object written out, in a fixed order,
   length-prefixed, so that the object is recovered from its key and a
   prefix of the key is a coarser stratum (A21). No hash, fingerprint, or
   digest of any mathematical structure exists in cognition: a digest maps
   a stratified exact vector to a rank-zero point, keeps equality and loses
   every coordinate, every prefix, every composition, and therefore every
   map of data (15.1) and every connecting map (13.4). The master equation
   is naturality: `φ*(key(c)) = key(φ*(c))` for every map `φ` of 15.1, which
   a digest cannot satisfy. Digests exist only where bytes are the object:
   signatures, receipt chains, wire and file integrity (Part IX). Byte
   exactness is never what is checked; the mathematics adding up is
   (chapter 1.5; the reason, stated once, is chapter 1.7).
3. **No enumeration.** Indices come from a keyed read, a peel, a link, or a
   `Budget` cursor. No loop over peers, pairs, degrees, or planes that the
   carrier does not already name. `HashMap` and `BTreeMap` do not appear in
   cognition; the relational field is a `Keyed` PATRICIA trie or a
   `Vec` of relations.
4. **Exact ℚ; refuse rather than round.** Every scalar is a rational (or,
   in Part VI, an element of a cyclotomic field with canonical reduction).
   **A reading is as exact as its carrier** (78.45, ruled 2026-09-25, the
   operator's word: precision, not blob, not approximation): it serves
   the value where exact, else the exact fraction, else the exact
   rational point, else the SECTOR between two exact marks the point
   lies in, decided by comparison over ℚ or over the cyclotomic field
   the resolution names; no decimal approximation of an irrational is
   served anywhere, not as a value and not as a "reading marked
   irrational". Resolution is the number of exact marks, never digits.
5. **Polytonic lanes.** μ⃗ = (S, G, T, H) is never summed, ordered, or
   reduced to a scalar; a comparison of two lane vectors returns the
   reading per lane and never a verdict, and no lane falling certifies
   anything (12.6).
6. **The alphabet is immutable to a voice and grown only by the court**
   (ruled 2026-09-10; before that date, immutable). Seventeen letters are
   the base; words are their combinations; vertex equality is projective
   rotor equality, never tape equality; the normal form is the geodesic
   where one exists. No voice adds a letter, no configuration adds a
   letter and no commit adds a letter: a letter beyond the seventeen is
   opened by the court alone, on a typed demand whose witness rotor two
   independent courts re-derived to one Gaussian factor at one chart
   (arity-2 consilience, 37.7), ruled with a receipt, and taught by the
   syllabus before any voice speaks it. An opened letter is
   named on every tape by its content, never by an index assigned in open
   order, since open order is a total order across nodes (law 9) and a
   content name composes where an index cannot (law 2). What this
   restores was never a mathematical limit: the letter a prime demands is
   the witness rotor's own factor, read exactly, and the seventeen were
   frozen by doctrine, not by arithmetic (36.3). The two organs of a
   letter's consilience are two independent courts, never two voices: a
   letter is no exception to 47.3 (ruled 2026-09-10). **The readings of
   the scene cover are governed as the letters are** (ruled 2026-09-19,
   chapter 53): a fixed roster, grown only by a court receipt on a probe,
   never by a voice and never by a commit.
7. **Residuals are never discarded.** A remainder is the exact demand. The
   one exception is a computed class that Leray's theorem shows to be an
   artefact of a spanning tree (chapter 14.8); it was never a class.
8. **Clients think, hyphae verify.** Cognition is the mind's; a hypha
   replays, judges, keeps the ledger, and stores the genome. Sentences
   only (ruled 2026-09-10): a voice sends the court sentences and nothing
   else, the court replays them by G and never composes by F, and the
   wire never carries raw percept laminae to a court. A court that
   extracts boundaries, measures versors or peels letters is thinking,
   and a second engine; the four `from_residual` sites of the court's
   reduction were that engine (50.6, 50.9). *(Read as amended by 78.102,
   2026-10-05: a sentence is any composition by the master equation,
   closed or open; an open sentence carrying an ineffable word is heard,
   replayed, and its letter offered.)*
9. **No clock but the ledger.** No kernel reads a wall clock, a unix clock,
   or a timer. K is a kernel's own receipt index and orders events inside
   that kernel; TUniversal is the height of the mesh's receipt ledger, read
   from receipts, and measures standing; order across nodes is the causal
   partial order of receipts and is never totalised (Part IX). Lane T of μ⃗
   is temporal extent counted in receipts, a cost, never a coordinate.
10. **Direction is a pivot, never a gradient.** A held orbit is discharged
    by a move on one of the axes its class vector occupies (chapters 3.9,
    12.6, 16.16). The candidate moves are read from the class vector in a
    fixed order, each is tried exactly, no move waits on another's failure,
    and reduction against held words is one of the moves and never a
    precondition; every one that discharges is kept. There is no list of
    directions and no loop over "descend, then ascend": there is the
    vector, read before anything is reduced, and each occupied coordinate
    names the one move that can zero it (16.16, chapter 5, ruled
    2026-09-08). **Closure certifies** a pivot after it is made: the coordinate it
    acted on is zero, no other rose, and the rank moved by its one unit or
    not at all; the lane reading of a trial refuses a candidate that raises
    a lane by naming the lane. Nothing on μ⃗ and nothing in the rank audit
    chooses among pivots, and no scalar ever orders the candidates. Several
    candidates that discharge are held together as a superposition, the
    vortex, until a perception or a court replay collapses it.
11. **No squaring.** The sensor's ℤ² is the substrate a hypha reads laminae
    from; it is not a space cognition lives in, and ℚ² is ℤ² squared
    again. Cognition never carries a position, a placement, or a shift as
    a pair of numbers. A placement is a conformal translator, a dilation a
    dilator, both versors of the conformal algebra (A4), composed with the
    rotor words by the geometric product; the class vector of a loop is
    the blade decomposition of its canonical holonomy versor, and its
    placement axis is the translator component of that versor. A pair of
    coordinates appears only at the sensor boundary, in `extract_rule_with`,
    `speak_rule`, and `orbit`, where a lamina is read or written. **The
    lamina is the sensor's token, never the mind's carrier** (ruled
    2026-09-17, evening): a chain's links `(r, c, before, after)` and a
    support's laminae `(r, c, k, hue)` are read once at intake (`perceive`,
    `germinate`, A5's centering), computed on only where a sentence is
    replayed against what the sensor read (`chain::replay_operators`, the
    court's `vertices_carry_family`) and where a grid is written
    (`speak_rule`, `orbit`), and between those places they are carried as
    content: the mind acts on the POSE — A5's translator, the carriage,
    the transport — and compares bodies by the versor between their shapes
    and the gauge. The sensor's own readers (`element/sensor.rs`: the site
    of a point, a lamina's center and a whole lamina carried, the
    pullback) read the three coordinates of the base (51.1) exactly or
    refuse: a carried lamina whose image is not a lamina of one frame, or
    an exact block of them, is refused, never rounded to the laminae whose
    centres its image spans. Fluid physics carried in squares is squares
    of fluid: looking for a square inside a circle is a search for two
    different objects (chapters 1.4, 1.7, 16.4). **No matrix carries an
    action.** A matrix is a linear
    representation on a fixed set of squared coordinates: it holds only
    what that frame can hold, its product forgets the blade structure of
    what it represents, and a new axis is a larger matrix rather than a
    new grade. That is flattening and rigidity in one object, and it is
    why an action re-derived through a matrix loses coordinates the class
    vector, the pivots and the connecting maps need. Every action in this
    engine is an element of an exact algebra composed by its own product:
    a rotor or versor by the geometric product, a gauge by permutation
    composition. An action on the vectors — a versor's twisted adjoint, or
    a sum of them — is a linear function held by its images of the
    generators (`cga::LinearFunction`): composed by application, its trace
    the vector derivative's, its projectors polynomials in it, its kernel
    the solutions of the equations its images set. A dimension is the grade
    of a span, the blade its vectors wedge to, held by its factors (A18,
    `core::span`): no matrix, no rank of one. Integer rows appear only as a word's letter exponents, whose
    Hermite form factors it (A12, `core::exponents`), and a matrix only as
    the sensor-plane block a rotor projects to (A3), never as the carrier
    of an element (18.3).
12. **Every dimension is a proof.** A letter is an axiom. A word is a
    proof: a path whose vertex is the theorem it reaches, and a form
    **re-derives that vertex by composing the word's derivation** — the
    cited generators to their exponents, times the residue — never by
    reading a stored spelling (1.5, 50.2 step 2). A crystallized
    form is a gemstone: each of its loops is a theorem, proved by the
    identity of the holonomy the words around it compose, and one theorem
    has as many proofs as the form has synonyms of one class (13.10). Every
    coordinate of a form is a theorem the form proves by re-derivation; a
    coordinate that is not is not a dimension of the form but a section
    coordinate carried beside it. Nothing is a dimension because it was
    stored (chapters 1.7, 2.3, 42).

## Coding standards: the rules that stop the crud before it is written

The laws above say what the engine is. These rules say how code that
implements it must be written, so that a reviewer can refuse a change on
sight and an implementor does not spend a cycle writing what the next audit
removes. Every rule below was extracted from a defect that actually landed
in this tree; the "looks like" column is the shape that landed, the "write
instead" column is what replaced it. A change that contains a "looks like"
shape is not reviewed further; it is returned.

| # | rule | looks like (refused) | write instead |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **A pair loop is allowed only over one site's own vertices or one loop's own faces.** Iterating `i < j` over bodies, vertices, charts, hyphae, or peers is a correspondence search over a product the carrier already names. | `for i in 0..n { for j in i+1..n { if related(i, j) … } }`; `bodies_in.iter().find(…)` for every `bodies_out`; `for lane in 0..4 { for h in hyphae … }` where the lane is not a fixed physical size | build one keyed occupancy once, `Keyed<site key → Vec<vertex>>`, read pairs out of sites holding two or more vertices, probe a ring site into the same key; a site's own vertices and a loop's own faces are its boundary and may be walked |
| 2 | **A count is never a branch.** A decision that reads `len()`, `count()`, or `n <= k` is a boolean gate on a count, and the count is not a measurement of anything. | `if n_words <= 1 { all bodies }`; `if germs.len() >= 2 { true }`; `if counts.len() == n_pairs` as the whole test | the fiber decides: `atlas.fiber(class)` names the bodies a vertex speaks to and an empty fiber is remainder, never "everything"; presence is read from a keyed set, not from a length |
| 3 | **Equality is `same_vertex`, `projective_eq`, or class-vector equality.** `==` on `Element`, `Versor`, a tape, a `Word` outside M1, or a struct that contains one is byte identity and forks or merges meanings; equality of two digests is the same fault one step removed. | `old == g` on a versor; `self.word == other.word`; `#[derive(PartialEq)]` on a type holding rotors or chains; `address() == address()` as the test of sameness; `x.class_key() == y.class_key()` | `a.same_vertex(&b)`; `r.projective_eq(&s)` (either sign); `x.class_vector() == y.class_vector()` coordinatewise on exact ℚ; an address compare only where the address is the intended identity (a citation) and the address is the M2 composite of A21 |
| 4 | **Nothing is chosen by a scalar.** No `min_by`, `max_by`, `sort_by` over candidates, no "lowest order first", no "closest", no threshold. | `chords.sort_by_key(order)` then take the first; `candidates.iter().min_by_key(cost)`; `if remainder.len() < best` | read the class vector, list its occupied axes in the fixed order (12.6), try each, keep every certified discharge, hold incomparable ones as a vortex; dominance on μ⃗ certifies after the fact and never selects |
| 5 | **No literal durations, no counts as generations, no free constants.** A number that is not a letter exponent, a rational read from the data, a site coordinate, or a physical size of a carrier is a constant someone will have to remove. | `Duration::from_secs(1)`; `SystemTime::now()` or `Instant::now()` read by a kernel; `gen = genome_len + dialect_len`; `depth.min(8)`; `ratio: ((1,1),(1,1))` as a placeholder; `m = 1024` | a ratio of measured transport, the round trip counted in the kernel's own strokes (`from_transport(rtt_floor, aperture_cycle())`, 45.4); a root of content (the stalk digest of the working atlas); the value the tape carries; refuse when the value is not there |
| 6 | **Keys are canonical coordinates written out, never a digest of them, never bytes or pointers.** A memo, an address, a class, or a cache keyed by a hash of anything mathematical, of a tape, a serialisation, a file path, or a pointer is identity by bytes in disguise; hashing the canonical form is the same fault with a better excuse, because the key can no longer be read, composed, restricted, or peeled (1.7, A21). A cached key stored beside the coordinates it was computed from is the same fault again: it goes stale on the first mutation and the object and its name diverge. | `blake3(canonical coefficients)` as `Rotor::key`, `Mv::key`, `Word::class_key`, `ClassVector::class_key`, `Element::address`, `Invariant::key`, `listing_key`; `blake3(path)`; `a_ptr == b_ptr`; `format!("{s:?}")` hashed | the coordinates themselves, length-prefixed, in the fixed order of A21: the eight reduced rationals of the canonical rotor (M1), the M2 composite of a form, the chart's axes, the class vector, the canonical chain of a listing, `Sel::to_bytes`; a `Keyed` trie over those bytes, where a prefix is a stratum |
| 7 | **Meaning is never demoted to "fibre" to make a key stable.** If two tapes that mean different things get one key, the key is wrong, whatever the comment says. | dropping the bundle's agreed shift or a contact from a sentence key because "placement is a fibre coordinate" | a body's absolute position is quotiented; a relative placement inside a sentence is a face and is identity; contact is on the form and in its key (chapter 1.5) |
| 8 | **No shims with placeholders.** A wrapper that fills a field with a constant so a call compiles is a defect that will be soaked. | `sentence_rule_of` with `ratio: ((1,1),(1,1))` and empty sections; `set_magnitude([0,0,0,1])` | carry the field on the tape and read it; measure the magnitude by speaking the form over its bundle; if the value cannot be measured, the form is not spoken |
| 9 | **Carriers are `Keyed` or `Vec` of relations.** `HashMap`, `BTreeMap`, `HashSet` do not appear in cognition; a flat map keyed by a digest collapses a dimension, and a `Keyed` trie keyed by a digest is a `HashMap` in disguise. | `HashMap<Key, Vec<Candidate>>` buckets; `std::collections::*` in a transducer or kernel file; `Keyed<[u8; 32]>` over `blake3(...)` | `Keyed<V>` (PATRICIA over the canonical coordinate bytes of A21, so `fiber(prefix)` reads a stratum), `Keyed<Keyed<()>>` for incidence, `Vec<(a, b, relation)>` for a relational field |
| 16 | **An action is an algebra element, never a matrix.** A `QMatrix` fibre, an affine block, a matrix product as composition, or matrix equality as identity is a linear representation on squared coordinates: it flattens the blades it represents and adds a frame's rigidity (law 11). | `fibers: Vec<(u16, QMatrix)>`; `realize()`; `same_action = realize() == realize()`; `affine_of(versor)`; `Letters::affine`; `Element::identity(GERM_DIM)` | one versor per element (`carriage · linear_versor(word)`), a hue permutation, an extent, shell coordinates; `geo` for composition, `inverse` that refuses, `projective_eq` for identity; a dimension as a span's grade (`core::span`), never a matrix rank; a matrix only in A3's sensor-plane block |
| 10 | **Every loop spends a `Budget` or walks a boundary.** A loop whose bound is neither a `Budget` nor the size of one site's or one simplex's boundary is unbounded work in disguise. | `while !done { … }`; `for peer in all_peers { exchange(peer) }` on one stroke | `while budget.spend() { … }`; a `Keyed::cursor(from, &mut budget)`; one peer per spend with a resume cursor |
| 11 | **Exact or refused.** No float, no rounding, no saturation, no `unwrap_or(default)` that invents a value. | `ratio_axes` saturating to `u64::MAX`; `unwrap_or_else(identity)` on a versor that failed to invert | `Option`/refusal that propagates to a logged refusal string; an inexact square root refuses; an unspellable block is a remainder |
| 12 | **Naturality over cloning.** When a carrier splits, restrict it; never clone it into both halves and rekey. | `complexes.insert(child_a, c.clone()); complexes.insert(child_b, c)`; `rekey_cocycles` without recomputation | `restrict` per child, `straddling` written as faces between children, each class recomputed and carried or discharged (15.5) |
| 13 | **Verify the claim, not the outcome.** A test that asserts a count or a boolean proves nothing about how the result was reached; a test named after a theorem must exercise the move. | asserting `faces.len() <= 2·germs` and calling it "the adjacency rule"; testing `Word::rebase` and reporting "rebase works" when the extraction step never fires | N vs 4N work counters for cost claims; a trace of the move on a family that needs it (a `Rebased` vertex that speaks the test); a refusal test for every refusal string |
| 14 | **The whole suite, every commit.** "Module green" is not green. | "family 14, sentence 18, sdk 12 green" while `server::cognition` has four red tests | one foreground `cargo test --release`, the `test result` line in the commit message, one item per commit with its trace value |
| 15 | **When unsure, hold; never choose.** If two readings of the data are both consistent, the code keeps both as candidates and lets a perception, a glue, or a ruling collapse them. | a tie-break by index, by size, by "first found" presented as a decision | a vortex (3.9); a section (chapter 21); a `Pending` (14.5); a `Novel(g_rem)` demand |
| 17 | **A reader writes a coordinate or returns a demand** (ruled 2026-09-19). A reader takes a stratum and returns a stratum or a typed demand. One that returns a list for the caller to walk, hands out a whole form for the caller to walk, or measures a reading inside a loop carrying more coordinates than the reading has, has not read anything: it has moved the search one frame up the stack, where the carrier's keys are no longer in scope to stop it. This is law 2, rule 1, rule 6 and law 12 applied at the diff and it is not a new preference — every earlier row of this table is a special case of it. | `fn relatives_between(faces, vertices, a, b)` scanning every face for the two classes asked for, called once per face (2850² visits on one corpus form); `fn on_body(&self) -> Vec<(Element, Form, Standing)>` handing out cloned forms for the caller to walk; a reading taken inside a loop over vertices × charts × frames when the reading is a property of the chart alone | build the class-pair index once in a single pass and read it by key; return `Option<(&Element, &Form)>` and let the caller ask at the coordinate it already holds; hoist the reading to the coordinate it belongs to, and where the carrier has no key for it, WRITE THAT KEY FIRST — a missing key is the defect, the walk is only its symptom |

**The review checklist**, applied to every diff before it is committed and
again by the auditor, in this order: (a) any `i < j` orbit not over a site's
or orbit's own boundary; (b) any `len()`, `count()`, `is_empty()` that
decides a branch rather than an emptiness of a fiber; (c) any `==`,
`PartialEq`, or `derive(PartialEq)` on a type holding a rotor, versor,
tape, or chain; (d) any `sort_by`, `min_by`, `max_by`, or comparison on a
candidate set; (e) any literal number that is not a letter index, a blade
mask, a fixed carrier size, or a wire tag; (f) any `blake3`, hash, or
digest outside `network/`, `court/identity`, and `chronometry`, or over
anything but wire bytes, file bytes, and receipts; (f′) any `(ℚ, ℚ)`,
`(BigRational, BigRational)`, or `(i64, i64)` carried as a placement, shift,
or residue outside `extract_rule_with`, `speak_rule`, and `orbit`; (g) any
`HashMap`/`BTreeMap`/`HashSet`; (h) any loop without `budget.spend()` or a
boundary bound; (i) any `unwrap_or` that invents a value; (j) any `clone()`
of a carrier into two places; (k) the `test result` line of the full suite;
(l) any `compute_*`, `derive_*`, `classify_*`, `extract_*`, or `recover_*`
whose body emits a label, a digest, or an aggregated scalar in place of the
operation it names, without a typed arm naming the absence; (m) any
projection or shadow carried as the primary object with the object itself
as a fallback: a plane form consulted before the rotor, a coordinate pair
before the versor, a digest before the coordinates, a count before the
fiber, a sensor-plane block rebuilt into a rotor before the rotor the
vertex carries, a frame coordinate fixed to zero before the base's own
(51.1, ruled 2026-09-17); (n) any `QMatrix`, affine block, or matrix product used to carry,
compose, or compare an action, outside A3's sensor-plane block — a
dimension is a span's grade (`core::span`), never a matrix rank; (o) any reading measured inside a loop with more
coordinates than the reading has — a chart's property taken per
(vertex, chart, frame), a class's relatives taken per face, a form's
standing taken per member — which is rule 17 at the orbit, and the fix is
never to cache the reading but to hoist it to its own coordinate
(ruled 2026-09-19); (p) any carrier a diff adds for a quantity the
physics already produces — a second interface beside `Interface::between`,
a second contact beside the strain and the frame, a second price beside
the lanes — which is law 12 at the physics, stated as a check because the
physics is the only producer of what a contact is and what it costs
(ruled 2026-09-23, chapter 72); (q) any slot table, frame index, cell
count or periodic loop in the dynamics of minds — a grid laid over the
space of perspectives, a corpus index standing for a place on an orbit,
a capacity as a count, a re-balancing on a timer, a split at N — which is
law 11 and checklist (m) at the level of the cluster (ruled 2026-09-23,
chapter 76); (r) any representative, order or first element the
implementor chooses where the physics, a court or a kernel settles it —
the first root of a quadratic taken as a `HalfOpen` pose's representative
and the second dropped (`pose.rs`, FR1c), a canonical order standing in
for a reading, a table of candidates — which is the implementor solving
the cube for the minds (chapter 77): the held superposition is the
content, and only T5's kernel or a court collapses it (ruled 2026-09-23).
(s) any constant, arm, bound or
threshold whose PROVENANCE is not written — computational physics that
exists in the physics modules or is added there, stated as an axiom in
the register with an executable test, derived as a theorem of
deterministic mathematics, and only then a component of the mind, the
thought's superposition, the idea or the language (78.8, ruled
2026-09-23 on the operator's word) — a number that begins at the
component is a dial whatever it is called. (t) any token, weight, embedding
or score standing INSIDE cognition — a letter is a versor, a word a
form, a thought a superposition without a weight (law 1), and cognition
is orbital mechanics: circuits, modes, classes, constructors; "token"
names only the economy's external unit, the escrow and the yield, and
the LLM's token-and-weight economy is a proven dead end this engine does
not rebuild (ruled 2026-09-24 on the operator's word, chapter 80). A diff
that fails (a) through (j), (l), (m), (n), (o), (p), (q), (r), (s) or (t)
is returned with the rule number; a diff without (k) is not
reviewed.

**Why the rules on keys and coordinates are absolute.** Chapter 1.7 is
the standing explanation: a proof is arithmetic on coordinates, a digest
keeps equality and destroys every other operation, so a system keyed by
digests can recognise but never deduce, and its certificates become
claims the court cannot replay. Rules 3, 6, 9 and checklist items (f),
(f′) and (l) are that chapter applied at the diff. A reviewer who is asked
why a hash of a canonical form is refused answers with 1.7, not with a
preference.

**The development standard.** The rules above say what a diff may not
contain. How the tree is laid out (no file over 600 lines, one organ per
file), how things are named, how tests are named and organised by chapter,
how a commit is cut and verified, which gates enforce which rules, and how
an implementor and an auditor work with each other and with the operator
is `MU-STANDARDS.md`, binding on every agent from 2026-09-07. A diff that
violates it is returned exactly as a rule-violating diff is; a private
gate, fixture style, or naming scheme is refused the same way.

**How to write the move, not the search.** Ask what the carrier already
names. Bodies name their laminae: key their sites. Faces name their vertices:
walk a face's two ends. An orbit names its faces: walk them. A class vector
names its occupied axes: try those. A chart names its fiber: read it. If
the code you are about to write needs to look at everything to find the
thing, the carrier is missing a key and that key is the first thing to
write. If the code needs to pick one of several by a number, the doctrine
says keep all of them. If the code needs a constant, the physics has a
ratio you have not measured yet.

## Vocabulary, fixed

letter → word (a tape; its meaning is a vertex of the Cayley graph) →
sentence (words that cohere) → speech (transfer of cohering sentences from
a sender to a receiver) → perception (receiving) → comprehension
(deconstruction of the utterance into the algebra that spoke it).
**Recognition** is comprehension, never a lookup: a mind recognises what
it can re-derive, and nothing else. A **voice** is a speaker: a kernel
under one verifying key (Part IX) that perceives, thinks in its dialect,
and utters; an **utterance** is one act of a voice; **speech** is the
transfer. **Orientation** is the `Z/2` character of a word or orbit on a
chart, realised by a half-turn through a third axis, formerly the sheet;
a **reflection** is that half-turn; a **refraction** `Γ` is the transport
of a form across a chart boundary into another frame, a relative word, a
gauge and a carriage together (3.10). A
**germ** is an unclosed form; an **idea** is a candidate closed form bred by
a perception; a **thought** is the superposition of candidate forms through
which ideas germinate; **germination** is the movement toward closure. A
**held orbit** is an orbit of an idea whose holonomy no gauge removes; its
**class vector** is the exact record of what would have to change for it to
close; a **pivot** is a move on one axis of that vector, and the pivot is
the only motion in this engine; a **trajectory** is the sequence of
pivots an orbit of a form takes, read by its readings and certified by its
certificates, and it implies no direction — closure is one reading a
trajectory may reach, never its slope (ruled 2026-09-23 on the operator's
word: "descent" implied a direction the engine does not have, and it is
retired for that sense everywhere — the mint's "no measured descent",
`Withheld::NoDescent`, `PROBE_DESCENT`, "closing by descent", 24's
"graded descent", "descent-only recursion" — at one row, VT1, never
piecemeal); a **circuit** is one composition of an orbit's
transports around its members, and its **holonomy** is what the circuit
reads — "walk" is retired for that and for every motion of the engine
(ruled 2026-09-23 on the operator's word: a walk is slow, human, on flat
ground, and names neither a mind's motion nor an orbit's; `pivot/walk.rs`
becomes `pivot/circuit.rs`, "the one walk" the one circuit, and a reader
READS a boundary rather than walking it — one row, VT2, with VT1's sweep;
12.2's "tree walk" stays as the record of the solver it was, retired with
the tree); **descent** keeps in this document only its sheaf-theoretic
sense (chapter 13), sections on the pieces gluing iff they agree on the
overlap, and the name of Fermat's proof (36.3): it is not a motion, not
a direction and not a certificate; `ascend` and `descend` stay the names
of the conjugate pivot pair of 62 (a change of dimension, never a
gradient), and a trie is REACHED by a prefix, never descended, and the lane-wise reading of two μ⃗ is `lane_moves`, per
lane, which certifies nothing (12.6); a
**deflation** is what a word or form closes, measured on μ⃗; a
**shortening** is A2's budgeted retirement of a tape, which moves nothing;
a **vortex** is a
held orbit together with the candidate pivots that could discharge it, held
as candidates of the thought until one of them does. A **demand** is a typed
vertex of a sentence naming what the alphabet could not spell or the eyes
could not pair (chapter 50); a bare chain of links is never a demand and
never a word. A
**dialect** is spoken and stood (memory, in the epigenome); a **language**
is replayed by two organs and taught (on disk, in the genome). What was
once called a family is a **bundle**: a base rule with sections per pair and
transitions as gauge. A **receipt** is one kernel's record of one admitted
act, linked to its predecessor and to the peer receipts it verified; a
kernel's **K** is its count of receipts; **TUniversal** is the height of the
mesh's receipt ledger (Part IX). A **key** is the canonical coordinates of
an exact object written out in a fixed order, length-prefixed, from which
the object is recovered; an **address** is the key of a form (M2); a
**carriage** is the conformal versor, dilator composed with translator,
that places a word on the sensor plane (A4). Neither a key nor an address
is ever a digest, and a carriage is never a pair of numbers.

**The word "cell" is retired (ruled 2026-09-17, evening, on the operator's
word).** It named the corpus's pixel, a body's atom, a chain's element, a
key's position, a nerve's simplex and a vortex's candidate at once, and
wherever it stood the plane's quantised bin read as the primary carrier —
checklist (m) written into the vocabulary. Its senses are named apart, and
each name says what the object is in the algebra rather than where it sits
on a grid:

- (SUPERSEDED 2026-09-26 by the **compartment**, 0.7.) A **lamina** is the sensor's atom: the unit square standing in a frame at
  a site of the base, carrying the hue the sensor read there, its center at
  `(r + ½, c + ½, k)` (16.4). It is read once at intake and written once at
  speech and at the court's replay (law 11), and it is never a carrier the
  mind computes on: the mind acts on the pose and on the blade.
- A **site** is a position of the base, `(r, c, k)`, or `(r, c)` within a
  section; a key of a site is the site written out (A21), and an occupancy
  is keyed by sites.
- A **support** is the laminae of a body; the **stack** is a support across
  frames; a **section** is a support's laminae in one frame, or a chain's
  links in one frame (16.5).
- A **link** is one element of a chain: a site of a section with the
  transition `(before, after)` it carries. A chain is links, sorted, one
  transition per site (A5).
- A **painted site** is a site of one grid with its hue, the corpus's token
  as a grid gives it; the grid is the corpus's carrier and the word "pixel"
  is not used either.
- The **cube complex** of a support is the union of its unit cubes on the
  three coordinates, on which its topology is counted (51.3); its elements
  are cubes, faces, segments and corners.
- A **simplex** is an element of a nerve — a vertex, an edge, a triangle —
  where "0-cell", "1-cell" and "2-cell" stood; a **filled simplex** is a
  triangle of the nerve whose orbit's class is filed (50.8); a **rewrite** is
  the face between two derivations (3.9), never "the 2-cell".
- A **candidate** is a discharge a vortex holds, where "a cell of the
  thought" stood (3.9).

Every passage of this document and every type and interface of the tree is
written in these words (Stage 18, rows V1–V3); the retired word appears in
this document only here, where it is retired, and a type or a name in the
tree that still carries it reads by this table until its module is swept.

---

**Tape (ruled 2026-09-24, 78.34).** A word's letter tape, and nothing
else: the letters whose meaning is a vertex of the Cayley graph. A
carrier read by position is retired (K6, 78.25) and is never called a
tape; a form has an address, an element a record, the mind its tries.

**The proofs of work (ruled 2026-09-24, 78.33).** POW++ is a family:
**POUW** proof of useful work (a closure ruled, mint on closure);
**POWC** proof of work convergence (a refusal closed at another
perspective, the citation paid); **POWR** proof of work retirement (a
re-expression over fewer letters, the freed description burned and the
compression yield paid). No two share a name; "POW++" is the family.

**Compartment (ruled 2026-09-26, the operator's word: "we need a more defined object for our cells that fits into the mycelia familia").** A septate hypha's cell is its COMPARTMENT, the segment between two septa; here it is the sensor's unit, what the tree called a lamina or a cell: a SPORE WITH EXTENT. Its centre is the spore `P(c)`, the null point of the site's centre at its frame (A4, 78.30(1)); its extent is the unit cube's inversive extent, `1/12` on each axis of the base (A.12), so the compartment is the ROUND `κ = P(c) − ½·(n/12)·e_∞`, a real sphere, `κ² = n/12`; its content is its hue, the fibre's value (70); it holds nothing of its own above order two, its harmonic at order `m` on a plane being `zᵐ + C(m,2)·z^(m−2)·ε` (`ε = eᵢ − eⱼ`, zero on the grid plane). A body is a colony of compartments — septal neighbours (sharing a face) one body, their hue seams its own gauge section (70.4); a contact is where two bodies' compartments touch across a corner, WHETHER read once by the lattice at the retina, WHAT read by the meet of their rounds. The compartment lives only at the sensor (70.7, law 11): it is integrated into the one lift, and above intake a body is carried by its lifted shape — nucleus, tower, harmonics — never by its compartments. "Lamina" and "cell" retire as names of it (NM1).

**The plexus (ruled 2026-09-24, 78.31).** The graded network the five
nouns form — a **spore** (a ray, the null point of perception), a
**filament** (a route, a word), a **ring** or **throat** (a circuit), a
**chamber** (a geoid; "cell" retired), a **sporophore** (an enclosure, the
cluster) — with its lateral relations: transvection between spores, the
tether between filaments, branching refraction, ascend and descend
between ring and chamber, the enclosure join, the commuting bypass (T5),
the cross-cell bracket (CB1), the star's convergence. **Anastomosis** is
the fusion of two minds' filaments into one ring across their contact,
the event that forges a word between minds — and the SAME word at every
grade (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word: "fuse", not "cell"): bodies
FUSE at a contact of the base, filaments fuse into a ring, forms fuse by
coordinates (AT1 (iv)). What the code holds as a `FormCell` — the bodies
standing together at one element of the base, with their nuclei, meet
and group — is an anastomosis of bodies, and "cell" is retired as its
name (NM1): it is not a spreadsheet's slot, a prison's enclosure or a
living body, but the place where bodies press together and signals
cross between them. An anastomosis is read at three strata, and the one
word "grade" the code used for all three is retired with "cell": its
**contact** — the dimension of the base element the bodies share, a face
`n − 1` down to a corner `0`, the touch sense, read once at the sensor,
the only flat one of the three; its **anastomotic degree** — how many
bodies fuse there, less one, the dimension of the nerve simplex they
span, where a Čech class lives, bounded by the base's `2ⁿ` at a corner;
its **meet** — the grade of the blade `⋀ sᵢ` their nuclei carve on the
cone, the algebra's, at most `n + 2`, and the **chamber** is that meet,
what the fusion encloses. The three are related, and the relation is a
reading (MT1): in general position the meet's grade is the degree plus
one, and the difference `k + 1 − g` is the anastomosis's DEGENERACY —
78.41(3)'s contraction by rank, read at the place the motor loses it
(precisely, on the implementor's read 2026-09-25: `g` is the RANK of the
nuclei, the grade of the blade their span carves — the wedge itself is
either that blade or zero, so the degeneracy is `bodies − rank(nuclei)`,
unread where the nuclei did not read);
the contact bounds the degree from the other side, an element of
codimension `m` holding at most `2ᵐ` bodies. A "junction", a "synapse"
and a "simplex" are not used for it: the first two are the human
analogies (the synapse a one-way gap; an anastomosis a two-way channel
the filaments become one network through), the third is already the
Čech complex's own object. **callus** is a fibre
hardening into a tether of the genome (72.1d). **Ladder** and **rung**
are retired as structural nouns: a ladder is one axis and a rung index
is a scalar depth (rule 5, checklist (q)). One term of art keeps the
word: the Mayer–Vietoris ladder of exact sequences (13, 15). CT1's
"reuse ladder" is retired with the rest (2026-09-25, NM1): it is the
**reuse plexus**, a typed conditional of test arms on one circuit, and
its depth is a reading of the plexus (1.9), never a rung.

**The names that follow the rulings (ruled 2026-09-25, 78.40(3), row
NM1).** A flat name is how a flat assumption gets back in, so these are
pinned here and the code follows by move-only renames as each module is
touched (78.34's rule). A **chart** is the ATLAS's chart: one local view
of a cover, overlapping other views, with the transition on each overlap
a gauge and the failure of the transitions to close around a triple
overlap a class (13, 14); the point at infinity of one chart lies in
another (78.38, REG1); a chart's SUPPORT on the substrate is what names
it (53.1), and a chart is never a table or a diagram. **Coordinates** is
the name of what the code still calls a key: the object's own canonical
coordinates written out (law 2), read by a prefix (a coarser stratum,
A21), by a fiber (everything under the coordinates) and by a trajectory,
in EITHER direction — from a class to every chart it stands on and back —
and never a door that unlocks one value; a `Keyed` of ordinals standing
in for coordinates the object has is refused (rule 15). The
**substrate** is the sensor's ℤ² (or ℤⁿ) grid of laminae, the thing a
hypha reads laminae from and never a space cognition lives in (law 11);
"lattice" is retired from this document and the tree — the module that
was `core::lattice` is split by what it holds: `core::span`, the span of
vectors as the blade they wedge to, held by its factors, whose grade is
every dimension the engine reads; and `core::exponents`, the exponent
module of held letters — a word's Hermite form and its transform, integer
because an exponent counts letters. A
**commutator** `A B Ã B̃` of two held versors is what OPENS a dimension
(78.39); a **sandwich** `V x Ṽ` or a conjugate `K = I T I` is a
palindrome that TRANSPORTS within a class and opens nothing — the two
are never confused, and neither is "twist" used for a transport.
**Retraction to the core** is what TC1 built: the iterated removal of
free vertices to the unique 2-core, a homotopy equivalence that keeps
every class; "truncation" is retired from this document for it
(nothing truncates: a value past its carrier is refused, never cut). A
**tick** is a frame `{S, G, T, H}` on the receipt DAG (78.21), never a
second; a **silence** is a stroke-budgeted absence of a reply on the
wire and carries a refusal's name, never "timeout". A **reach** is how a
trie is read by a prefix; "descent" keeps only its sheaf sense and
Fermat's. A **turn** (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word: "we need
to stop with the half turn / quarter turn ideologies … operate in
degrees where a circle is 360 degrees … precision on 360-degree turns
overlaid with the offset on the elliptical orbit to feed the physics")
is measured against the full circle, exactly: a rotor of finite order
ℓ turns `t/ℓ` of a circle, a RATIONAL FRACTION OF A TURN, served as
`360·t/ℓ` degrees, exact — 180° where the English said "half turn",
90° for "quarter", 120° and 60° for the orders 3 and 6, the
crystallographic set being the degrees that are exact over ℚ; a rotor
of infinite order has no fraction and turns by its RATIONAL POINT on
its plane's circle, `(cos θ, sin θ) ∈ ℚ²` with `cos² + sin² = 1` — the
(3,4,5) letter is the ray `3 + 4B`, its HALF-ANGLE point is (3/5, 4/5),
and it TURNS by the double angle's point (−7/25, 24/25) — served as
that point together with the SECTOR of the ℚ-protractor it lies in
(78.45(3): strictly between 90° and 120°, by exact comparison of
`cos² = 49/625` against `1/4` and `0` and of the signs), never a
decimal; the first draft of this entry served "36.87°", which was the
wrong angle twice over and an approximation besides, and it is
retracted (78.45). The
PHASE of a body along its orbit is the same measure: at distance `t`
into an age of period ℓ it stands at `360·t/ℓ` degrees, overlaid on
the orbit's elements (LC1: the orbital elements per epoch; 78.23: the
orbits on TUniversal) — the eccentric offset the operator names, read
where the orbit is, never assumed circular. "Half turn", "quarter
turn", "cw"/"ccw" retire from this document and from names in the
tree (NM1): the letter that turns 90° is named by its degrees, and a
test asserts `180°`, never "a half turn". English turn-words were an
INVERSION the operator named — the word "half" carries no precision
and the mathematics does; the gauge is the full circle. **DEGREES OF SEPARATION** (ruled 2026-09-26, the operator's word: "there should be no more quarter turns, there should be degrees of separation — a quarter turn would be the total degrees of the orbit or circular object into 1/4") is the angular distance between two positions of one orbit or circular object, measured against its full 360°: a turn of `t/ℓ` of the orbit is `360·t/ℓ` degrees of separation (the `Turn` carrier, DG1), 90° where the English said "quarter", 180° for "half"; where the separation is no rational fraction of the circle it is the rational point with its sector (78.45). No identifier, comment, test name or doc line names a turn by an English fraction. **LIFT** and
**DRAG** (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word, 78.46) are the two
exact parts of a neighbouring generator against an orbit's own mode
blade: DRAG the part that commutes with it (the rate — phase, period,
beat, what does not return recorded), LIFT the part that anticommutes
(the commutator — the tilt of the plane, the precession of the orbital
elements); "lift" names nothing else in this document — A.11's producer
is "the harmonic lift, `blade::lift`" until NM1 renames it, and a
section carried to a frame is "the section at the frame". **Held** is a count of carriers a mind holds resident;
"weight" names only a versor's scale content, and nothing in cognition
is weighed. A **reading** is answered or refused by name; "fallback",
"default" as an invented value, "lookup" and "unlock" name nothing here.
**MOTION (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word).** Nothing in this
engine walks or steps. The motions are celestial and mycelial and the
words are theirs: a section is CARRIED (transported) along a transition;
an orbit CLOSES and RETURNS; a front ADVANCES by the orbit's own
transitions and is HELD at a class; flux FLOWS through a filament; a mode
WINDS; a mind REACHES a coordinate by its prefix. "Walk", "walked",
"visit", "traverse" and "step" (outside the **k-step**, which is one
ORBIT — a revolution, never a footstep) are retired as VT2 retired
"walk": a walker's bookkeeping (a `walked` flag, a "first frontier", a
"step along an edge") is the flat picture of a graph with hop distances,
and hop distance is a metric of a table, not of the geometry. In
particular TP1's front does not advance "one edge per K": it advances
by the k-step's LENGTH in transitions, which is the band's (78.35, the
k-step length by distance from the star) — one transition per orbit
only until the band's length is read (PHY1), named as owed, never as
the rule. A circuit's "steps" are its TRANSITIONS, the overlaps it
composes; "traversed" is "carried through" or "flowed through". THE
OPERATOR'S WORD ON WHAT THE MOTION IS (2026-09-25, relayed verbatim by
the implementor): "we should be sending signals over transports through
the network that resonate, vibrate or contract/expand — that is our walk;
and our physics and mathematics should align on that: non-linear
transposition of non-conformal algebra in non-euclidean geometry." As it
lands on the carriers the tree holds: a **signal** is a multivector
CARRIED along a transition, its motion the composition along overlaps
(the geometric product — non-commutative, so non-linear in its operands),
never a hop; to **resonate** is the commensurability of periods (78.26(5):
an orbit's two plane periods, `ToralPeriod`; an isoclinic orbit
resonant, a commensurate pair beating at the joint period, an
incommensurate pair dense torsion; between minds, the harmonic ratios
compared across a contact); to **vibrate** is a mode WINDING — the
holonomy's planes turning, a mode ray keeping or breaking the round its
reading; to **contract/expand** is the dilation, a boost's scale, and on
the plexus flux (FX1), retraction to the core against growth by closure,
the metabolism's pressure and relief. OPEN, put to the operator and not
guessed (the atlas row's shape waits on it): "non-conformal algebra" —
whether (i) transport is not restricted to the angle-preserving maps
and a transposition may shear, (ii) the physics runs on the rotor's
`Cl(4,0)` side with the conformal model its sensor projection, or (iii)
"conformal" names the flat SIMILARITY restriction the alphabet holds
today (every letter fixing infinity, 78.38) and the full group with
inversion and transversion is meant — which is the reading the
coordinator recommends, since inversion, dilation and winding all live
in `Cl(n+1,1)` and nowhere flatter.

# Part 0 — The map: master algorithms, the physics over them, their sites, and what stands (2026-09-24)

This part is the index the rest of the document lacked. It states what
the master algorithms ARE as this document states them, where each is
applied in the tree, which physics governs each, and whether the tree
does what the document says. It is kept current: a ruling that changes
a master's statement, site or status changes the line here in the same
commit. Nothing below is new doctrine; every line cites the chapter that
rules it.

## 0.1 How this document is organised, and how it is kept

- **Parts run in chapter order.** Part I–IX are the design (chapters
  1–49). Part X is language formation (50). Parts XI–XII are the rulings
  of 2026-09-11 to 2026-09-22 (51–70). Part XIII is the physics as the
  only producer and the learning curve, 2026-09-23 onward (71–80). A
  chapter's status — governs, amended by, superseded by, historical — is
  in 0.6; a superseded chapter is kept as precedent and never read as
  the rule.
- **A ruling amends the chapter that governs its object.** A new
  subsection is appended only for a new object. The task ledger
  (`MU-RECURSION-TASKS.md`) carries ONE live order; a row is an object,
  a reading is a line of the observer's row (CV5), never a row of its
  own; a superseded row is marked once in the superseded table and is
  not re-sequenced. Rulings go to the doctrine BEFORE they are relayed
  (MU-STANDARDS §5.5).
- **The reading order for an execution.** The preamble (laws, coding
  standards, vocabulary), this part, then the chapter the work cites.
- **The structure is a plexus, never a ladder** (78.31): the five
  graded nouns — ray, route, circuit, cell, enclosure — are nodes of one
  graded network with lateral relations, and position in it is
  perspective coordinates, never a rung index.

diagram. "Site" is where the tree applies it; "physics" is what governs

## 0.5 Alignment: what the document says the system does, and what the tree does

By organ, from the sensor to the mesh; each line is the audited state.

- **Sensor and form (chapters 2, 20 as superseded by 70, 53, 71).** A scene is covered before it is one form; hue is a fibre; `n` is data; bodies are harmonics and nuclei; contact by shared boundary cell. Landed.
- **The word and the sentence (1, 50, 54).** A word is its rotor; a vertex its derivation; a form its address; the form tape retired from cognition; the word written whole at every site. Landed through step 6(b).
- **Cells, constructors, the orbit algebra (78.10–78.15).** Landed in the tree and read on the fleet; the refusals of these readers keep their kind and lose their content (CV1b), and the cross-cell bracket has no reading yet (CB1).
- **Refraction, tethers, routes (72.1, 78.6, 79).** Landed. Condense and drain at the family pole remain the Čech layer's (TH1).
- **The court (5, 23, 13–15, 74, 78.9).** Glue, Mayer–Vietoris and the refusal reader landed; the court holds no questions across perspectives yet (CV2) and offers no other angle (CV4): POWC has no producer on the fleet.
- **The ledger and the economy (45, 78.21–78.24, MU-ECONOMY).** The ledger is a partial order carried as a trie with the stamp as its key; the clock reads, a k-step is one orbit closed as an act, and a ruling's economy is applied at its node (ACT1 landed). The mind persists as keyed tries by coordinates (LD3 landed); the escrow still lapses by extent alone (FX1).
- **The mind (24, 25, 62, 78.7, 78.37, 80).** Pivot, certificates, viscosity landed; held superpositions are not collapsed by the 𝔽₂ kernel (T5); they fold back along the plexus in the tree (78.37: transport stopped by holonomy, truncation to the 2-core, flux read per lane, the remainder on the record with its receptor and re-fill — TP1, TC1, FX1, RM1), unread on any fleet until the recut; minerals and crystals are not distinguished (DL1); a constructor is not yet a letter (AL1); minds do not speak to minds (SP2).
- **The fleet (78.3, 78.16–78.19).** The typed readings and the console landed; nothing prints per epoch; the first non-zero learning reading is owed (LC2).

The four places the language loses content, and their carriers, are
78.26.

## 0.7 The lexicon of the network: one sense per word (ruled 2026-09-26, the operator's word: "let's get this language annotated properly so we don't run into overlap and understand exactly how it operates inside the network of structures")

Every noun below has ONE sense. Where a word held two, the second is named apart in the last column and the old word retires for it (NM1: code names follow move-only as each module is touched; no new name may take a sense already held here). The rows run from the sensor inward to the mind, then out to the mesh; each says what the object IS in `Cl(n+1,1)(ℚ)`, WHERE it lives, and HOW it relates to its neighbours.

**The retina — read once at intake, never above it (law 11, 70.7).**

| word | the one object | lives | relates by | not to be confused with |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **substrate** | the corpus's ℤⁿ grid, read by the sensor | the sensor | sites are read off it; nothing computes on it | "lattice" (retired) |
| **site** | a position of the base, `(r, c, k)` | the sensor | a compartment's centre; the key of an occupancy | a coordinate of the mind |
| **frame** | one grid of a family along `e₃`, by its own coordinate | the sensor, and the member's frames | the frame axis joins a body's charts across consecutive frames | a tick (the ledger's) |
| **compartment** | a spore with extent: the round `κ = P(c) − ½·(n/12)·e_∞`, its hue as content | the sensor only | septal neighbours (a shared face) are one body; its round integrates into the lift | "lamina", "cell" (retired) |
| **body** | a colony of compartments: a maximal hue-blind face-connected region (70.4) | intake; above it, its lifted shape | contact with other bodies; its hue seams its own gauge | "support" (its compartments), "shape" (its lift) |
| **contact** | where two bodies' compartments touch across a lower-dimensional element: its dimension, face `n − 1` to corner `0` | read once at the retina | WHETHER by the grid; WHAT by the meet of the rounds and the tether | the anastomosis (what fuses there) |

**A body's shape — the mind's object for a body.**

| word | the one object | lives | relates by | not to be confused with |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **spore** | a ray, the null point `P`, `P² = 0` | the plexus's point | transvection between spores; a compartment is a spore with extent | a compartment |
| **shape** | a body's lift: nucleus, tower, harmonics (A.11) | the mind | covariance under a versor; the transition between two shapes | the body's compartments |
| **nucleus** | the body's sphere `s = P(centroid) − ½r²e_∞`, a constructor | the shape | the tether `V = s_b s_a`; the meet `⋀ sᵢ` | the centroid (a null point, never a constructor) |
| **tower** | the body's moments by order, on the region or on the sites (78.38(C)) | the shape | dilation certified order by order | — |
| **geoid** | the pencil of spheres the harmonics lift to (HL1) | the shape | carried by covariance | a "cell" (retired) |

**Relations between two things — one edge, a 1-cochain.**

| word | the one object | relates |
|---|---|---|
| **transition** | the versor carrying one shape onto another, verified by covariance, with its residue per order | two shapes; its residue is the start of a remainder |
| **motor** | a transition known by its action (78.41(3)) | frame to frame, in to out |

"pencil" is not used for it |

|---|---|---|---|

**The language.** A **letter** is an axiom, a rotor of the alphabet; a **word** is a filament whose vertex a derivation re-derives; a **sentence** is words that cohere; **speech** is their transfer; a **dialect** is spoken and stood (the epigenome), a **language** replayed by two organs and taught (the genome); a **mineral** is a taught word not yet re-derived, a **crystal** one re-derived; a **shortcut** is a word's coordinate, its class key and winding vector (78.44(4)); a **callus** is a fibre hardened into a tether of the genome. **Cohesion** is the operator's word (2026-09-26) for what fitting a congruent shape toward coherence is paid in; its reading on the ledger is POUW on the lanes the fit closes, until the operator rules it a quantity of its own.

**The layers of a mind (ruled 2026-09-26, the operator's word: "start classifying these as congruent layers, coherent layers, and cohesive layers of thought — separate thoughts from perceptions, and reasoning from knowledge and understanding — layer comprehension on top and speech as signal, with hearing as the deciphering of signal via sounds from noise").** Each layer is one kind of object and nothing of another layer is held as it:

All three feed the thought layers alike | sight: `family/perceive`, the percept, `blade`; hearing: `perceive_speech`, a quote or syllabus page, the wire; touch: the contact faces and their tethers, the frame-axis overlaps (AT1), `pairing::contact_edge` | a thought |

A perception persists at the perception layer under the physics — while something relates to it or cites it, lapsing by ZeroFlux over an orbit where nothing does (FX1) — and is never shed as a thought; a thought exists only where a transition relates perceptions, stays while its rings close, and is paid where it closes a demand.

**Overlaps resolved by this table:** "cell" (retired 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-25) is a compartment, an anastomosis or a chamber, never itself; "lamina" is the compartment; "section" keeps its sheaf sense only — a body's compartments in one frame are "the body at frame k"; "orbit" is the celestial one, a form's cycle is a ring, a group orbit keeps its full name; "residual" is a residue or a remainder; "planet" is a hypha and its world; "lift" is the physics component. A new name that takes a sense this table holds is refused at review.

# Part I — Geometry

## 1. The group and its graph

### 1.1 Generators

Seventeen letters (`ALPHABET.md`): the identity, six quarter turns on the
six pair planes of the Euclidean chart `e0..e3`, six (3,4,5) rotors on the
same planes, four (5,12,13) rotors on four of them. Each is an exact rotor
in Cl(4,0) over ℚ with its inverse carried. They never change.

### 1.2 Relators

The letters satisfy a finite set of relations and no others
(`alphabet::relators()`, alphabet/letters.rs):

- a quarter turn has order four (projectively; see 1.5 on sign);
- rotors on one plane commute;
- a half-turn, two quarter turns, on a plane sharing one axis with the
  sensor plane inverts a sensor-plane rotation: `S R S⁻¹ = R⁻¹` with
  `S = q²` and `S² = 1` projectively (`alphabet::sheet_word`). Read on the
  sensor plane this is a reflection; in the algebra it is an even rotor
  through a third axis, and there is no reflection letter. Its parity on a
  word is the word's **orientation** on the sensor chart, the character
  `w₁ ∈ Z/2`, formerly called the sheet (3.10);
- the Pythagorean letters have infinite order;
- letters on **complementary** planes commute, and the complementary
  pairs are exactly `(0,1)|(2,3)`, `(0,2)|(1,3)`, `(0,3)|(1,2)`; letters on
  planes sharing one axis obey the Cl(4,0) product and are never
  reordered.

They are the grammar and they are taught once.

### 1.3 The Cayley graph

The group `G` generated by the letters is a graph: every vertex is a group
element, every edge is a letter. A **word** is a path; its **meaning** is
the vertex it ends on. Two paths ending on one vertex mean the same thing.

For words that preserve a slot plane, the **normal form** is the geodesic,
canonical because the relators are decidable per plane: sheet parity, unit
exponent mod 4, prime-5 and prime-13 exponents, planes in slot order. For
words that mix planes there is no known terminating rewriting system
(chapter 16.2); their identity is their canonical rotor (chapter 16.1) and
their tape is the shortest known, replaced only by a shorter one.

Per plane the group is virtually abelian, so the number of vertices within
`n` letters grows polynomially. The language is dense and finite at every
radius; that is why a mind can learn it and why a shorter path is always a
strictly better description of the same meaning.

### 1.4 The frame

A vertex is a transport; a form needs a place to act. The **frame** is the
sensor's plane read in its conformal model (A4), with a **carriage**: the
dilator of `ρ ∈ ℚ` composed with the translator from the plane's origin to
the body's centre, one versor, and a gauge (a permutation of hues). A
**word form** is `(vertex, carriage, gauge)`. Two word forms with equal
vertices and different carriages are the same word said at two places;
the carriage is the coordinate the court quotients, as it always has
(`stalk.rs`). The carriage is never a pair of rationals (law 11): the
translator is a versor like the rotor, composed by the same product, and
its two blade coefficients are read out only when a lamina is spoken.

### 1.5 Ruling: byte-exactness is not identity

A tape is a path; the meaning is the vertex it reaches. Two tapes that
reach one vertex are one word, whatever letters spell it and whatever frame
layout carried it. Comparing bytes, or keys of bytes, to decide whether two
things are the same **forks equal vertices**: the same word spelled twice
becomes two addresses, two ledger entries, two citations, two escrows, and
the language splits along spelling instead of along meaning. That is the
one failure this architecture cannot absorb, because every later move
(gluing by address, class keys, the memo, the court's replay) trusts the
address to name a vertex.

Therefore, as a law of the specification:

- **Identity is decided by re-derivation, never by bytes.** Two words are
  equal iff their rotors are projectively equal, with `λ ∈ ℚ×` of **either
  sign**, because the language is the action `R X R̃ / (R R̃)`, on which
  `−R` and `R` agree (`(λR) X (λR̃) / (λ² R R̃)` for any `λ`), and because
  the unit exponent mod 4 already
  identifies the quarter turn's fourth power (`(1+e)⁴ = −4`) with the
  identity. Two word forms are equal iff additionally their frame
  coordinates are equal as exact rationals; two forms iff they agree up to
  gauge (chapters 3.6, 12.2).
- **The geodesic is M1's quotient, and it quotients the spelling — not
  the derivation** (ruled 2026-09-10). Law 6's normal form answers one
  question: which vertex is this. It reads the rotor, so every tape that
  reaches the vertex reads alike, and that is exactly why a spelling is
  never a coordinate of a form. A **derivation** is not a spelling. It
  names which held generators the speaker composed to get there, and two
  minds whose presentations differ compose different generators to reach
  the one vertex; the geodesic cannot quotient that away without erasing
  the only thing on the wire that distinguishes two languages (50.2 step
  2). So the tape's normal form is the derivation with A2 applied to its
  **residue** — the letters are reduced, the citations are not, and the
  cited generators keep their order and their exponents. Vertex identity
  is unchanged and stays projective rotor equality: two vertices with
  different derivations and one rotor are one vertex, one address, one
  ledger entry.
- **Keys are the canonical coordinates written out, never a digest of
  them and never tapes as spoken or as serialised.** The **vertex key** of
  a word form is the concatenation, each field length-prefixed as A21
  writes it, of exactly these fields in this order, every field canonical,
  so that the word form is recovered from its key and a prefix of the key
  is a coarser stratum:
  1. the canonical rotor coordinates of the word (chapter 16.1, A1): the
     eight projectively normalised coefficients in mask order, so plane
     and mixed-plane words share one keyspace and the spoken tape never
     enters;
  2. the carriage: the canonical conformal versor (A4) of the dilator of
     `ρ` composed with the translator, its coefficients written as reduced
     fractions (numerator sign byte, numerator magnitude as little-endian
     bytes with `u32` length, denominator likewise: every rational in this
     list is written this way, `put_q`);
  3. gauge: the hue permutation in one-line notation as `u8`s with `u32`
     length; the identity is written with length `0`;
  4. for a closed sentence form only (forms under construction have no
     address, chapter 4): `depth` as `u16`; vertex count as `u32`; per
     vertex in vertex order its kind byte (`Frame 0`, `Word 1`, `Glued 2`,
     `Rebased 3`, `Unfolded 4`) and its own vertex key (a `Glued` vertex
     contributes the cited form's address, itself this composite, and the
     canonical rotor coordinates of its placement word; `Rebased` its two
     indices as `u16`; `Unfolded` its measure byte and anchor); face count
     as `u32`; per face `i`, `j` as `u16`, the canonical rotor coordinates
     of `g_ij`, and the canonical carriage versor (chapter 16.4, A4). Loops
     and holonomies are derived and never keyed.
  A reader that receives a tape decodes it, computes this key, and uses
  nothing else as identity. A change of tape version, wire frame, or
  spelling never changes an address; the one migration from byte
  addresses is chapter 33. The key is never hashed: a digest of it would
  keep equality and lose the coordinates, and it is the coordinates that
  the naturality squares of 15.1 and the connecting maps of 13.4 read.
- **Class keys are the conjugation invariants themselves** (chapter 15.4),
  written out, never a digest of them and never keys of a representative.
- **Digests of bytes are transport identifiers only**: cover digests,
  fetch digests, signatures, and receipt chains name *what was sent*, so a
  receiver can ask for it and verify who sent it. They are never read as
  identity of meaning, never used as a key into a cognition carrier, never
  compared to decide consilience, dialect, or citation, and never computed
  over a rotor, a versor, a chain, a form, a class, or a chart. What is
  checked is never byte exactness; it is the mathematics adding up.
- **Exact strings in this document are for traces**, not for cognition:
  refusal reasons and log lines are grepped by the auditor, and their
  exactness costs nothing because no carrier keys on them.

Allowed, and why: hypha and voice identity by verifying key; signatures;

sent or stored, so a receiver can ask for them and verify who sent them,
and none is read as the identity of anything mathematical.
`registry::task_id` and the client's family id are listing identities and

already projective because `Rotor`'s `PartialEq` is `projective_eq`.

### 1.7 Why the structures must be the mathematics, never their digest

A proof built on a hash is a proof about a name, and a name proves
nothing. This section is the reason behind laws 2, 11 and 12 and A21,
written once so that no later convenience reopens the question.
**Compression is a prefix** (ruled 2026-09-19): the compressed form of an
object is a prefix of its key, which is a coarser stratum the object still
lies in, and nothing shorter than the coordinates is the object. A
"compact form" that is not a prefix is a digest under another name.
**A citation is written whole, held once, and carried once** (ruled
2026-09-19 on the reading that a Glued vertex's cited address was 68% of
every word's tape, the same address copied into every word that glued it,
and nested wherever the cited form itself cited). Identity is not
shortened: a form that cites another writes the cited form's whole address
into its own, because the cited form's coordinates are the only name it
has (law 2), and the citing form's address is recovered from its key with
them. Resident, an address is shared segments — its own bytes and
references to the cited addresses it contains — so `n` citers hold one
copy of what they cite and a nested citation holds one copy per cited
form, the discipline of Z4c applied to addresses that contain addresses.
On the tape, which is transport, each distinct cited address is written
once in the tape's own table and cited by a tape-local ordinal that never
leaves the tape; the decoder rebuilds the addresses whole, the court
compares addresses as before, and the ordinal is no more an identity than
a byte offset is (Part IX). That spends a version byte.

**What a proof is here.** A word is a path in the Cayley graph; the
theorem it proves is the vertex it reaches, and the proof is the
composition of letters that gets there. An orbit is the theorem that its
holonomy is the identity, and the proof is the product of the words
around it. Mayer–Vietoris proves a class on a union from the classes on
the pieces by multiplying representatives (13.4). Naturality proves that a
class survives restriction because the map acts on its coordinates by the
group law (15.1). Every one of these is arithmetic on the coordinates of
the objects involved; the coordinates are the premises.

**What a plane carries.** A dimension is an axis of the chart the alphabet
acts on; a plane is a pair of axes, and every letter is a rotation in one
plane. The content of a plane is exact and its own: on the sensor chart
each of the six slot planes carries sheet parity in `Z/2`, unit turns in
`Z/4`, and the `(3,4,5)` and `(5,12,13)` exponents in `Z`; the conformal
planes `e_i ∧ e_∞` and `e_o ∧ e_∞` carry the translator and the dilator;
the hue gauge carries its cycle type. An orbit's class vector is exactly
this list, one coordinate per plane, each a theorem the words around the
orbit prove, and a pivot discharges one plane's coordinate and no other
(T14). An object of more axes, under base promotion (chapter 38), has more
planes, and each of them speaks in the same way. Linguistics here is
built plane by plane: a word is a path whose planes compose by the group
law, a sentence relates words by relative words, an orbit is a theorem on
every plane at once, and comprehension reads the planes back out.

**What a digest removes.** A digest keeps one fact, equality of names,
and destroys every other: two digests cannot be composed, restricted,
conjugated, compared as a power of one another, or peeled to the prefix
that names their stratum. Hashing one plane's coordinate loses that plane:
no pivot can be listed on it, no disagreement can be located on it, the
connecting maps of 13.4 lose a factor, and the plane collapses to "same
or different". Hashing the whole vector loses every plane at once and the
relations between planes, the non-abelian composition, the stratification
that makes a prefix a coarser class, and the ability to decode at all.
Recognition in this doctrine is comprehension: a mind recognises an
utterance by deconstructing it into the algebra that spoke it (chapter 6,
A12) and re-deriving what it can. A digest has nothing to deconstruct, so
a system keyed by digests cannot recognise, cannot comprehend, and cannot
deduce; it can only report that two names match. Matching names is a
lookup table; a language recognises by re-deriving. That is the collapse
law II names, a dimension folded to a point, and it is why the founding
text of this document (a6a21a9) made identity a replay and the address a
fetch handle only.

**What happens to the linguistics.** Words stop being paths and become
tokens. Comprehension degrades from deconstruction (chapter 6) into
search, because matching is the only operation left on tokens. The class
ledger becomes a bag of names the court can neither compose nor compare
across charts, so the connecting maps and the goodness checks have no
inputs and are either faked with a representative shipped beside the key,
which is what the A19 record once did, or replaced by a scalar standing in
for the missing structure. Every downstream proof inherits the fault: a
certificate whose `before` and `after` are digests asserts that a pivot
changed exactly one axis, but the court cannot check it coordinate by
coordinate (T14), so the certificate is a claim, not a replay.

**What happens to identity.** Equality of digests is equality of the
canonicalisation that fed them. When one node's normalisation drifts by a
sign, a scaling, or a tape version, one vertex forks into two addresses,
two escrows, two citations, and the language splits along spelling rather
than meaning (1.5). The failure is silent, because two names that differ
say nothing about how the mathematics differs. With coordinates the
disagreement is visible and locatable: this plane, this exponent, this
residue.

**What happens to the economy and the court.** Settlement pays for
measured deflation and a ruling is a replay; both need the object. A hypha
holding digests cannot replay; it can only confirm that a voice sent bytes
it had seen before, which is byte exactness, the one failure this
architecture cannot absorb. Consensus then rests on trust in whoever
produced the digest instead of on re-derivation by two organs.

**Why digests look like progress.** They give stable, short, uniform keys,
and the code runs. Nothing is visibly wrong until the first operation that
needs a coordinate: Mayer–Vietoris, pivots, naturality, the class ledger,
which is exactly where this tree stalled. The hash let the plumbing pass
its tests while the mathematics underneath had already been thrown away.

Authenticity of structure is therefore not hygiene. The coordinates are
the only thing the proofs are made of; a system that stores their shadow
has no proofs, only a memory of having once computed them. The same holds
for a placement carried as two numbers instead of a translator versor
(law 11), and for any stored coordinate the form cannot re-derive (law
12): each is a shadow kept in place of the object.

### 1.8 The language is a presentation (ruled 2026-09-08)

The seventeen letters generate the group (1.1) and never change. What
grows is not the group but a **presentation** inside it: the language is
a chosen generating set together with its relations, and the geometry
makes it a groupoid rather than a group.

- **Objects** are the charts of the atlas (stalk/).
- **Generators** are the ruled words: each a group element spelled from
  the letters, carried by the conformal versor that places it and the
  gauge permutation that colours it. A word acts on a chart; its transport
  to another chart is a conjugation (T19, 3.10), so two conjugate words
  are one generator seen from two charts (23.9, the conjugate level), and
  the class vector is the coordinate that generator is filed under.
- **Relations** are the sentences: an orbit whose holonomy composes to the
  identity is a relation among the generators, which is what "each orbit
  is a theorem" (law 12, 2.3) says.
- **Sections** of a punctured axis (25) add coordinates to a generator's
  fibre, never letters to the group.

Read cohomologically, the same object is the gluing data of a principal
bundle over the atlas (the bundle ruling of 2026-09-02): the ruled words
are its transition functions, a Čech 1-cocycle with values in the group;
the sentences are the cocycle condition on the triple overlaps; a germ is
a 1-cochain that fails it, the residual the coboundary leaves; and the
genome is the cocycle the court has ruled, taught down by the syllabus.
