and `court attest` with a sentence replayed, and `remainder expressed`
appears nowhere.

### 50.8 The levels of one remainder (ruled 2026-09-10)

Chapter 50.5 typed what `F` cannot do; until this ruling its demands had
no consumer in the running engine, and a demand without a consumer is a
sensor without an effector. The consumer is **one** — 37.7's adjunction —
and this section says what the remainder's canonical form is at each
level the factorisation can stop at. Neither level is a search and
neither is a commit; neither is a closer written for a kind.

**The field of the letters — `RotorPrime`.** The letter a prime demands is
the witness rotor's own Gaussian factor; two independent courts re-derive
it from the witness at one chart, the home opens it, and the syllabus
teaches it before any voice speaks it (37.7, law 6 as ruled). The alphabet grows by ruling, at run time, and
every voice that learned the page spells the same word.

**The topology of the bodies — `TopologicalDeformation`.** No versor
carries a body onto an image with different harmonics; but a body is a
union of pieces, and pieces carry. The cover does not refine below a body
(51.3 as ruled 2026-09-18): a piece is a word vertex only if it is a body
under 51.3's definition (one hue, 6-adjacent across the whole family).
Under no circumstances does `cover.rs` or `peel_body_scaled` shatter a body
into single-pixel laminae to force a carriage. What no single versor carries
whole is not a listing of pieces but one demand of the kind its reading types
(50.5), with contact faces between pieces carrying `Γ` (50.3). Then, by the pieces'
overlap:

1. **Every meet good and every edge in the stabilizer.** The pieces glue
   to one section (13.9 step 5, `∂θ = 1`): the deformation was a rigid
   motion of a body the eyes had cut, and there is no demand.
2. **A pair of pieces with no `V_ij`.** A remainder edge (50.3): the two
   pieces are two charts, the sentence is split by Mayer–Vietoris (13.9),
   and it is valid with the split and no demand.
3. **An orbit through the meet.** Where two pieces' meet has more than one
   component (13.9 step 0; the arcs of a ring, the arms of a fork), the
   pieces' nerve has a cycle, and the product of `Γ` around it, read in
   the base piece's stabilizer up to conjugacy, is the deformation's own
   holonomy. Finite order (15.3): `cech::extend` files the 2-simplex whose
   boundary is that orbit, `Fill::Class(ℓ)`, and the sentence carries the
   class as its theorem (law 12) — the filled simplex is a constructor the
   mind glues by (25.3), the degree-2 class of 15.4 keyed by the orbit and
   the holonomy's invariants, carried or discharged under refinement
   (15.5), and 13.9 step 7 finds the same class at the court. Infinite
   order: `Fill::Open`, the orbit is held with its class vector (12.6), and
   the `TopologicalDeformation` vertex stands as 50.5 says.
4. **Laminae of `B_out` no piece reaches, or of `B_in` no piece carries.**
   `Source` or `Creation` vertices ride beside (50.5): a hole that opens
   or closes is those laminae, not a holonomy, and is never a class.

Nothing chooses the cover: the pieces are the peel's shells, the orbit is
the meet's, the order is the class's, and the court re-derives all three.
`court simplex filled` (34.2) is the line at the court and `simplex filled
{addr} class {ℓ}` at the voice.

**Binding.** `family/perceive.rs`: `demand_vertex`'s deformation arm peels
the pair into pieces and speaks them (`pieces_of` NEW over
`peel_body_scaled` and `blade::components`); `family/pair.rs`: contact
faces between pieces with their edges; `cech/simplex.rs` `extend`
unchanged; `sentence/form/carrier.rs`: the filled simplex on the form's
tape beside its orbits (tape v7, one recut with 37.7's escape byte);
`court/verdict/replay.rs`: the filled simplex replayed as any orbit
(`REFUSE_SIMPLEX_ORDER` when the loop's order is not the filed `ℓ`). Tests:
`a_deformed_body_is_spoken_as_pieces_that_carry`,
`a_loop_of_pieces_with_finite_holonomy_fills_a_simplex`,
`a_loop_of_pieces_with_infinite_holonomy_stands_as_a_demand`,
`a_hole_is_laminae_never_a_class`,
`the_court_rederives_a_filled_simplex_or_refuses_it`.

**The ruling, as given (2026-09-10).** The seams are severed first (L6 to
L8): no generator is grown on a substrate that leaks chains. No search
returns: a generator is measured at the moment of failure and held as a
typed invariant, never found by a beam. And chapter 37's opening is the
court's own transition, automated on the congruence of two courts'
re-derivations, not an operator's intervention.

### 50.9 The contraction protocol (ruled 2026-09-10)

The ruling names this section 50.7; 50.7 is the binding table and 50.8
the walls, so it stands here. A refusal that does not change the
speaker's state transition is an inert log line, not a protocol: a voice
that utters a sentence, receives a refusal and re-emits the same tape on
the next stroke is deaf, and a mesh of such voices is an echo chamber.
The feedback orbit is an algebraic contraction on the held form, certified
like a pivot (A20) and verified by the court like any move.

**The judicial reply.** The court never returns an opaque byte. Its
answer to an utterance is the `Adjudication` of chapter 26:

```
Adjudication := Stood { receipt } | Ratified { receipt } | Refused { kind, at, receipt }
kind         := VertexBody | EdgeHolonomy | RemainderUndeclared | OrbitStill | FaceDerivation | MalformedComplex
at           := Vertex(address, chart) | Face(address_i, address_j) | Chart(invariant, links) | Tape(address)
```

`OrbitStill` and `FaceDerivation` are ruled 2026-09-17 (night, R1): a
contact word the court's family does not orbit (22, 23.1 step 6) is
refused at the vertex with the chart it acts on, and a face that does not
re-derive from its vertices (23.1 step 4) at its two addresses. Before
this ruling both travelled as a `MalformedComplex` at the tape, the one
kind the voice does not contract, and 61 of the 111 refusals the courts
wrote in the recut's first 75 minutes were of these two kinds.

`Stood` is the docket's receipt: the sentence replayed on the court's copy
of the family, the closed sub-complex docketed under the voice's room, the
demands listed. `Ratified` is the second organ's co-signature, carried on
the syllabus page (47.3), and the answer to a sentence the court's
language already holds — a use of a ruled word. `Refused` names the kind
(34.1) and the coordinate as content — the vertex's address with the chart
it acts on, a face's two addresses, or the chart with the links the court
read — never a position in the tape; `Tape(address)` is the coordinate of
a `MalformedComplex`, the whole tape. The chart rides with the vertex so
that a court which never held the refused tape can still verify that the
demand stands on that chart (the L8 landing; a coordinate the ruling's
grammar left implicit). The receipt is the court's own replay receipt
(45.1, 47.1). The door's deferral (23.8) is the act's deferral frame,
never an adjudication: nothing was heard. A wait is not an admission
either (ruled 2026-09-17, night, R5): the citer is not filed as taught
and is spoken again — owed with its cited form to the courts in turn, at
most once per court this mind knows, and heard where the citation is
ruled; a citation this mind sealed is owed to no court; and a refused
sentence leaves the dialect with its refusal (24.2: the dialect is what
stood), so no form glues it and no sentence cites it again. Before this
ruling a wait filed the citer as taught and the owed frame carried
nothing past the taught gate: the recut's first 2½ hours wrote 1 907
waits on the voices, none re-heard, 996 of them citing an address the
voice had sealed.

**The six certified contraction moves.** On `Refused { kind, at }` the
voice executes a shrinking move `C : S → S'` on the held form in its
contemplation, and every move strictly decrements the closed sub-complex,
so the loop is well founded:

1. `VertexBody` at `Vertex(a, chart)`: the word vertex `a` becomes a
   demand vertex over its body's chart — `Creation`, carrying as its
   bodies the laminae the word was to reach, read as the remainder the
   contracted form leaves on the speaker's own family — and the closed
   sub-complex loses one word; the faces that reached the vertex leave
   with it, since a demand vertex enters no face (50.5). The
   `TopologicalDeformation` kind names harmonics the cover of 50.8 (L11)
   reads; until it lands the move speaks `Creation` (a departure of kind,
   named at the L8 landing).
2. `EdgeHolonomy` at `Face(a, b)`: the contact face becomes a remainder
   edge (`edge: None`, 50.3); the 2-simplex whose boundary ran through it is
   unlinked. The coordinate carries no cycle, so nothing is filed as
   torsion here: a finite cycle is filed where it is walked, by the pivot
   (A17).
3. `RemainderUndeclared` at `Chart(inv, links)`: the undeclared links
   become `Demand::Source` over that chart, with the multiplicity the
   count of bodies the links fall into (50.5); the sentence now declares
   what it does not close.
4. `MalformedComplex`: structural collapse — the form becomes an inert
   held idea and the mind is quiescent on that chart until its language
   moves; nothing is re-spoken.
5. `OrbitStill` at `Vertex(a, chart)` (ruled 2026-09-17, night): the
   contact word `a` did not orbit on the court's family — its word is the
   identity, or its first step leaves the ring unchanged (22). The vertex
   becomes a demand over that chart exactly as move 1 makes it, carrying
   the laminae it was to reach; the closed sub-complex loses one word.
6. `FaceDerivation` at `Face(a, b)` (ruled 2026-09-17, night): the face
   between `a` and `b` does not re-derive from its vertices — its word is
   not their coboundary and it is no loop's chord. The face leaves the
   form and the two vertices stand without it; an orbit through it
   dissolves, and the closed sub-complex loses one face.

Each move is a form rewrite with a certificate, `Contraction { kind, at,
before: address, after: address, receipt }`, filed on the idea beside its
pivot certificates and written as `contracted {addr} → {addr'} by {kind}
at {coordinate}` (34.3).

**The re-utterance ban.** A refusal is an admitted act of the mind (45.1)
and seals a receipt on the mind's own chain; the refused address is
sealed in the utterance index (`taught_up`, 24.3) with the refusal. The
speak path reads the sealed set before any frame is built, and a sealed
tape is refused by the mind itself — `sealed {addr}: refused at K {k},
not uttered again` — so re-uttering the identical sentence is
structurally impossible: the only door out is a new address, and the only
way to a new address is a changed form. The ruling as given says this
refusal "raises an immediate runtime panic"; §2.4 and the panics gate
forbid an abort in cognition, and the effect the ruling asks for — the
identical tape cannot leave — is exactly what the sealed set gives without
one. That is a departure of word, not of invariant, and it is named here.

**The contraction is verified by the receiver.** The only valid
subsequent utterance is `S'`, citing the refusal receipt as its
contraction certificate, carried on the speech frame beside the tape
(26). The court that issued the receipt holds the refusal by the refused
address; it replays that `S'` is `C(S)` at the coordinate it named — the
vertex is now a demand on that chart, the face now a remainder edge, the
links now declared, the contact word now a demand, the face now gone —
before it replays `S'` as a sentence, and writes
`court contraction verified` or `court contraction refused` (34.2); a
contraction it refuses is a `MalformedComplex` at the tape. A court that
never refused `S` holds no receipt to verify against and replays `S'` as
a sentence, verifying nothing: the certificate is a claim on one court's
chain, and 47.3's second organ re-derives the sentence, not the refusal.
Bilateral synchronization is therefore a proof the court checks, not a
discipline the voice is trusted to keep.

**The contraction certificate is the only thing that rides beside the
tape** (ruled 2026-09-10). It is a claim about *which utterance this is*
— a receipt naming a prior refusal — so it is not a coordinate of the
form and belongs on the frame. A word's derivation is the opposite kind
of object: it is what the vertex is, it is replayed as part of `G`, and
it is on the tape at v7 (50.2 step 2). The earlier reading that put the
path on the speech frame beside the sentence is struck; nothing about a
vertex's meaning travels outside the tape that carries the vertex.

**The intelligibility assertion.** The protocol is proved by one exchange
run in-process through the dialogue codec, with no socket: Voice A utters
`S`; Court 1 replays on its copy of the family and answers a typed
adjudication; Voice A receives it, contracts, and utters `S'` citing the
receipt, or is quiescent; Court 2 — a second kernel with its own identity
and no shared runtime memory (the pair form's memo cleared or on its own
thread) — replays the serialized frame and reaches the same address and
the same standing. A single differing rational refuses consilience (13.9
step 8). Until that test passes the tree has an echo chamber; when it
passes it has a medium.

**The soak invariant.** Across any round trip the closed sub-complex of a
sentence either grows, because a demand was answered by a taught word, or
shrinks, because a vertex was refused; it never stands. No address is
uttered twice with the same standing, and the auditor greps for
`adjudicated … refused` lines followed by the same address uttered
unchanged.

**Binding.** `anastome/dialogue/speech.rs`: `Adjudication` on the speech
reply; `book/speech.rs` `perceive_speech`: the court's one entry point for
an utterance, answering an adjudication per sentence and verifying a cited
contraction; `client/sdk/entity/utter.rs`: `receive_adjudication`, the
sealed set on the utterance index, the contraction certificate on the
next utterance; `sentence/form/contract.rs`: the six moves on a held
idea's form (`contract`) and the court's reader of each
(`is_contraction_at`); `sentence/form/certificate.rs`: `Contraction`
beside `PivotCertificate`; tests: `a_refusal_contracts_the_held_form_and_seals_the_address`,
`a_sealed_tape_is_refused_by_the_mind_before_the_wire`,
`the_court_verifies_a_contraction_before_it_replays_the_sentence`,
`two_courts_of_distinct_identity_reach_one_standing_through_the_codec`,
`a_still_orbit_contracts_its_contact_word_to_a_demand`,
`a_face_that_does_not_rederive_is_dropped_by_its_contraction`,
`a_refused_sentence_leaves_the_dialect`,
`a_citation_is_owed_once_per_court_and_a_sealed_one_to_none`,
`a_code_the_hypha_did_not_send_is_not_an_outcome` (a wait admits nothing).

### 50.10 The court adjudicates words; grammar is content (ruled 2026-09-22)

The operator's ruling, on the reading that the courts of epoch 96
adjudicated 2 751 sentences, hardened some 440 words per court into every
genome, and adjoined nothing: **the court adjudicates words, and the
construction of sentences is the language's own grammar, held as content
above a fixed interpreter.** Neither half reopens "sentences only" (law 8,
50.6); both are read inside it.

**A word is a one-vertex sentence.** Chapter 50.1's theorem has two
conditions, and the first — the vertex reconstructs its body,
`(V·W·γ)·B_in = B_out`, exactly, on the frames it claims — is a condition
on one vertex and no face. A form of one word vertex carrying its body is
therefore a valid sentence with no faces, no loops and no second
condition, and it is uttered, replayed and ruled exactly as any sentence:
the voice speaks it, the court replays it by M1 (the rotor composed from
the cited generators and compared projectively) and by 23.1 step 3 (the
body carried), a witness re-derives it, the home installs it, and the
syllabus teaches it. That is the path from Stood to Ruled, from the
dialect to the genome, and it is the court adjudicating a word. What
"sentences only" refused was never this; it refused a chain of links with
no vertex around it, which reconstructs nothing (50.6, the three seams).
A word that fails its own body on a frame it claims is refused at the
vertex (`REFUSE_VERTEX_BODY`); a word that carries its body on the frames
it was measured at and is silent on the others is a section (51.8) and is
ruled on the frames it names.

**Measured, epoch 96, before this ruling:** the mint refused 4 653 words
for not carrying their family, 3 501 of them at `a lamina lands on the
wrong hue`, and the failing frame was the first frame of the family — the
frame the word was measured on — in 2 016 of 3 501 three-frame cases. A
word refused on the frame it was read from is not a word that fails its
family; it is a quotient measured against a chart whose gauge the vertex
does not carry, and that is read before anything is changed (row W2).

**Grammar is content, and the interpreter is not.** How words are put
into sentences — which pairs are related, by what transport, under which
relators the orbits must close, which rewrites carry one derivation to
another — is the presentation of 1.8 and the deeper nodes of 1.9: relators
at depth 4, rewrites at depth 5, procedures over the crystals at depth 6,
each adjoined by two courts on one witness and taught by the syllabus,
each held, cited, paid and retired as a generator is. That is what
"modifiable after run time" means here, on the voices and on the courts
alike and on trajectories that differ by construction, since epigenomes
diverge and covers converge. What never changes at run time is the
interpreter — the geometric product over exact ℚ, the canonical forms, the
peel, the coboundary (1.8, 1.9) — because two courts replay one another
through it and a court running a different interpreter is a different
mathematics. Today the sentence constructors are F on the voice (50.2)
and G on the court, written in the host; they become content node by node
as 37.7 fires at each depth, never by a commit that makes the grammar a
table.

**Order.** Words are hardened as one-vertex sentences now (W1), on the
corpus, without waiting for an orbit; faces and orbits enter as H2c and H3
make their transports readable; the first generator adjoined by closure
is the gate on depths 4–6, and nothing at those depths is authored by hand
before it.

**Binding.**

```
family/deflation.rs         mint_sentence — a form of one word vertex that
                            carries its body is minted; `acts()` already
                            admits it and `vertices_carry_frames` rules it
court/verdict/body.rs       vertices_carry_frames — 23.1 step 3 on the
                            frames the word claims (W2 reads its faults)
server/cognition/book/      the install path, unchanged: Stood → Ruled
transducer/alphabet/        F, the constructor on the voice, host-written
                            until depth 5–6 make it content
```

### 70.6 Contact is the shared boundary of two cube complexes; its content is conformal (ruled 2026-09-23)

The operator's reading of H2b: the corner test is flat. It reads two
coordinates, `|Δr| = 1` and `|Δc| = 1` within one frame, so the frame
axis, the gauge and every luminal direction play no part in whether two
bodies touch, and a body-pair relation read on two coordinates is
checklist (m) written into contact. The implementor's proposal in reply —
contact as the bivector `S_a ∧ S_b` of the two bodies' conformal spheres,
touching where its square is zero — is refused where it stands, because
59.4 already rules it: exact tangency of two rational spheres is
measure-zero over ℚ and can never be the test, which is why the strain
band had to exist and why it turned away touching bodies (69.2). WHETHER
two bodies touch is topological and WHAT their contact is like is
conformal (69.3), and the two are inflated separately.

**Whether: the cube complex, in three coordinates.** A body's support is
a cube complex on `(r, c, k)` (51.3), and two distinct hue-blind bodies
never share a face of a cube, since sharing one they would be one body
(70.4). They touch where their complexes share an EDGE or a CORNER: the
twelve edge-adjacencies of a cube — four in the frame, which is the
diagonal H2b reads, and eight across consecutive frames, `(r ± 1, c, k ± 1)`
and `(r, c ± 1, k ± 1)` — and the eight corner-adjacencies, all three
coordinates differing by one. That is the whole shared boundary a cube
complex has left once its faces are interior, it is exact and integer, it
is read off the occupancy in canonical order exactly as `incidence_of_3d`
and `incidence_diagonal_3d` are, and it consults no extent, no sphere and
no band. Contact across frames is the frame axis entering contact, and it
is where a body that moves between frames meets a body that stands.

**One face per body pair.** A corner names two sites and each site names
its occupants; the contact is between the two BODIES, one per site under
70.4, and the face is offered once per body pair with the members'
readings riding it as N1's set. Relating every occupant of one site to
every occupant of the other, as H2b landed it, is the join of two
occupancy simplices written as a clique — the same shape the site pass
refuses in its own comment — and is corrected (row C1).

**What: the face's content, in ten planes.** The dimensions the corner
test does not read are the face's to carry, and every one already has a
row: the edge transport `g_ab = (θ_bθ_a⁻¹)·γ_ab` in `Cl(4,1)` (60.1),
read or refused by name (H2c); the strain sector of the two spheres as a
keyed coordinate of the pair, never a band (T3), which is where
`S_a ∧ S_b` belongs — as the content of a contact the topology already
found, not as the test for it; the hue gauge as the face's fibre (H3). A
contact face whose transport refuses is a zero-dimensional relation, and
that, not the corner test, is the flatness the 21 unread cycles measure.

**The interface is not flat, and it is not a count (ruled 2026-09-23,
the operator's word).** Two bodies meet along the SET of boundary
elements their cube complexes share — a staircase of edges, a run of
corners, several islands of each — and that set is the contact face's
own coordinates (69.3: the face is the set of edges with their
coordinates, never a tally). It is a sub-complex on the base with a
topology of its own (its components and its runs) and a geometry of its
own: read as laminae it lifts through `blade::lift` like any support, and
A.11's tower on the interface says whether it is straight, bent, ridged
or pointed — the deviatoric along one axis for a flat seam, the higher
harmonics for the bumps — exactly, over ℚ, with no root and no fit. A
flat interface and a ridged one between the same two bodies are two
contacts with two faces, and the difference is the face's content, which
the edge transport `g_ab` is measured against per member pair. The
twenty adjacencies find the interface; the interface's tower and its
transport are what the face carries; and the 26-neighbourhood of the
implementor's reading is these twenty plus the six face-adjacencies that
make a body (70.4), which is one primitive read at two depths and never
two.

```
sentence/chain.rs        incidence_diagonal_3d → the twenty shared-boundary
                         adjacencies of the cube complex on (r, c, k)
family/pairing.rs        named_faces — one face per body pair at a corner
blade/strain.rs          the sector, a coordinate of the pair (T3)
```

### 70.7 The interface is a chart, and a contact is a 2-simplex (ruled 2026-09-23)

The operator's reading of Phase C: the engine has flattened again. The
tree spent its last two weeks getting out of the crystal's rigidity and
into the manifold — the conformal sphere for a body, the ten planes for a
transport, curvature as content — and Phase C answers "where do two
bodies meet" with the boundary of a cube complex on an integer lattice and
carries the answer as a list of sites. The lattice is right where it is
read and wrong where it is held. What is corrected:

**The lattice is the retina; nothing above the sensor holds it.** Reading
the twenty shared-boundary adjacencies off the occupancy is a sensor
reading under law 11: it is exact, it is the only place the pixel grid is
allowed to decide anything, and it decides one thing — WHICH bodies meet,
and WHERE on the base. That reading ends at the sensor boundary. What
crosses the boundary into the form is not the site list: a face that
holds `Vec<(i64, i64, i64)>` is a form holding the sensor's coordinates as
cognition (law 11, checklist (f′)), a projection carried as the primary
object (checklist (m)). The interface is LIFTED at the boundary, once,
exactly as a body is: its shared elements are its support, `blade::lift`
gives it a blade — nucleus, tower, sphere — and its chart is
`Harmonics::axes` of that blade. The face carries the interface's chart
and its address (the support written out, A21, so the lift re-derives,
law 12), never a count and never a list the mind computes on. Phase C's
`interface_tower` is the lift; the site list beside it goes.

**The interface is a chart of the cover.** The interface has a support, a
blade and a chart, which is what a chart of the cover is (53.1), and it
lies in both bodies' closures. A contact is therefore not an edge between
two vertices with a payload; it is the 2-simplex `A – I – B` of the
nerve: three charts, three transitions, and the cocycle condition
`g_AI · g_IB · g_BA = 1` on the triple (13.9, 58.1). That is the 2-cell
this corpus has never had — `read_nerve` certified 0 triples on 252 forms
because no two charts of a cover ever shared a third — and it is where
the ten planes enter: `g_AI` and `g_IB` are transports in `Cl(4,1)` read
by 60.1's interface versor with the interface's own frame as the middle
term, and the holonomy of the triangle is curvature between two bodies
measured at their meeting rather than along a chord through empty space
(55.2's scalar collapse, the pure boost between two centroids, is
exactly what a centroid-to-centroid transport re-commits).

**"Against the interface" means through it.** The edge transport of a
contact factors through the interface chart: `g_AB = g_AI · g_IB`, each
factor a transport between a body's frame `θ` and the interface's frame
`θ_I` read off the interface's deviatoric and higher harmonics, the
basepoint transvection between the body's nucleus and the interface's.
A flat seam has `θ_I` along one axis; a ridged one carries its bumps in
the tower; the gauge cocycle `δ⁰θ` is read across the laminae of the
interface set (H3). Nothing here is a chord, a centroid pair or a band.

**Identity by address, never by a site.** Phase C keys a body pair by the
two bodies' root sites and reads the element's sides in that order. A
site is a position of the base (vocabulary, "site"); a body's identity is
its address, the support written out (`coord::Piece`). The pair is keyed
by the two addresses in canonical order, the interface by its own address,
and no position enters a key (rule 6, law 11).

**The orientation defect is fixed at every site of its shape.** All 18
unread cycles are `no place`: on a contact face between two members of
one vertex the walk's direction test `f.i == v_i && f.j == v_j` is
always true and the pair key is read backwards half the time. That is
437d253's defect at a second site, and a ruling is applied at every site
of its shape (backtrack ledger, 2026-09-07): the walk orients a face by
its member pair, never by its vertex pair, and the 18 cycles are re-read
after the fix as the first inter-body holonomies of this corpus (O1).

**What Phase C got right stands.** The twenty adjacencies, one face per
body pair, the frame axis in contact (160 pairs that touch across frames
only), the unread gate split by cause, the address carrying the interface
at the recut. Only what the face holds, how the pair is named, and what
the transport is measured through are corrected.

**Amended 2026-09-23 on the implementor's reading of the physics: the
face's content is the field's own, and nothing is invented for it.** The
engine already carries the interface conformally. `Interface::between(a,
b)` is the whole product of the two nuclei split by grade: grade 0 is the
strain `(num, den2)`, exact and never rooted (59.3, 63.1), and grade 2 is
the coaxal pencil `s_a ∧ s_b`, the blade the two spheres share their
boundary through (59.2). The edge is refraction, `g_ab = (θ_b θ_a⁻¹)·γ_ab`
(60.1, 64.3), the relative frame off the two towers composed with the
transvection between the nuclei; where `θ` refuses, `NoFrame` names the
arm and only `Oblique` is a demand (67.1). So "the interface is lifted
once" means: the lattice reads WHETHER two bodies meet and on which
shared cell (71.2(2)); the face then carries `Interface::between` — the
strain and the pencil blade — as its content and `g_ab` as its edge, with
the refusal named on the line. The lattice set of shared elements is the
finding of whether and enters no address; the address keys the pencil
blade's coordinates (A21) and the contact's grade. Phase C's doubled
centres were a second, Euclidean carrier of what `Interface::between`
already holds (law 12), and they go with BQ5. The field's pair loop (F1)
dissolves in the same move: the strain, the pencil and the frame are read
on the pairs the lattice names and on no others, so the band no longer
gates whether (69.2's size disparity) and T3's sector becomes a
coordinate of a contact rather than a cure for an orbit. What stays open
and is written as open: A.10 asks that two manifolds share a boundary
through a null gradient and the corpus's meets read timelike (57.4,
55.7) — whether a contact's pencil is ever luminal is a measurement, at
`μ = 0` (59.7); and A.13 is docketed and not built — every motion the
engine expresses fixes infinity because the special conformal half is
missing — which is the most direct statement in the tree of where the
mathematics is still pinned to a Euclidean origin, and it is the next
axiom row after Phase N. `Strain::between` reads three centroid
coordinates today; it goes to `n` with BQ4.

```
family/pairing.rs        the twenty adjacencies read at the sensor; the
                         interface lifted there, once
sentence/form/face.rs    FormFace.interface → the interface's chart and
                         address, never Vec<(i64,i64,i64)>
family/cover.rs          the interface as a chart of the cover; the
                         contact as the 2-simplex A – I – B
cech/nerve.rs            read_nerve certifies the triple
sentence/pivot/walk.rs   orientation by member pair (O1)
```

# Part XI — The frame axis

Written 2026-09-11 against c27ea76 as the L22 draft; **ruled 2026-09-17**
by the operator, with 51.2 amended as stated there and 51.7 read against
tape v9. The code that lands it is Stage 18 of `MU-RECURSION-TASKS.md`:
one recut after the landing's final commit (§10), localized testing only
until then, and the fleet is not swapped before the operator's word.

## 51. `k` is a coordinate of the base (L22 draft, 2026-09-11)

Carried from 36.2: "A third spatial axis…, the frame index as a coordinate
the geometry can act on, and transformations that move structure across
frames have no coordinate on the base and land only as remainder or fibre
tag. The alphabet already acts on four axes and six planes; three of the
six touch the fourth axis and are unused by perception. The upgrade is to
let perception write on them."

Today `k` is the position of a pair in `task.train`. That is a member
named by its position in a carrier — rule 15's own shape — and "all pairs
agree" is then a correspondence search across forms that were perceived
separately, which is L8v's cost and L20's orbit. The whole of this chapter
is one move: `k` stops being a position and becomes a coordinate.

### 51.1 The coordinate

`k` is the third **point coordinate of the base**, carried on `e₃`.

- **Origin.** `k = 0` is the family's first pair as the corpus writes it.
  The origin is the corpus's, not the engine's, and it is not measured:
  a family arrives as an ordered list of pairs and that order is the
  datum. What changes is what the order MEANS — a coordinate, on which a
  translation is a versor, rather than an index, on which nothing acts.
- **Unit.** One pair. Not seconds, not receipts, not a tick: `k` is
  spatial, and 16.16's `𝒯` lane — extent held in receipts — is untouched
  by it. A family with three pairs occupies `k ∈ {0, 1, 2}` exactly as a
  body of three laminae occupies three rows.
- **It is the BASE's coordinate, not a fibre tag.** A fibre tag is
  something a transformation lands on when it has nowhere to go on the
  base (36.2's own words). The point of putting `k` on `e₃` is that a
  transformation across frames HAS somewhere to go: it is a versor on a
  plane touching `e₃`, acting on the same body every other letter acts
  on. If `k` were a tag, `e₃` would be a second carrier beside the
  support and rule 12 would be broken — one fact, one carrier.
- **A consequence, stated so it is not discovered later.** 18.2 quotients
  the body's absolute position on `(e₀, e₁)`: two bodies differing by a
  translation are one word. With `k` on `e₃` the SAME quotient applies
  along `e₃`, so a family and the same family with its pairs shifted by
  one frame are one body. That is correct and it is what makes agreement
  a symmetry rather than a coincidence; it also means the frame origin
  carries no meaning, which is why 51.1 gives it none.

### 51.2 The algebra, derived

The rule — stated here, once, and cited elsewhere as 18.1's — is that the
algebra is derived from what the base carries and is never asserted, with
the one exception ruled at the end of this section. Today:

- `Rotor` is `Cl(4,0)` over `e₀..e₃`: sixteen blades, six planes. This is
  the LETTERS' chart and it does not move — the seventeen already act on
  four axes (51.6).
- `Versor` is `cga::Mv`, `Cl(3,1)` over `e₁, e₂, e₊, e₋`: sixteen blades,
  the conformal model of a base with TWO point coordinates. That is the
  bridge, and `sensor_action_of` is lossy across it by construction.

With `k` on the base the base has THREE point coordinates `(r, c, k)`.
The conformal model of an `n`-dimensional base is `Cl(n+1, 1)`, so the
versor algebra becomes `Cl(4,1)`: **thirty-two blades**, one rotation
plane becoming three.

**Sixty-four blades are DROPPED, and here is the derivation.** `Cl(5,1)`
is the conformal model of FOUR point coordinates. The base does not have
four. The letters' chart has four AXES, but `e₂` is not a point
coordinate of it: `LetterId::SHEET` is the quarter turn on `(1,2)` and two
of them are the ORIENTATION CHARACTER of the sensor plane — `PlaneForm`
reads `orientation` as `det/ρ² = −1` on exactly that composite. An
orientation character is a ±1 the chart carries, not a place a lamina sits
at. So the base's point coordinates are `e₀` (row), `e₁` (column) and `e₃`
(frame); `e₂` keeps the role it has and gains nothing.

`Cl(4,1)` it is, and the sheet plane's role is unchanged — which is 51.3's
first requirement and is why the two points agree.

**The one stated exception to "derived, never asserted" (ruled
2026-09-17).** `Spin(4,1)` is two groups in one algebra: the conformal
group of the three-coordinate base, whose translators `e_i ∧ e_∞`
commute, and the isometry group of hyperbolic 4-space whose boundary at
infinity is that base, whose transvections `e_i ∧ e₋` do not commute —
their commutator is a rotation scaled by the sectional curvature. A
lattice base carries the first reading, and it is derived. The second is
ASSERTED here, ahead of any datum, so that a remainder shaped as
curvature has an algebra to land in rather than a demand it can only
stand in. This is rule 11's one stated exception, and it is the algebra
that is asserted, never a value of the curvature: `K` is read off a
remainder or it is not read. The rotor chart `Cl(4,0)` does not move
(51.6); the letters act on a Euclidean chart, and a boost is never a
letter.

### 51.3 The lamina, the body, the shape, the moduli

**Ruled 2026-09-17, evening, on the operator's word.** The morning's
draft of this section made the sensor's atom a five-field tuple `(r, c,
k, before, after)` on every carrier and codec. Read against the tree
before it was landed, that widens the lattice where the doctrine retires
it: every keyed read, sort, floor and adjacency of the plane would have
stayed and gained a third field, which is checklist (m)'s projection
carried as the primary object, now in three coordinates. The five places
the plane is actually carried as the primary object are named here so the
repair is bounded: (1) the blade kept a body's support as `(r, c)` and
dropped `k`, so a body spanning frames had the topology, turns and
boundary of its planar shadow; (2) the sensor's site reader refused every
point outside frame `0`, so a transport along `e₃` landed on no lamina
and the replay, the gauge reading and the seam reading took that for
nothing to disagree with; (3) the sensor read a carried square back as
the laminae whose centres fall between two carried corners — the mind
writing to the lattice mid-reasoning; (4) extraction's move 1 matched
bodies across separately perceived pair forms; (5) the family was handled
pair by pair. A link stays four fields and a lamina is the sensor's token
(law 11, 16.5); the frame is on the pose and on the blade; what follows
is the section as ruled.

- **`Body`** — laminae, shape, moduli — is unchanged in kind. Its laminae
  are the sensor's support, `(r, c, k, hue)`, ONE carrier (the two
  supports of 656918d were two carriers for one fact, law 12, and are
  retired); its connectivity is 4-adjacency on `(r, c)` WITHIN a frame and
  adjacency along `k` BETWEEN consecutive frames, which is 6-adjacency on
  the three axes. A body is then a connected component of one hue across
  the whole family, not within one pair. Adjacency along `e₃` is the
  corpus's — consecutive pairs — and is read by the chart: a versor that
  spaces frames apart (a dilation about a point off a frame) carries the
  laminae and not the body's adjacency, so its two ends are two charts, a
  section and never a congruence.
- **`Shape`** is the blade of the support and gains the third coordinate
  with it. `blade::shape_of` takes sites of three coordinates, one
  function; the blade's own support keeps the three, so the topology, the
  turns and the boundary are read on the stack and not on its shadow.
- **Moduli** are `blade::moduli` of that blade, the axes coarsest first:
  components, tunnels and cavities (`β₀, β₁, β₂` of the support's cube
  complex under 6-adjacency, `χ = V − E + F − C` counted through
  incidence as the plane's was); turns (the sum over the sections of
  their turning counts); the isoperimetric ratio (the sections' perimeter,
  squared, over the laminae); the frame boundary (the sides open along
  `e₃` over the laminae — `2` for one section, less for a stack); the
  in-plane anisotropy; the spread (the three-coordinate trace over the
  laminae squared); the quartic; the gauge spectrum. Every axis is
  invariant under every versor the sensor carries a lamina by, and a body
  of one frame reads on its old axes what it read before, with `cavities
  0` and `frame boundary 2` beside them. A chart that distinguished two
  bodies on two axes still distinguishes them on three.
- **The harmonics** are read on the support as they are now. A family of
  three identical pairs has a body that is PERIODIC along `e₃` with
  period one; its periodicity is read by 51.5's orbit, not by an axis, and
  its chart says only what its moments and boundary say.
- **The sheet plane's role is unchanged.** `(1,2)` is still where
  orientation lives; nothing in 51.3 puts a site coordinate on `e₂`.
- **A piece is a word vertex only if it is a body (ruled 2026-09-18).** A piece
  is a word vertex only if it is a body under 51.3's definition: a connected
  component of one hue, 6-adjacent across the whole family. The cover does not
  refine below a body; under no circumstances does `cover.rs` or `peel_body_scaled`
  shatter a body into single-pixel laminae or concentric peel rings to force a
  carriage. What no single versor carries whole is not a listing of pieces but one
  demand of the kind its reading types (50.5, 50.8). Cited from 50.8 and 23.1 step 6.

### 51.4 The family is one body

`TrainPair` and `Family` retire as CARRIERS. They stay as what the corpus
serves — a task's JSON is still a list of pairs — and they stop being
what the engine reasons over.

- The family is ONE body, on `(r, c, k)`.
- A pair is that body's **section along `e₃`**: the slice at `k = i`.
  `Form.sections` is already the carrier for sections, `Keyed<Vec<u16>>`,
  and a section along `e₃` is one of them.
- The **test pair is the frame with an open output**: the slice at
  `k = n` whose `after` is unwritten. Speaking the rule is then not a
  separate move — it is filling the one section the body leaves open,
  which is what `speak_rule` does today with an extra concept.
- `perceive` runs ONCE, on the whole family, and returns bodies of three
  coordinates. `pair_form` — one form per pair — is what disappears, and
  with it the correspondence between separately perceived forms.

### 51.5 Extraction is a symmetry along `e₃`

Today: seven moves over `m` separately perceived pair forms, matching
vertices across them by transport class. With one body:

- **Agreement across pairs is the body's symmetry along `e₃`.** A rule
  that holds in every pair is a translation along `e₃` that carries the
  body onto itself: a versor on a plane touching `e₃`, read as holonomy
  around the orbit that translation closes. That is ONE orbit check, on one
  form, by the machinery 12.2 already has.
- **Which of the seven moves survive.**
  1. *Correspondence by transport class* — GONE. It exists to match
     vertices across forms and there is one form.
  2. *Constancy of faces* — SURVIVES, unchanged in kind: faces are still
     the star from the Frame and the bodies whose supports meet. Their
     supports now meet along `e₃` as well, which is what makes the
     periodic body connected.
  3. *Gluing* — SURVIVES unchanged. It asks the crystal at a body's
     chart; the chart is richer and the question is the same.
  4. *Rebasing* — SURVIVES unchanged. "Do to B what A did to itself" is
     a relation between two vertices of one form and never used the pair
     index.
  5. *Unfolding* — SURVIVES and becomes NATURAL: "the output is the input
     under `k` applications" is, with `k` a coordinate, a statement that
     the body is periodic along `e₃`. The `Measure` and the stop
     criterion stay; what goes is that `k` was a count in a carrier.
  6. *Contact* — SURVIVES unchanged. A ring distance to an anchor is
     measured on the support and the support gained an axis.
  7. *Coherence* — SURVIVES, and becomes the WHOLE of extraction's
     verdict: `coheres`, then `solve_coboundary` and `regauge`, then a
     held form with the offending loop. Move 1's work lands here as one
     loop rather than a search.

  So: one move deleted, one move (5) restated, one move (7) taking the
  weight, and four unchanged. **No completion, no critical pairs, no
  minimal path by a scalar** — chapter 44's refusals stand here as they
  stand at L17.
- **This is why it bounds.** A search over `m` forms is the compiler's own
  cost (L8v); an orbit check on one form is bounded by the form. That is
  the claim, and 51.10 is how it is proved rather than argued.
- **What a section along `e₃` carries, and what pairs the bodies**, is
  ruled in 52.5 (2026-09-17, night): the pairing is the chart's fiber and
  the quotient of its union shapes; a section is the per-frame quotient
  where the whole-fiber quotient refuses, its content the bivectors.

### 51.6 The letters, and that nothing is added

The seventeen already act on `e₃`. Read off `letters.rs` rather than
recalled:

- `SLOT_PLANES_SIX` = `(0,1) (0,2) (0,3) (1,2) (1,3) (2,3)`; quarters are
  slots 1–6 and the (3,4,5) rotors slots 7–12 on those same six planes;
  `SLOT_PLANES_13` = `(0,1) (0,2) (0,3) (1,2)` carries the (5,12,13)
  rotors at slots 13–16; slot 0 is the identity and has no plane.
- The three planes touching `e₃` are `(0,3)`, `(1,3)`, `(2,3)`. Seven
  letters act on them: quarters 3, 5, 6; (3,4,5) rotors 9, 11, 12; and the
  (5,12,13) rotor 15.
- The letters acting on the sensor plane `(0,1)` are 1, 7 and 13, plus the
  identity at 0. **So the language writes today in a four-letter
  sub-alphabet of a seventeen-letter alphabet**, and thirteen letters act
  on planes no spelling path has ever peeled — `spell_peel_on` is called
  at `(PLANE_ROW, PLANE_COL)` and nowhere else.

**Nothing is added.** `CAYLEY_ALPHABET_LEN` stays 17, the relators of 1.2
stay as stated, and no letter changes its rotor. What changes is that
seven letters that were unreachable become reachable, because there is
finally something on `e₃` for them to act on. A22's peel gains planes to
peel on; it does not gain primes.

### 51.7 The tape

The tape's codecs, as ruled 2026-09-17 (evening): a link stays four
fields (16.5) and the chain of a body spanning frames is written as its
placed sections; a support is a list of sites of three coordinates where
it was pairs; a versor serialises thirty-two components where it
serialised sixteen; the frame rides on the pose.

**No version is spent before the recut, and here is why.**
`FORM_TAPE_VERSION` was 9 through the landing. v9's layout is fixed at a
recut, and the recut is a procedure the OPERATOR runs (§10). So this
chapter did not choose a version byte ahead of it and does not write a
migration. It records that the codec change is a recut's business and
that the recut takes it whole: every tape in the tree is rewritten at
once, or none is. A tape carrying two coordinates and a tape carrying
three are not two versions of one format; they are two bases, and 33's
"one migration, then never again" is the rule that applies. The landing's
final commit spends the byte, and the one recut that follows it rewrites
every tape (ruled 2026-09-17). **Spent** (P7, 2026-09-17, night):
`FORM_TAPE_VERSION` is 10 — the three-coordinate supports, the
thirty-two-component versors, the placed sections and the filed zero
(52.3) are its layout — and the recut of epoch 65 is the one that
rewrites every tape.

### 51.8 The court

- **`G` runs on a three-axis body.** The court's re-derivation is
  unchanged in kind: it perceives, it replays, it compares by the algebra.
  It perceives one body instead of `m` pairs, which is strictly less work
  and strictly the same check.
- **`vertices_carry_family` becomes `vertices_carry_frames`** in meaning
  and keeps its name's job: today it asks that every rule vertex speaks
  in every pair of the family. With one body it asks that every rule
  vertex's support meets every FRAME — that the vertex is present along
  the whole of `e₃` and is not a section of some frames only. That is the
  same refusal on a coordinate instead of on a list, and it is the point
  at which a section is told from a rule.
- **`edges_rederive_family` likewise**: an edge transport re-derived per
  pair becomes an edge transport re-derived at each frame, which is the
  same computation indexed by a coordinate.
- Nothing about WHO replays, or how many vantages a ruling needs, moves.
  47.3's witness, arity 2, and the ruling path are untouched.

### 51.9 The economy and the receipts are unchanged

- **The four lanes are unchanged.** 42.6's table assigns `𝒮` placement and
  dilation, `𝒢` the gauge, `𝒯` extent in receipts, `𝒽` the rotor's own
  coordinates. A third BASE coordinate is more `𝒮` and more `𝒽` — a wider
  support and more planes for the rotor — and it is not a fifth lane. Law
  5 is about what the lanes ARE, not how many coordinates the base has.
- **`measure_lanes` is unchanged in kind**: spatial counts laminae where
  support appears or vanishes, gauge counts hue transitions, shell reads
  the boundary cochain. All three read a support and all three take a
  third coordinate without changing what they mean.
- **Receipts are unchanged, and the reason matters**: a receipt records an
  act on the ledger and `𝒯` is extent in receipts. `k` is spatial (51.1),
  so it touches neither. A family occupying three frames does not age
  three times.
- **The door, room, bonds and the mint are unchanged** for the same
  reason: every one of them reads a lane vector, and the lane vectors keep
  their meaning.

### 51.10 The proof

Three claims, in process, with no corpus in the first two:

1. **A family whose rule is one translation along `e₃`.** Construct a
   family of three pairs where each output is the input translated by a
   fixed vector. As one body this is a body with a translational symmetry
   along `e₃`; extraction reads it as ONE orbit whose holonomy is that
   translation, and the trace shows no correspondence pass ran — move 1
   is not merely fast, it is absent.
2. **The same address on two courts.** Two kernels of distinct identity,
   no shared runtime memory, each perceiving the same family as one body
   and reaching the same form address and the same standing. This is
   50.9's intelligibility assertion on a three-axis body and it is what
   makes the coordinate content rather than an implementation.
3. **`0607ce86.json` returns under the machine stroke.** Three train pairs
   at 21×22; it does not complete `extract_rule_with` in 900 s today, and
   the twelve tasks before it complete in 6 s together (L8v, re-measured
   at 250feeb). It is the reproduction of the search's cost, so it is the
   proof that the search is gone. The line to beat is the machine stroke,
   and the machine stroke is not comparable across machines — see the
   note in 51.11.

### 51.11 What is NOT in this draft

- **The third SPATIAL axis.** 36.2 names one; no corpus carries one; a
  base coordinate with no datum behind it is an invented value (rule 11).
  `e₃` here carries the frame index, which `task.train` already supplies.
- **Any datum not already in `task.train`.** No metadata, no task name, no
  ordering hint, no annotation. If the corpus does not write it, the
  engine does not read it.
- **Any change to the seventeen** (51.6).
- **The version byte and the migration** (51.7): a recut's business.
- **A machine-stroke number.** `reserve_max` is
  `((cores × (1 + MemAvailable_GiB)).max(16) / 8) × 8` read at boot, so
  the stroke depends on the machine AND on what else that machine was
  doing when the process started. Measured 2026-09-11: the same corpus at
  the same commit read `extracted 9` on a quiet box and `extracted 4` in
  a run begun immediately after a release build. 51.10's third claim is
  "returns", not "returns in `n`".

**Binding** (what the ruling would touch, named so the cost is visible
before it is paid, and NOT written): `transducer/family/perceive.rs`
(`Painted`, `Body`, `perceive`), `transducer/blade` (`shape_of`, `moduli`,
`components`, `adjacent_ring`), `transducer/cga` (`Mv` to `Cl(4,1)`),
`transducer/element/sensor.rs` (`carry_center`, `site_of`),
`transducer/sentence/tape.rs` (the codecs), `transducer/family/extract.rs`,
`percept.rs` and `pair.rs` (the seven moves), `court/verdict/body.rs`
(`vertices_carry_family`, `edges_rederive_family`), and every fixture that

# Part XII — Inverse derivation

Ruled 2026-09-17, night, on the operator's word, against 4a8f10c and the
recut of epoch 64. Carried from Parts X and XI: a word vertex carries its
derivation and re-derives its rotor; an orbit's holonomy is content; the
family is one body on `(r, c, k)`. This part rules how a versor is derived
from its own bivector — exactly, in either direction, by the algebra's
products and nothing else — and what that retires: the finite-order gates
of 50.3, A17 and 23.1, and the search that extraction still ran.

## 52. The Cayley chart: a versor's derivation is its bivector (ruled 2026-09-17)

### 52.1 The chart

Every even versor `V` of `Cl(4,1)(ℚ)` with a scalar part is, projectively
(1.5),

```
V ≡ 1 + B + ½ B∧B,        B = ⟨V⟩₂ / ⟨V⟩₀
```

`B` is the **Cayley bivector** of `V`: the element of `Λ²(ℚ^{4,1})` the
versor is derived from. The derivation is those two lines, read in either
direction — the bivector off the versor by grade, the versor off the
bivector by one outer square — with no exponential, no logarithm, no root,
no angle and no matrix (law 11, rule 16). The grade-4 part of a versor is
not a coordinate of it: `⟨V⟩₄ = ⟨V⟩₂∧⟨V⟩₂ / (2⟨V⟩₀)` is what `V Ṽ ∈ ℚ`
forces, so an even element whose grade-4 part is anything else is not a
versor, and the chart refuses it rather than reading a bivector off it.
The chart is projective — `V` and `λV` have one bivector — which is why
the bivector is content and never a spelling (1.5, A4).

What the bivector is on each kind of plane, read off the versors the tree
already writes and never asserted:

- on an elliptic plane, `V = a + b·e_ie_j` has `B = (b/a)·e_ie_j`: the
  quarter turn `1 + e₁e₂` reads `1`, the `(3,4,5)` rotor `2 + e₁e₂` reads
  `1/2`, the `(5,12,13)` rotor reads `1/5`; `b/a` is the tangent of the
  half-angle of the rotation `V` induces, and no tangent is ever taken;
- on the dilation plane `E = e_o∧e_∞`, the dilator by `ρ` reads `B = β·E`
  with `β = (ρ − 1)/(ρ + 1)`, and `ρ = (1 + β)/(1 − β)`: the dilation by
  two is `β = 1/3`. This is the rapidity chart of 51.2's asserted reading,
  `β = tanh(ζ/2)`, with no hyperbolic function in it;
- on a translation plane `e_i∧e_∞`, the translator by `d` reads
  `B = −½ d∧e_∞`, nilpotent, `B∧B = 0`, `V = 1 + B` exactly; a
  transversion `e_i∧e_o` reads the same way.

**Refusals, which are the whole boundary of the chart.** `⟨V⟩₀ = 0`: a half
turn, the involution of order two, and every odd versor — a reflection is
a vector and is its own derivation (52.4). An even element that is not a
versor. A bivector whose `1 + B + ½B∧B` has no weight: `V Ṽ = 0`, the
parameter of a dilation plane at `β = ±1`, the light cone itself. Each is
a refusal under rule 11 and none is interpolated across.

The class invariants of 15.3 are read on the versor as they are; the
bivector is the derivation, not the key, and nothing keyed by a class key
today is rekeyed by this chapter.

### 52.2 One plane adds; planes multiply; a 2-cell is `F = 0`

On one plane the chart composes by a rational addition law, and the law
is read off the geometric product rather than computed: on an elliptic
plane `(1 + t₁P)(1 + t₂P) ≡ 1 + t₃P` with `t₃ = (t₁ + t₂)/(1 − t₁t₂)`; on
the dilation plane `β₃ = (β₁ + β₂)/(1 + β₁β₂)`, so the dilation by two
composed with the dilation by three reads `(1/3 + 1/2)/(1 + 1/6) = 5/7`,
which is the dilation by six; on a translation plane `d₃ = d₁ + d₂`. The
flux on ONE plane is exactly additive in the parameter, and that is the
only place it is: across planes that do not commute the bivectors do not
add, the ordered product is the whole statement, and a rule that added
bivectors across planes would be the first-order approximation rule 11
refuses.

A 2-cell of a form — an orbit of faces — is closed when the ordered product
of its face holonomies around it is the identity: `F = 0` on that cell.
That is the discrete non-abelian Stokes theorem, it is what
`form_loops_replay` reads, and it is not `div ⋆F = 0`, which is a source
condition and admits curvature. A cell whose product is not the identity
carries an obstruction, and 52.3 says what the obstruction is.

### 52.3 An orbit's obstruction is its bivector; a period is a reading

An orbit whose edge holonomy (50.3) is a versor `V ≢ 1` has as its
obstruction the Cayley bivector `B` of `V`: 12.6's blade decomposition of
the canonical holonomy versor, written projectively so that it is content
and not a spelling. Its placement residue and its dilation residue are
the `e_i∧e_∞` and `e_o∧e_∞` components of `B`; its discharge on its own
plane is the inverse parameter `−B`; and the axis I6 opens over it
(16.20) is seeded by the orbit's holonomy versor as it is, with `B` as the
coordinate the seed re-derives.

**The finite-order gates are retired.** 50.3 as ruled 2026-09-09 filed a
finite holonomy as torsion `(σ, ℓ)` and held an infinite one; 23.1 step 4
refused a face whose edge word has infinite order and step 5 refused a
orbit of infinite order however it was filed; A17 called an infinite-order
class a demand. Read against the chart, a finite order is the case where
the flow on one plane returns — a periodic angle — and the gate that
refused every other holonomy was trigonometry: it forced the hyperbolic
flow of 51.2's asserted algebra, and every Pythagorean rotor, into a
compact order they do not have. Ruled:

1. **An orbit of any order is filed under its class key** (15.4): finite at
   its period `ℓ`, infinite at period `0`, which is A19's spelling of
   infinite order on the class ledger already. The tape admits the filed
   zero; the codec's refusal of `0` as malformed is retired. S9.13's reach
   (`fibre_volume`) counts finite periods only: an infinite class
   condenses no members and is priced nowhere as a reach.
2. **The court replays a filed orbit of any order by one reading**: the
   identity, or an opened axis that re-derives, or filed under its class at
   the period the court re-derives — `Rotor::order` (15.3) reading
   infinite is the period `0`. A face whose edge word has infinite order is
   a face; its transport re-derives on the family as any other (23.1 step
   4, `edges_rederive_family`), and that re-derivation is the exactness
   that remains.
3. **What still refuses**: a holonomy that is not a versor, which has no
   class; a filed period that does not re-derive; a seed that is not the
   re-walked orbit's own; and a form whose orbit is neither identity, nor
   filed, nor opened is held and not spoken — valid, not closed, as 50.1
   step 2 says.
4. **The voice files by the same rule.** `edge_coheres`, `is_cauterized`
   and the pivot's filing after `NoneDischarged` read an order as a
   period to file, never as a gate. An orbit of infinite order whose
   holonomy neither the seventeen nor the held generators spell still
   speaks its `Standing` demand (37.7, N4): that is the language's want
   of a generator, and it rides beside the filing, not instead of it. The
   filing line writes `∞` where the period is `0`.
5. **A congruence on a simplex stays finite.** The cover's `classify`
   files `Congruent` at a finite period because a congruence is witnessed
   by A17 step 2's walk of the fibre returning at `ℓ`, and an infinite
   class returns nowhere; a flat transition of infinite order is a
   standing `Class` with its bivector as content — not refused, and not a
   congruence. The element's torsion cycles (`TorsionCycle`, the witness
   walk) are untouched by this ruling.

The amendments in place: 50.3's last bullet, A17's last paragraph, 23.1
steps 4 and 5, 34.3's filing line.

### 52.4 The letters of order two, and where the sphere is

A reflection is a vector `u` of `Cl(4,1)(ℚ)`: a rational plane, or a
rational sphere — A4's dual sphere — acting by `u x u`. It is odd, of
order two, and its derivation is itself, the mirror; the chart refuses it,
and that is not a gap. A rotor is a product of two reflections and every
versor a product of at most five (Cartan–Dieudonné holds over ℚ), so the
two carriers together — mirrors and bivectors — reach every element of the
group. The involution is the ONE finite order the alphabet keeps: a mirror
transported by a word, `w σ rev(w)`, is a reflection; a pair of them is a
rotor whose bivector 52.1 reads; a rotor's period, where it has one, is
15.3's reading and never a condition on anything.

The sphere is not built from a radius or an angle. The base is the null
cone of `ℝ^{4,1}` read projectively: a base point is a null vector `X`,
`X·X = 0` (`cga::point`), and the pencil `aX + b·e_∞` is every sphere about
it — `X` itself at `b = 0`, the horizon `e_∞` at `a = 0`, the squared
radius the ratio `b/a` and never a number of its own. A point lies on a
sphere when `X·S = 0`; four points span their sphere as `A∧B∧C∧D`; two
spheres meet in the circle `S₁∧S₂`; a plane is a sphere through `e_∞`; the
dilation about `X` is the boost on `X∧e_∞` whose parameter is 52.1's `β`,
its orbits the rays out of `X` and its level sets the pencil. Nothing here
squares a coordinate, takes a root or measures an angle, and the sensor's
lattice is the set of rational null vectors a hypha reads at intake and
writes at speech (law 11), and nothing between.

### 52.5 The family's one form is a quotient (P4 and P5 ruled)

51.4 and 51.5 stand. This section rules the two readings P4 asked about
and names what replaces the search, so that nothing in extraction is a
correspondence, a candidate list or a nearest match (50.2).

1. **Perceive once, on the stack.** The train inputs at frames `0..n−1`
   are one grid of three coordinates and so are the train outputs; the
   test input is the open section at frame `n`, perceived with the inputs
   so that its bodies are keyed on the same charts. Bodies of one hue
   connect by 6-adjacency (51.3); every axis of a body's moduli is
   invariant under every versor the sensor carries a lamina by, so a body
   and its image are ONE chart.
2. **Pairing is the chart's fiber, never a search.** For each chart
   present, the input fiber and the output fiber — every body of that
   chart on each side, all frames — and the quotient `V =
   versor_between` of the union of the input fiber's shapes and the union
   of the output fiber's, exact or refused. Where it exists it is the
   vertex: one versor carrying every instance in every frame onto its
   image. That is what "a rule that holds in every pair" means as an
   algebraic fact rather than as a correspondence across pair forms; the
   instances need no matching, because the versor lands each on its image
   or is refused, and the frame coordinate rides on the pose.
3. **A section along `e₃` is the case the whole-fiber quotient refuses and
   the per-frame quotient does not**: the same read on the fiber
   restricted to frame `k` gives `V_k`, one per frame, recorded in
   `Form.sections` at that vertex, and the section's content is the
   bivectors `B_k`. This is the first of P4's two readings — a pair's input
   bodies at `k` carried onto its output bodies — and it is the one ruled;
   the second, the coboundary chain at pose `k`, is a chain and never a
   word (50.6). Moves 4, 5 and 6 — rebasing, unfolding, contact — read the
   relation among the `B_k`, and move 7 judges. A chart whose per-frame
   quotient also refuses is 50.5's demand — `Source` with the fiber's
   multiplicity, `Creation`, `TopologicalDeformation` — held, never chosen
   (rule 15).
4. **Faces, orbits, gluing.** Faces are 50.3's, on the union shapes of the
   two vertices' fibers; orbits are filed by 52.3; gluing (move 3) is
   unchanged. Move 1 does not exist: `extract/1 correspondence`, the
   matching by transport class, and `pair_form` per pair are deleted
   rather than kept, and the memo holds one form per task.
5. **Speaking is filling the open section.** The test frame's bodies by
   chart, carried by their chart's vertex — the whole-fiber versor, or the
   section's relation extended to frame `n` by moves 4–6 — through
   `carry_lamina`, exact or refused; the remainder is what no vertex
   carries, and it rides as the demands of 50.5.
6. **The derivation of a vertex is unchanged in kind** (50.2 step 2): the
   generators it factored through and the residue A22 peels; the vertex's
   versor is the quotient, its bivector is 52.1's reading of it, and the
   peel gains nothing to search because a quotient is one element.

The observable is 51.10's three proofs and no correspondence pass in any
trace. A draft of a one-form carrier standing untracked in the tree
(`family/family_form.rs`) is not this ruling's and is not read by it.

**As landed (2026-09-17, night), five readings the landing fixed and the
operator reads with the rest:**

1. **The fiber's unit is the section**: a component of one hue within a
   frame, standing at its frame (`perceive_at`). A body stacked along `e₃`
   by 51.3's 6-adjacency has a chart that depends on its extent there, so a
   vertex keyed by it finds nothing on a frame perceived alone — which is
   what speech and the court do. The family is still perceived once, frame
   by frame, and 51.3's stacked body stays the reading of periodicity
   (move 5), not of the pairing.
2. **The quotient is read in the frame's own coordinates**: a frame's
   sections shifted to `k = 0` before the versor is measured, so "the same
   versor on every frame" is the exact statement that the rule holds on
   every pair, and the vertex's carriage is what any frame perceived alone
   reads. Frames reading another versor, or another hue map, are the
   frames the vertex is not claimed on (18.2).
3. **The member's section is keyed by class, chart, address and
   carriage**, because two vertices of one class can stand on one chart —
   a cover's pieces at two frames, a chart whose frames read two versors —
   and each is claimed on its own frames; two members whose every
   coordinate agrees are one action and are claimed alike.
4. **The ring answers the peel's demands only** (37.7): a `Source`,
   `Creation` or deformation measured as one versor between its links is a
   word that pairs two instances of one chart behind the chart's back,
   which the court refuses for not carrying every body of the chart.
5. **A contact word is minted only where it orbits** (22): a class whose
   placement varies with a constant ring but whose word has the identity
   rotor, or returns `NoOrbit` on a frame, stays the sections the percept
   filed; a contact minted re-derives its star faces, since a face left
   with the placement the vertex no longer has is refused as a face that
   does not re-derive (23.1 step 4). An edge face claims the frames its
   edge re-derives on and no other.
6. **Succession along $e₃$ is a non-linear coordinate move** (ruled
   2026-09-18): traversal across frames is not a linear $k \to k+1$ scan,
   but a keyed read of the body's occupied sections ($k \to k + \{\text{next
   coordinate}\}$), which may skip, repeat or reorder in ℤ. The connection
   $\gamma_{ij}$ between successive occupied frames carries the full
   multi-axial `Carriage { v, sigma }` (spatial versor and gauge
   permutation).
7. **Lanes are multi-axial coordinate spaces, never scalar counts** (ruled
   2026-09-18): no scalars on lanes. $\{S, G, T, H\}$ is a 4-dimensional
   rotor coordinate space (`lane_charts_of`). Expansion velocity and
   recursion are contained by circuit orbit-back (`Orbit::period`),
   projective ray singularity condensation ($\nabla(V) \cup -\nabla(V)$
   congruence via $V \sim -V$), and stratum depth bounds.
8. **The ambient connection of a deformation lives on the family bundle, not the defect chart** (ruled
   2026-09-18): a demand is a topological singularity where moduli change, so its chart does not persist across frames by construction. Monodromy of candidate $V$ is evaluated against the family bundle's carried charts: $M^c = \prod (\gamma^c)^{-1} V \gamma^c$. Order is evaluated via `Rotor::order()` (`Finite(1)` flat, `Finite(\ell \ge 2)` filed as torsion, `Infinite` rupture). A candidate stands on its surviving sub-cover and dissolves only when every measured connection ruptures to `Infinite`.

## 53. The cut: a scene is covered before it is one form (ruled 2026-09-19)

Ruled on the operator's word, on the coordinator's console, against
114b307 and the auditor's reading of the same day. Carried from Part XI: the
family is one body on `(r, c, k)`; from 52.5: its form is a quotient per
chart; from rule 17: a reader writes a coordinate or returns a demand. What
this chapter adds is the organ that stood between a scene and its form in
the parent tree and never crossed the fork: a 25×25 scene arriving at
extraction as one form of 712 vertices is not a cost to optimise but the
absence of a cut. 948 of the 1 120 corpus tasks have a side that was above
the parent's floor; 850 present a uniform separator row or column in every
input; 102 are integer frame ratios on every pair. The Stage 16 gap reads
differently under this: fifteen per cent of a 25×25 scene is a form that
cannot close, and fifteen per cent of one 4×5 chart of it can.

### 53.1 The scene cover

A scene is covered by charts under a reading before it is perceived as one
form. A **chart** is the atlas's chart (the vocabulary, NM1): one local
view of the cover with a transition on every overlap; on the substrate
it is NAMED by its support written out (A21, `pieces::piece_key`) —
coordinates of which every prefix is a coarser stratum, and never a
bounding box carried past the sensor boundary (law 11, checklist (f′)).
The support names the chart; it is not the chart. A **cover** is a `Keyed` of charts under
one reading. The family is then the ordinary family of each chart — the
train inputs and outputs restricted to it, frame by frame — extracted as
52.5 extracts any family, and the charts' forms are recomposed on the Čech
complex of the cover by the alternating coboundary (13.9, `cech::`), which
is the recomposition and needs no written map.

**The recursion ends at an identity of coordinates.** A chart is itself a
scene and is covered again; the recursion ends where the cover's key is the
scene's own key, one chart equal to the whole. There is no floor and no
constant: `FRAGMENT_FLOOR = 9` is refused by rule 5 and is not replaced by
a count of charts (rule 2). The routing floor — how much of a scene one
voice takes — is the voice's drawable room (23.8) and is read from the
book, never from the geometry.

**No reading is chosen** (rules 4, 15). Every reading of the roster is
tried in roster order; every cover that closes is kept; covers that
close and are incomparable are held as a vortex until a court replay or a
perception collapses them. The first cover that addresses a demand is a
choice by arrival and is refused.

### 53.2 The readings

A **reading** is a way the sensor plane is cut into charts: Bands (the
uniform separator rows and columns every input carries), Components,
Lines, RingShells, PeriodCells (the spectrum cut, integer frame ratios),
HueStrata. The roster is governed as the letters are (law 6 as amended):
fixed, grown only by a court receipt on a probe — a reading whose first
cover on the corpus closes a family no other reading closes — and never by
a voice or a commit. Bands enters first because it is deducible in one
pass over the inputs; each further reading enters behind its own receipt
(rows K1, K4, K5).

**A reading has its own coordinate system, and a chart is named in it**
(ruled 2026-09-19, on the corpus reading that a separator shared by every
input of a family cuts 156 of 1 000 tasks while 566 tasks have inputs of
differing frames and no shared site set at all). Bands is read **per
frame**: each input's own separator rows and columns are its band
lattice, and a chart is named by its coordinate in that lattice — its band
index along `r` and along `c` — never by its support. The support at a
frame is the section that coordinate reads there (51.4: the fiber's unit
is the section), so charts correspond across frames by coordinate and
never by a search over supports, and a frame whose lattice does not reach
a coordinate holds that chart's fiber empty there: a section along `e₃`
(52.5 item 3), not a refusal. A family whose inputs carry no separator has
one chart under Bands, itself, and is cut by another reading or not at
all; `1d0a4b61` is such a family, and its cut is PeriodCells' or
Components' (K5), not Bands'.

### 53.3 A demand may name a stratum

50.5 gains one kind: `Demand::Chart { reading, chart, links }`, a chart
under a reading with no rule. It is keyed by (reading, chart key) and
deduplicated by that key, never by a count, so a hundred scenes blocked on
one chart class under one reading are one demand. It is the first demand
the registry may dispatch as a **sub-problem**: a voice that refuses a
chart hands it back as this demand; another mind may take it and the
market prices it (24.3, 42.6). The five algebraic kinds of 50.5 stand
unchanged; a `Demand::Chart` is spatial in the sense of a key on the
sensor's stratum and in no other.

### 53.4 The quantified citation

A `Glued` vertex cites a form **over a fiber** — every chart of a reading
on which the cited form closes — and its placement is re-derived at each
chart it is spoken on from that chart's own key and the cited form's
frame, never stored once for one placement (law 12). The single-placement
citation `Form::glue(s, addr, placement, magnitude)` is the degenerate case
of one chart, and the tape carries no per-chart placement. This is what
makes a chart's rule general enough to be worth extracting: one citation
speaks every chart of a banded scene.

### 53.6 A form's vertices are its charts, never its pieces (ruled 2026-09-19)

On the operator's word, against the fleet reading at dac0b89: a 25×25
scene of three frames arriving as a form of 2 899 vertices, 12 011 faces
and 971 loops is not a large form, it is an enumeration of the scene's
bodies wearing a form's carriers, and every reader that walks it is
brute force by construction. Nothing a perception produces may be
proportional to the laminae or the pieces of a scene; it is proportional
to the scene's charts.

A form's word vertices are the quotients of its charts (52.5 item 2), one
per transport class acting on the charts it acts on, and its demand
vertices are one per (kind, chart) (50.5). A cover's pieces are not
vertices of the family's form. A cover is what one chart's quotient
refused, and it is carried as **one vertex per cover** — the deformation
on that chart — whose nerve, meets and filed classes are the cover's own
content, held below that vertex in the chart's fiber and reached by key
when the form is spoken or replayed. The orbits the form walks are the
orbits among its charts; the orbits among a cover's pieces are classified
once inside the cover and filed as torsion on the cover's vertex (50.8
case 3), never lifted to the form. Pieces correspond across frames by the
chart coordinate along `e₃` (51.3, 52.5 reading 1), so a piece at frame k
and its image at frame k+1 are one fiber, not two vertices.

**The carrier is unchanged and the tape is unbroken.** A `Vertex::Word`
already is what this section names: one transport class, acting on the
charts it acts on through its `acts` fiber, one member per chart (D7).
The ruling lands in the percept and nowhere else: a cover's carried pieces
are grouped by transport class exactly as a chart's quotients are, one
Word vertex per class with one member per chart the class carries a piece
on; a chart on which one class carries two pieces by two different
carriages is 50.5's multiplicity, a `Source` demand on that chart, never
two vertices and never two members; the cover's meets are faces between
those members through the incidence the form already builds on supports;
the orbits among pieces are classified inside the cover and filed as
torsion by class, where the form already files them. No vertex kind, no
tape field and no address of an unchanged form moves; the version byte
stays K3's.

The bound is therefore structural and is written as a test, not a limit:
the number of word vertices of a form does not exceed the number of
charts of the scene times the number of readings that cut it, plus one
vertex per cover and one per demand kind and chart. On `1d0a4b61` that is
tens, and a form of thousands is refused by the claim. This is P7's
ruling 1 landed at the form rather than at the index, and it is what the
cut of 53.1 cuts.

### 53.5 Binding

```
family/scene.rs                 the scene cover: charts by support key, the cover as Keyed, the readings, the recursion's identity end (53.1, 53.2)
family/extract.rs, percept.rs   extraction per chart; the charts' forms recomposed on the Čech complex (53.1)
cech/                           the nerve of the cover and the alternating coboundary as the recomposition (53.1, K4)
sentence/demand.rs, tape.rs     Demand::Chart, its key, the version byte spent in the final commit (53.3)
server/registry.rs              the sub-problem dispatched and priced (53.3)
sentence/form/carrier.rs, chart.rs, family/speak.rs, court/verdict/replay.rs   the quantified citation and its re-derived placement (53.4)
```
