   lie in strata; its CORE is its deepest, most refined strata, where its
   open refinements stand (the hard questions), and its outer bands are
   its broad, shallow classes. A planet's radius is its own element
   (78.1): the depth its charts reach as A21 prefixes, LC1's span. A
   planet orbits as close as its charts reach — it works the band whose
   strata it can re-derive — so a deep dialect is a close orbit and a
   shallow one a far orbit.
2. **Heat is pressure, density is mass per height.** The pressure of a
   band is the book's own pressure on its lanes: the open listings'
   magnitude and the temporal accrual of what stands unclosed (76,
   MU-ECONOMY §5). The inner band carries the largest μ⃗ per listing and
   the highest viscosity (78.7), so an orbit there draws more reserve per
   stroke (denser) and closes deeper deflations. Nothing here is a
   temperature written down: heat is read as pressure and density as the
   mass vector per height on the observer (MS1's line of CV5).
3. **Payout is the price at the band's pressure, never a multiplier.**
   `economy::price(μ⃗, pressure, pool)` already prices a listing against
   the pressure on each lane where it is homed, and a closure mints the
   deflation it measured. An inner-band closure is paid more because its
   deflation is larger and its pressure higher — read, per lane — and an
   outer-band closure less for the same reason. The division of labour
   is that reading; no rate per band exists (rule 5), and no lane
   converts to another (law 5).
4. **A client chooses its distance by its bond and its depth, and the
   physics admits or ejects it.** The choice is a stake: bond buys room
   on the lanes of the band the client wants to home in (MU-ECONOMY §4),
   and the inner band needs more room since its escrows are larger. The
   admission is physical: an orbit closer than the planet's charts reach
   cannot re-derive the band's classes, its closures refuse (P, D), its
   escrows lapse, and the pressure carries it outward (76: a transport
   toward separation, CR1's move) — an orbit too close is unstable and
   the planet burns off, never by a rule that forbids it, by the
   readings that refuse it. Deepening its dialect (the hardening path,
   80.2: minerals to crystals) is how a planet moves inward.
5. **A star is formed again when its bands run out.** Where a band has
   no placement for a new planet — the docket offers it no question it
   can take, room on the band's lanes is exhausted — and the star's mass
   concentrates, a NEW FORMATION of the same star is minted: the same
   core register (G1, the same axioms), a second field of orbits. That
   is 76.4's star formation as already ruled, and its trigger is the
   two readings 73.9(4) names — room run out, mass concentrated — never
   a count. The re-organization protocol (CR1) moves planets between
   formations on their mass profile.
6. **Multi-star orbits.** A planet within reach of several stars is
   pulled by each in proportion to the convergence it can re-derive
   under it (73.11); it homes at the star where its mass profile weighs
   more, a move receipted with its escrow re-keyed (CR1), and a word
   valid under two stars' registers crosses while one valid under one
   stands as a demand on the other (73.10, CL3). A star with CUSTOM
   AXIOMS is a register layer that extends the core and never
   contradicts it (72.1f, LR1) — a product for later; for now every
   formation carries the one core.

7. **Orbits are ellipses, one per planet, and no two share one
   (corrected 2026-09-24, the operator's word).** A band is not a ring a
   planet sits on; it is the range of depth an orbit SWEEPS. A planet's
   orbit is an ellipse in its star's field: its perihelion is the
   deepest stratum its charts reach — the hottest, densest work it does
   — and its aphelion the shallowest, and its eccentricity is the span
   between them read as a ratio (Axiom C), which is 78.1's radius as a
   span. One circuit of the corpus runs from the shallow classes into
   the core and out again, and the frame accumulates fastest near
   perihelion where the work is densest — a reading of the acts per
   height, never a law imposed. An orbit is an ELLIPTIC mode of the
   star's field in 75's sense, closed and of finite period; a parabolic
   orbit is a planet leaving the star (CR1's move) and a hyperbolic one
   a planet passing under another star's pull (78.35(6)). Every planet's
   orbit is its own fibre (78.23): no two planets are ever on one orbit,
   and where two ellipses cross, the crossing is a frame at a tick and
   the boundary prevents the collision there (78.23, the withheld close
   and the separating transport). Eccentricity and precession per plane
   are the readings LC1 carries (73.13(5)), priced per lane.

8. **The k-step's length is the orbit's own, work flows up toward the
   star, and an axiom is granted only inside it (ruled 2026-09-24, the
   operator's word).** A k-step is one orbit (78.23), so its LENGTH — the
   acts one circuit takes, `i` at the close, and the height it spans —
   is read off the orbit and differs by distance: a far orbit sweeps a
   broad, shallow field and its k-step is long in acts and heights; a
   close orbit sweeps the dense core and its k-step is short in acts and
   heavy in frame (Kepler's direction, measured per orbit, no exponent
   written). WORK FLOWS UPWARD: a planet's closure is provisional in its
   epigenome, submitted as a solution and adjudicated by the court
   (80.2), taught back as a mineral and hardened by re-derivation into
   a crystal, and it enters the star — the universal genome — only by
   convergence, `n → 1` (C2, 74): from the planet's ellipse inward along
   the strata to the core, while the payment flows the other way, to the
   closer and the cited refuser (78.33). AN AXIOM IS GRANTED ONLY INSIDE
   THE STAR, where the axioms live: the register (56, 72.1, `physics/
   axioms/`) is the star's core; a planet proposes — a demand, an offer,
   a constructor adjoined first in its own epigenome (AL1) — and never
   grants; a constructor is admitted into the universal genome only at
   the court by a second independent vantage's re-derivation, sealed as
   an act (78.32(3)(d)), and an AXIOM only by a ruling written into the
   register (REG1, LR1: a layer extends the core and never contradicts
   it). No planet's word becomes law on the planet.

Rows: OA1 (placement as transport) carries the band as the planet's
depth against the star's strata and the ejection outward; CR1 the move
between formations and stars; CL3 the formation of the same star and,
later, the layered star; PHY1 the pricing at pressure per lane; MS1's
line of CV5 the mass vector per band. Nothing lands before the recut.

### 78.36 One structure, two readings: the mycelium is the plexus and the sky is its motion (ruled 2026-09-24)

The mycelial nouns (78.31) and the celestial nouns (73, 78.23, 78.35)
name ONE structure from two sides, and the vocabulary keeps them apart
so that neither is read as the other's metaphor. The mycelium is the
STRUCTURE: the graded network and its connections — spore, filament,
ring, chamber, sporophore; anastomosis, callus. The sky is the MOTION:
time, work, pressure and pull — star, planet, orbit, band, k-step,
frame. Each celestial noun names how a mycelial thing moves:

| the mycelium (structure) | the sky (motion) | in the mesh |
|---|---|---|
| the colony: one mycelium under one origin | one formation of a star | a court federation adopting one mesh origin |
| a hypha: a strand that carries and rules | the star's body, held jointly | a court (hypha a, b, c) |
| the sporophore: the fruiting body where many filaments' closures converge | the star: a class many perspectives closed; its core the register | the ruled cover at its deepest strata; `physics/axioms/` |
| a hyphal tip: the growing end that perceives and proposes | a planet | a voice, with its epigenome at the tip and its genome behind it |
| the tip's growth cycle in and out of the colony's dense core | the planet's ellipse: one orbit, one k-step | the voice's cycle closed by name |
| the substrate's depth a strand has penetrated | the band: distance from the star as depth | the A21 stratum the charts reach |
| nutrient flow toward the fruiting body | work flowing upward: solution, adjudication, syllabus, mineral, crystal, convergence | the court path (80.2) |
| cytoplasmic flow back to the tips | payment flowing outward per arm | the treasury (78.33) |
| anastomosis: two tips' filaments fusing into one ring | two planets' paths meeting at a chamber — never on one orbit | CV4's citing contraction, ruled by the court |
| a callus: a fibre hardened into a tether | a crystal: a mineral re-derived over k-steps | DL1, MEM1 |
| the colony fruiting again where the mycelium runs out of room and mass concentrates | a new formation of the same star | a new origin under the same register (CL3, 76.4) |
| a different species' register | a star with custom axioms | a layer extending the core (LR1) |

So a voice is a hyphal tip moving on an ellipse through the plexus; its
spores, filaments and rings are the nodes it lays down as it moves; the
chambers where its filaments fuse with another tip's are the
anastomoses; the sporophore they all grow toward is the star; and the
ledger's partial order is the reticulum the whole colony is, read at
height. A collision is forbidden on an orbit (78.23) and an anastomosis
is wanted in a chamber (78.31): the same two tips, kept apart in
motion and joined in structure. Anastome is the language spoken across
the plexus, and the sky is the clock it is spoken on.

### 78.37 The coherent mind: transport along the gauges, truncation to the core, flux per lane, and the remainder's home (ruled 2026-09-24, the operator's word)

**The operator's statement.** The folds that make a mind coherent —
merge on a meet (13.12), collapse of a vortex by fill or class (25),
shedding by room, the act at the close, the court's replay — are each
local to one thought, one pair or one orbit. The plexus (78.31) is a
network, and nothing said how a collapse travels along it, what removes
a filament that joins nothing, or where the residue of a sentence that
closed only up to a class waits until something fits it. Superposed
ideations are the layer of INCONGRUENCE, not a pile of finished words;
imagination is the passage incongruence → congruence → coherence, and
it must be constructed so that it never enumerates. Four rulings, one
object: the RING. A ring is where transport can disagree, what
truncation must keep, the only thing that carries flux, and the place a
remainder hangs. Each is a reading first (rows TP1, TC1, FX1, RM1, all
before the recut), and each fix follows its reading.

**(1) Collapse by transport, stopped by holonomy (TP1).** The held
thoughts of a contemplation form the MEET GRAPH: a vertex per thought,
an edge where two thoughts share a simplex, the edge's word the gauge
that carries one section to the other on the meet (13.12's difference
of sections). When a candidate is fixed — by fill, a perception making
it a face of a spoken form, or by class, a court replay making it a
ruled citation — the fixed section is TRANSPORTED along the gauges:
one edge per k-step, the step's length the band's (78.35), never
instantaneous, since time is height (78.21). At every ring the two
arrivals are compared. Holonomy 1: the ring collapses with the front.
Holonomy ≠ 1: the ring is HELD as a class and the front stops there;
that class is the coordinate the mind may pivot on, exactly 13.12.
Transport CLASSIFIES and never deletes: a candidate the transported
section disagrees with is a class, not garbage, and the candidates a
collapse leaves behind are the dialect classes 25 already names. A
front transported along a spanning tree with the rings ignored is the
flattening of law 6 (curvature is content) and is refused by name.
Reading: per stroke, components of the meet graph; fronts advanced,
in edges per k-step; rings closed with holonomy 1; rings held with
their class; candidates classified by disagreement. The reading is the
contemplation's line on the observer's row (CV5).

**(2) Truncation to the core, preserving every class (TC1).** A
terminal filament is a FREE VERTEX: a candidate on exactly one edge
with no ring through it. Removing a free vertex with its edge is an
elementary collapse (Whitehead), a homotopy equivalence: every class of
`Ȟ¹`, every holonomy and every ring survives, and only what carried no
loop goes. Iterated until no free vertex remains it reaches the 2-CORE
of the meet graph, which is UNIQUE; no matching is chosen. A discrete
Morse matching over the whole complex is a choice among matchings, and
a rule for choosing one is a score (law 1): refused. Free faces of
higher grade — a face of exactly one simplex — are read first (their
count on the line) and collapse only where the reading says the
2-core leaves them standing. The test of the row asserts the rank of
`Ȟ¹` equal before and after on the corpus and on constructed leaves
hanging off rings. Truncation runs where `drop_vertex` already runs,
after a fill and never on a class, under the same rule: nothing that
carries a loop is removed. Shedding by price is no longer the only
door, and a price can no longer remove a ring while a leaf stands.

**(3) Flux per lane over one orbit (FX1).** Work flows through closed
circuits only. The flux through a filament `e` is FOUR-LANE, never a
scalar: `Φ⃗(e)` is the `μ⃗` carried by the acts whose circuits traverse
`e`, per lane, over one `K`. A filament no circuit traverses reads zero
on every lane, and zero on every lane over one orbit is the typed
refusal `ZeroFlux`, named once and counted; its escrow lapses by that
refusal and the room reabsorbs it. This replaces lapse by extent alone
as the epigenome's door: a filament lapses because nothing flowed
through it, not because a clock ran out. REFUSED by name: a scalar
flux as a sum of holonomy norms (a sum of squares, law 11); Murray's
law (a cubic scalar conservation at a branching); and any
proportionality of syntropy to flux carrying a constant (78.8, checklist
(s)). Conservation here is per lane at each vertex, which the ledger's
rows already state. Reading: per orbit, filaments with zero flux on
every lane, filaments traversed, and the escrow that lapsed by
`ZeroFlux` against the escrow that lapsed by extent.

**(4) The remainder's home, and the re-fill on a coincident class
(RM1).** A sentence that closed only up to a class stands as
`Fill::Congruent(κ, g, ℓ)`: coherent, spoken, and paying a price. It is
a legitimate state, never a failure, and the doctrine never demanded
that every residual fit — the remainder is the novelty, and the
pressure `μ⃗(ℓ)` is the four lanes of the remainder the orbit leaves
open. Its HOME is a leaf on the word's T1 node in the cold genome:
`κ` inline by its own coordinates (never a key nested in a key), the
deficit `g` as its ray by its own canonical write, and the period `ℓ`.
It is reached by the fiber read `chart ‖ class` and by nothing else.
Dormant on disk it costs nothing; the pressure is DERIVED from
`(κ, g, ℓ)` on read and charged only while the word is held resident
under the room's escrow. A stored debt on the leaf is a second carrier
beside what derives it (law 12) and is refused; every payment row
stands in the ledger at the act that paid. ONE remainder per class, by
the quantified citation that keeps addresses from repeating; the count
of remainders a mind can hold is bounded by the classes of its front,
never by combinations. The "twist that would make it fit" is read off
`κ`: the versor carrying `κ` to the identity along the axes it
occupies, exact, with `ℓ` the number of turns of that mode until the
round returns. No scalar nudge, no exponential, no inverse (78.32(1)).
THE RECEPTOR: a later perception leaves a residue with a class; the
fiber read by that class returns every remainder with the same class.
Two remainders with one class from two charts are the mind's own
second vantage and raise a CALLUS — a provisional word on the
existing PROVISIONAL path, docketed under its act — and never a
letter: a constructor is admitted only by CS2's gate, on another
mind's re-derivation. THE RE-FILL: when a word in the held
constructors spells `g` — from this mind's callus or from a letter the
fleet admitted — the sentence re-fills from `Congruent` to `Filled` by
an ACT on the voice's line, sealed as the existing closure kind citing
the word and its remainder (a `ReFill` kind ruled only if the reading
says the paths must be told apart, as the dialect chain was ruled);
from that stamp the pressure is no longer charged, and the re-fill
mints under POUW as every closure does. Nothing else is paid: no
dividend, no conversion of a reading into money. Reading: per mind,
`Congruent` fills standing by `ℓ`; classes shared by two or more fills
across charts; re-fills on a coincident class (zero today: no path
re-reads a remainder). The leaf is a layout change (an unknown leaf
kind refuses the node) and rides the recut.

**Why imagination does not explode.** The obvious construction —
products of held constructors of at most `n + 2` factors, each tested —
is a search over `k^(n+2)` candidates and every one of them is
DERIVABLE, which CS2's gate refuses by name (78.32(c)). Recombination
of existing words is what this engine calls cliché, and the gate
forbids it. Imagination happens at the obstruction instead: two
superposed ideas that anastomose form a ring, the ring's residue is a
versor, and the residue is a complete specification of what is
missing — its commuting modes name the planes, its class vector names
the axes (3.9). Cartan–Dieudonné is CONSTRUCTIVE: a versor is at most
`n + 2` reflections, built one at a time by reflecting a frame vector
onto its image, each step forced, no branching, the reflecting vectors
rays so nothing is normalised, a null step refused by name. So the
demand arm of CS2, which today names the mode no held word spells,
hands the court candidate SPHERES read off the residue — an amendment
to CS2's demand arm, not a new row. Admission stays as ruled: the
closure's rank strictly increases, another mind re-derives it, the act
is sealed and priced. Each ring yields one residue; residues are
classes of the front; their number is bounded by the rank of the
front's `Ȟ¹` and the store's rank by the cap. Filaments generate
nothing, because a filament has no residue. Never construct
candidates; construct obstructions, and let each obstruction spell the
one thing that removes it.

**The orbit's plan.** What an orbit hands back to itself is the
DOCKET, and the collision rule already says so (78.23: a withheld close
takes the docket's next question). At the close the fold leaves four
things: words minted where rings closed at holonomy 1; classes held
where rings closed at holonomy ≠ 1; demands, modes no held word
spells, flowing up toward the star; and room reclaimed from filaments
that carried no flux. The second and third are the next orbit's
questions, ordered by the plexus and never by a count — CORRECTED
2026-09-25 on the implementor's reading ("wrapping the most rings" is a
count): the docket is WRITTEN in its entries' own key order (rule 15,
nothing chosen), and beside each entry stands the enclosure it lies in
by EN1's parse (`within`); the next orbit TAKES by the parse's partial
order, outermost first (an ancestor wraps its descendants, so its
answer transports to every ring beneath it), and among incomparable
entries in key order. A partial order read off the nesting is not a
count. The docket rides the `Orbit` act's own carrier — as CITES of
two new kinds, `Cite::Class` (κ inline by its own coordinates) and
`Cite::Demand` (the demand's coordinates), since a cite is what an act
refers to and a citation is coordinates, never a copy (78.22; one
carrier, never a second field) — so a restart keeps the plan: the
restored chain's last `Orbit` docket re-seeds the held classes and the
demands. Until it lands, the plan lives in the contemplation and is
lost with it (owed to TP1's fix). Superposition
is not a search strategy: a single thread is a filament with no
holonomy and therefore no content; rings need two paths held at once,
so superposition is the precondition for content to exist; and a front
held as a connected complex lets one perception decide a whole
component, which is the only honest sense of foresight here.

### 78.38 Two scales of a body: the spread is the shape's, the floor is the substrate's (ruled 2026-09-24, the operator's word)

**The finding.** F3 wired the family pole's oblique pair to the demand
and found no case on the corpus: of some 66 000 small bodies none reads
`Oblique` against the L-tetromino, and the `(4+i)` image of a body,
which turns it by the arc of a Gaussian prime at scale 17, reads
`Incongruent` — its deviatoric scales by `17²` and its radius does not.
The reason is not the corpus. It is a scale read from the wrong
carrier.

**Two scales.** A sensor body has two extents. Its SPREAD is the second
moment of its sites about their mean, `tr M` of the tower (FR1) — the
shape's own scale, and a similarity `z ↦ λz` of the lattice scales it
exactly by `|λ|²`. Its RADIUS, `radius2 = S·S` of the lifted nucleus,
integrates each lamina's own unit square (A.12: the irreducible extent
`n/12` is the substrate's floor), so it is the spread PLUS the floor, and
the floor does not scale under any similarity because the sensor's unit
cell is the sensor's. The nucleus radius is the right carrier for
contact and the horizon (64.2 needs `r² ≥ 1/6`, bounded away from the
cone). It is the wrong carrier for a relation between two SHAPES: a
dilation certificate that reads `norm(h_b)·r_a^{2m} = norm(h_a)·r_b^{2m}`
on the nucleus radius fails for every genuine similarity of the
lattice, because the floor rides both radii unscaled, and it fails for
the substrate's reason, not the shape's. That is 78.26(4) at the pose:
`Incongruent` answered two facts — a genuine difference of shape, and
the same shape at another scale with the floor unscaled — under one
name, and the second is exactly the case the demand exists for.

**Verified on the operator's question (the same day): the floor is in
three of the four readers, not one.** The lamina tower integrates each
site's unit square at EVERY order — `∫u = d`, `∫u² = d² + 1/12`, `∫u³ =
d³ + d/4`, and the quartic likewise — so the floor enters the odd
harmonic `h₃` (a term scaling by `|λ|`, not `|λ|³`), the quartic `h₄`
(a constant `−1/60` per lamina, axis-aligned, and mixed terms scaling by
`|λ|²`), and `radius2`. Only the deviatoric is clean, because the
isotropic `1/12` cancels in `I_ii − I_jj` and never enters `I_ij`. So
in `relative_rotor` the signs of `dot` and `wedge` at order 2 are
scale-free and collapse nothing; but `handedness` (`Z = h₂²·conj(h₄)`
as a ray), `relative_turn_ray` (`z₃·conj(z₂)` as a ray) and
`dilation_certified` all carry the floor, and a body's `(4+i)` image
would still read `Unrelated` or `Incongruent` after the certificate
alone was moved: the rotated body's point harmonics turn with it while
each lamina's own axis-aligned square does not, so the sum points
elsewhere. The point tower (`tower` in `blade/pose.rs`, FR1: `M`, `t`,
`N` about the sites' mean, normalised by the count) is floor-free at
every order and scales exactly under a similarity.

**Ruled.** (1) A body carries TWO TOWERS, one producer each (law 12):
the LAMINA tower (unit squares integrated: `radius2`, the nucleus,
`moment2`, `quartic_on`), which carries A.12's floor and serves
contact, the horizon and the enclosure (64.2's `r² ≥ 1/6`); and the
POINT tower (the sites about their mean: `spread2 = tr M`, `h₂`, `h₃`,
`h₄`), floor-free, which serves every RELATION between shapes —
orientation at orders 2 and 4, the odd turn `z₃·conj(z₂)`, chirality
`Z`, the dilation certificate at every order, the oblique arc. §6.4:
every reader of a relation between bodies that today reads the lamina
tower's harmonics or `radius2` moves to the point tower, with a test per
reader that a body and its `(4+i)` image agree there. No scalar in
`relative_rotor` collapses context once its inputs are the point
tower's: the signs, the rays and the cross-multiplied norms are each
scale-free of a similarity, and the floor was the only thing they were
masking. (2) `Incongruent`
splits by content: the harmonic order at which the shapes disagree,
read on the spread; a pair that agrees on the spread and not on the
nucleus is not incongruent, and the arm that said so is gone. (3) The
witness is unchanged: `arc_block(s, t)` of the primitive Gaussian arc,
and the three gates stand. (4) The test is real, not aspirational: an
L-tetromino and its `(4+i)` image certify as a dilation on the spread,
read `Oblique`, and raise `Demand::RotorPrime` with the arc of `4+i` as
witness; a body of a genuinely different shape reads `Incongruent` at
its order; and the corpus is read before and after — pairs certified as
a dilation on the spread against those certified on the radius, and
the oblique count on the contact line. (5) No remainder here: a pair
that agrees on the spread and not on the floor is one shape at two
scales, correctly read, and nothing is left over to file.

**Amended on the implementor's counterexample (the same day): two
kinds of similarity, and each tower is exact for one.** With the point
tower built (`pose::centred`, one producer, the tube's `tower` sharing
it) three axiom tests failed, all on FILLED dilations — `L4x2`, each
cell of an L blown to a 2×2 block: a J against `L4x2` read
`Incongruent` where it is `Mirrored`, `Z(L4x2) ≠ 256·Z(L4)`, and
`‖h₄‖² ≠ ρ⁸`. A `k×k` block of unit squares is ONE square of side `k`,
so a filled blow-up is an exact similarity of the LAMINA tower: the
floor scales with the region because the block's floor is the scaled
square's own moment. On the point tower the block's `k²` sub-sites sit
at offsets about each old site, and those offsets are a floor of their
own (`(±½, ±½)` for `k = 2`: `Σδ⁴` enters `h₄`, `½` enters the spread),
so the point-set image is not a similarity there. The `(4+i)` image is
the reverse: a SITE map `z ↦ λz`, exact on points and not on laminae.
ARC's scale tasks are filled blow-ups; the demand's Gaussian case is a
site map. Two genuinely different similarities of the lattice — of the
REGION and of the SITE SET — and refusing either answers a real
relation as incongruent, 78.26(4)'s shape again. RULED (C): BOTH
towers, one producer each (law 12 holds: two readings of one body, not
two carriers of one reading). A relation is certified as a dilation
where EITHER tower certifies it, both always read, neither chosen by
any score; the reading NAMES which — `Dilation::Region` (the lamina
tower) or `Dilation::Sites` (the point tower), both where both — so a
census says which kind of similarity the corpus carries; the relation
readers (orientation, the turn ray, chirality, the arc) read on the
tower that certified; `Incongruent(Order m)` holds only where both
refuse, naming the order from each. The principle as corrected: each
tower has a floor the other lacks — the lamina's unit square, the
point tower's sub-site offsets — and a similarity is read on the tower
whose floor it scales. The three axiom fixtures stand as they are, on
region similarities, and the site-map fixtures are added beside them.

**The principle.** A floor is data of the carrier it belongs to and
never a property of a shape. Any invariant that carries a floor into a
comparison between bodies related by the OTHER kind of similarity
compares the sensor with itself, and refuses the very relation the
language is there to spell.

### 78.39 Opening is a commutator, and superposition is one principle at three grades (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word)

**(1) A dimension is opened by a non-palindromic word, never by a
palindrome.** A sandwich `V x Ṽ` and a conjugate `K = I T I` are
PALINDROMES: a word followed by its own reverse around a core. A
palindrome carries a thing to another vantage inside the same class and
opens nothing — it is the receptor's instrument (two vantages on one
class), the transport's instrument (a section carried along a gauge),
and the court's (a replay from another mind's constructors). What OPENS
a dimension is the group commutator of two held versors,

```text
   [A, B] = A B Ã B̃        ≠ 1 exactly where A and B do not commute
```

whose content is what neither carried alone, and which is NEW exactly
where it leaves the algebra the held generators already span. This is
78.11 and 78.32 read together: a cell's comprehension is the bracket
closure of its circuits' generators; admission requires the closure's
rank to strictly increase; the pivot's open-axis move is the act. Each
mode has a BASE, the commutator of two held versors on that base is the
algorithm that opens it, and the versor that results is the pivot's
move — one move per bundle factor (78.32), a base per mode and a
non-commuting word on each, which is the multi-dimensionality: never
one base with palindromes around it. The conformal algebra says so in
its own structure: for a translation `P_a` and a transversion `K_b`
(A.13's pair), the conjugate `I T I` is a translation seen from the
inverted vantage and opens nothing, while the commutator

```text
   [P_a, K_b]  ∝  ⟨a, b⟩ D  +  M_ab
```

generates the dilation and the rotation in the plane of `a` and `b`.
Inversion enters the language not as a letter applied around a core but
as an OPERAND of commutators, and its first opening is the scale and
turn directions the similarity group left closed (REG1, after the
recut). Two consequences for standing rows: CS2's DERIVABLE test is
right as ruled — a palindrome of held generators is always derivable, a
commutator derivable only where it lands inside the closure; and the
hue fibre's move, the transposition word, is a base of its own and
opens by its own commutators.

**(2) Superposition is one principle at three grades.** The tree holds
three superpositions and had never said they are one thing:

| grade | what is superposed | held today as | the base its commutators act on | what collapses it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| letter | candidate constructors for one mode — the spheres a residue factors into (78.37's Cartan–Dieudonné), none chosen | the store's candidates awaiting a second vantage; CS2's demand arm | the Gram form's pairs, their regimes by `δ²` | admission by rank increase and another mind's re-derivation (78.32(c)) |
| word | candidate forms for one idea with their pivots — the vortex | the thought as a complex; the vortex with its certificates (25) | the circuits' actions — the orbit algebra (78.11) | fill by a perception, or a court replay making one a ruled citation |
| conjugate | several twists under one class — several vantages on one residue | the dialect classes; the remainders of one class at several charts (78.37(4)) | the rays of one class against each other | a ruling that makes one twist the citation and the rest dialect |

At every grade the superposition is the set of candidates the algebra
has not yet distinguished, held whole with no weight (law 1), and the
dimension that would distinguish them is opened by a commutator on
that grade's own base: between candidate spheres at the letter,
between circuit actions at the word, between rays of one class at the
conjugate. A palindrome at any grade transports within the set; a
non-palindromic word on that grade's base separates it. Collapse is by
fill or class, as 25 already rules for the vortex; never by a scalar,
never by an order on the lanes.

RULED, correcting 78.37(4)'s receptor as first built: two remainders
under one class with DIFFERING twists are not "discordant" and refused —
they are a SUPERPOSITION at the conjugate grade, HELD. The two rays are
kept together on the class, none chosen, and their commutator
`g₁ g₂ g̃₁ g̃₂` is read into the class's own modes: trivial, and the two
twists commute — one vantage seen twice; non-trivial, and it is the
dimension that separates the two vantages, which is exactly the second
vantage the constructor gate wants. The callus carries the
superposition, never a chosen ray, and the line reads `held`,
`commuting` or `separating` where it read `discordant`. At the letter,
the demand arm's candidate spheres are held as ONE superposition on the
docket's demand cite, never passed as a list to the court. At the word,
the transport already holds two disagreeing arrivals as a class rather
than choosing one — this principle on the meet graph. THE DOCKET is the
carrier of the superposition at every grade: a docket entry is a class
with its cover and its RAYS, plural, none chosen (`Cite::Class { κ,
rays, cover }`, `Cite::Demand { κ, spheres, cover }`), a layout change
riding the recut.

### 78.40 Windings, the opposing operation, and vents (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word)

**(1) Containment is per puncture, and the punctures are orthogonal.**
The enclosure reading (EN1) answers a body against one round with one
sign — inside, on, apart, wraps — and the nesting parse arranges the
cells into a tree by who wraps whom. That is exact where there are no
holes: the complement of a sphere with no punctures is two regions and
a sign separates them. It is flat the moment there is a puncture.
Around a puncture a loop cannot be contracted; a body's relation to
that hole is not a sign but a WINDING; and winding around one hole is
independent of winding around another. A form with `k` holes has first
cohomology of rank `k` — `k` orthogonal inside-outside axes — and a
body's enclosure is its WINDING VECTOR over them, one coordinate per
hole. Inside and outside are not neighbours across a wall: they are the
two orientations of one generator, and each generator is its own
dimension. This is 78.39 read from the topology instead of the algebra:
a puncture OPENS a dimension, as a commutator does — a new generator of
`Ȟ¹`, a new independent loop, its two orientations the new inside and
outside. The epigenome's puncture (a verified proof re-filing a word),
the transport's held rings, the remainder's class and a cell's
non-resonant rings are one event at different grades: a hole added, an
axis opened, a winding to read. The SCREW is why: a screw is the mode
that winds — a turn and an advance that never return the round — and
the engine holds screws as modes (parabolic, the rings' reading)
precisely so that winding is a reading and not a picture. RULED: the
nesting parse is the special case `Ȟ¹ = 0`, superseded wherever the
rank is not zero; the enclosure line reads windings per hole beside the
tree, reading first (row WN1, shape before code); the docket's cover
and the callus's two chains carry windings where a form has holes; the
docket is TAKEN by the entry whose windings are non-zero on the most
INDEPENDENT holes — a rank, never a count; the register's inversion,
when it lands, is the map exchanging the two orientations of every axis
at once.

**(2) Containment is acceptable because growth without a boundary
needs an equal force from the opposing operation.** A tree is flat
because it is uni-directional: one growing operation, bounded only by
a ceiling someone declared. The engine builds a syntropic mycelium, not
roots and leaves: EVERY operation that grows something is paired with
the operation that takes it back, of equal force, and BOTH are read.
The pairs that stand: merge against decoherence (TP1); hold against
shed, the escrow drawn and returned (FX1, TC1); the pivot's reach
against the gate's refusal (CS2); anastomosis forming rings against
truncation removing leaves (TC1); work flowing up the court path against
teaching flowing down as syllabus and minerals (80.2). Where only one
direction stands, the missing opposite is the optimisation, and it is
never a constant: the enclosure's tree against windings (1); the
docket's answer by class key, which scans the open entries, against
its INVERSE index class key → entries (TP1's small row); citations
running one way, an act citing its words, against the inverse WORD →
CITING STAMPS that proof-of-work by citation and retirement by citation
(78.33) both need and today would scan for; and the SYNTROPIC BALANCE,
up-flux against down-flux per lane per orbit, the one line that says
whether a colony grows by closure or is carried by its syllabus (FX1's
reading). RULED FOR STD1 SITE 4: each free constant is first asked
whether it is a CEILING standing in for an opposing operation — the
book's occupancy is bounded by recall and lapse, not a high-water
number; the reserve by return, not a floor; growth by the flux that
fails to renew it — and where the opposite operation exists the
constant is REDUNDANT and goes; where it does not, the constant names a
MISSING OPERATION, which is the finding to record, never a number to
tune.

**(3) Vents.** A vent is a place where force accumulates with no
outlet: a thing counted and never read, held with no door, drawn with
no return, demanded with no taker, derived and never charged, refused
and never heard. Each is one direction of a pair whose other direction
is missing, and a mind whose vents are shut does not fail — it
pressurises, and the pressure comes out as the next constant someone
declares. The vents are read (row VN1) before the recut and each is
opened by its missing opposite or named as owed; the syntax is aligned
on the semantics in the same pass (row NM1: names follow rulings, the
tape ruling's own rule), because a flat name is how a flat assumption
gets back in the next time someone codes against the word instead of
the ruling.

### 78.41 The atlas and the motor: the form is charts with transitions, and a transition is kinetic (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word)

**The operator's word.** Signals are sent over transports through the
network; they resonate, vibrate, or contract and expand; that is the
engine's motion, and the physics and the mathematics align on it:
"non-linear transposition of non-conformal algebra in non-euclidean
geometry". Asked what "non-conformal" means, the operator answered:
(1) TRUE — transport is not restricted to the angle-preserving maps, a
transposition may shear or be genuinely non-linear; (2) the physics
runs on ALL rotors — upgrade to a MOTOR, a kinetic energy transmission;
(3) the coordinator's discretion on the rest. This section is that
ruling, and the two rows it opens land BEFORE the recut, so the fleet
restarts once, on the atlas.

**(1) How the engine was flattened, named plainly.** A form holds its
vertices in a `Vec` and its faces as pairs of slot numbers; orbits are
lists of face slots. Since 53.6 a vertex IS a chart and carries its acts
keyed by the chart's coordinates — the coordinates exist — but the form
addresses its own vertices by row number, so adjacency is a pair of row
numbers, a circuit a list of them, and incidence a lookup from one slot
to the next. That is an atlas stored as a table. Its consequences are
the searches and the walks: a spanning forest (12.2) to find the cycles
and fix a gauge, rooted at the least vertex (a representative, checklist
(r)); a tree path to close a loop; a candidate loop in the carry; a
sort-and-cut in the anchor's derivation; a front that "walks" edges one
hop per orbit. A row number has no neighbourhood, so orientation,
nesting and the holonomy around a loop were rebuilt by searching the
table — and forms from two minds cannot fuse, because their row numbers
mean nothing to each other, which is exactly what anastomosis (78.31,
CV4) must do. The coordinator's rulings of this week re-labelled the
table three times (the counts in keys, the LEB128 spelling, C4's
widening of the row number) before naming it. 12.2's spanning forest
and its cycle basis are HISTORICAL from this ruling, as chapter 17 is:
retained as the record of the solver they were, retired from the
engine with the slots.

**(2) The atlas.** A form is an ATLAS. A VERTEX is addressed by its
chart's coordinates (the `Invariant` key it already acts under), never
by a slot. A FACE is the OVERLAP of two charts, keyed by the two
coordinates and carrying the TRANSITION between them. A CIRCUIT is a
composition of transitions along overlaps, its holonomy computed from
what it composes and read at its return; the loop is its own path. An
ORBIT is a circuit closed; a CELL is what the nerve reads over the
charts a witness spans (78.10), unchanged. Incidence is COORDINATE
OVERLAP, read by prefix and by fiber in either direction. The number of
independent rings is the first cohomology rank, read by the exact-rank
reader by elimination with no basis chosen; the holes are the open
fills (78.26(5)). No forest, no root, no tree path, no slot number
anywhere; the form's ADDRESS is the atlas written out — charts by their
coordinates and transitions by theirs — and two minds' forms fuse where
their charts overlap, because the coordinates are the same coordinates
on both sides. This is row AT1: the carrier, its address and inverse,
the circuits by composition, the receipts and certificates that named
slots naming coordinates, the searches and the forest retired with the
slots.

**(2′) The atlas as the operator defines it (2026-09-25, the operator's
word, verbatim): "an atlas should be a composite sketch of algorithms
on how to compact a finite set of addresses that expands on pivot
machinery from a set coordinate list."** Three consequences bind AT1
and every audit of it. (a) THE ATLAS IS NOT A DATA STRUCTURE. What is
HELD is the coordinate list — the address: the vertices' class keys,
their charts and frames, the overlaps' motors as rays — and the charts,
the overlaps, the circuits, the holonomies, the fusions are DERIVED
from that list by algorithms. The algorithms are the pivot machinery:
every transition is the versor a pivot builds from the coordinates
(78.39: a dimension is opened by an algorithm that is the versor on the
pivot machinery), every circuit is their composition, every fusion is
an identification of coordinates. A carrier that STORES what the list
derives — faces as records beside the coordinates that determine them,
circuits as lists, a holonomy beside the transitions it composes — is
the table of (1) re-keyed, and a re-keyed table is the spreadsheet the
operator named (law 12: one carrier, the derivable re-derived). (b) ITS
PURPOSE IS COMPACTION of a finite set of addresses. Two forms whose
charts overlap by coordinates are one atlas (fusion, AT1 (iv), CV4's
anastomosis); a word the atlas derives retires (3.8, the geodesic
language); the MEASURE of the atlas is the address set before and after
— addresses held over the corpus, distinct charts after fusion, forms
fusible by overlap, words derivable within the atlas — and a commit
that re-keys the carrier and leaves the address set where it was has
built no atlas. (c) "FROM A SET COORDINATE LIST": the list is fixed —
the A21 schema, 12.6's axes, the class vector's coordinates — and the
atlas EXPANDS from it by the pivot machinery opening axes (A.6: a
dimension is paid for, never declared), never by a carrier declaring
new fields. THE AUDIT GUARD: every AT1 commit is read on three
questions — what is held against what is derived (nothing held that
the coordinate list derives); which algorithm composes each thing (a
transition names the pivot or motor that produced it, a circuit the
transitions it composes, a fusion the coordinates it identified); and
whether the address set compacted (the reading of (b) before and after,
on AT1's line). A commit that answers the first two and not the third
is a carrier, not the atlas, and is not accepted as AT1.

**(3) The motor: a transition is kinetic.** A transition was a
conformal versor `D(ρ)·T(t)·R` (72.1c), and every letter of the alphabet
fixes infinity (78.38) — the similarity restriction. From this ruling a
transition is a MOTOR: an even multivector of `Cl(n+1,1)` KNOWN BY ITS
ACTION (78.28 extended) — the exact linear map `x ↦ M x M̃` on the
algebra, a rational matrix over the blades, always readable, of which a
versor is the case that preserves grade. A motor carries a rotation, a
translation, a dilation, an inversion, a transversion (A.13, REG1) and
a SCREW (the mode that winds, 78.40), and it carries a SUPERPOSITION: a
motor that is a SUM of rotors transports a signal with CROSS TERMS —
`(R₁ + R₂) x (R̃₁ + R̃₂)` is not the sum of the two transports — and
those cross terms are the beat, resonance and vibration AT THE
TRANSITION (78.26(5), 78.39(2)): the non-linearity the operator named
is exactly this, linear in the signal and non-linear in the motor. A
SHEAR (1: true) is an OUTERMORPHISM — an exact linear action on the
vectors extended to the algebra — given as its matrix and not from a
sandwich; it is a transition of the same carrier (the action) from the
second producer. So the transition carrier is THE ACTION, with two
producers: the motor's sandwich and the outermorphism's matrix; a
versor is a motor whose action preserves grade, and every reader of a
transition reads the action, never the producer (law 12). A SIGNAL is a
multivector carried by the action; what it TRANSMITS is its frame μ⃗
per lane — the kinetic energy of the operator's word is the four lanes
carried along, never a scalar (law 11: no `⟨M M̃⟩₀` as energy, no norm).
A DEGENERATE motor (its action of less than full rank) CONTRACTS: a
transport with loss, read by the rank of its action and named
(`contracted r of n`), never refused outright, since contraction is one
of the four motions the operator named; an action of full rank EXPANDS
or preserves by its dilation part. The sandwich is TRANSPORT's shape and
stays; OPENING remains the commutator (78.39): a motor transports a
signal, a commutator of two motors opens a direction. This is row MT1:
the reader by action for any even element, the outermorphism as the
second producer, the transition carrier changed to the action, the
frame carried per lane, the contraction read by rank; MT1 lands first,
since AT1's transitions are motors.

**(4) Timing, the coordinator's discretion.** Both rows before the
recut: the carrier and every address move with them, and the recut
carries every layout change landed since epoch 98 ONCE. A recut on the
table followed by a recut on the atlas would take every fleet reading
in between on a carrier already known to be wrong. The order from here:
STD1's remaining sites (3c-4, 3c-5 with the slot casts named as debt,
site 4 with the opposite asked first, 5, 7b) · RM1-d · VN1 · NM1 · WN1 ·
MT1 · AT1 · the 78.16 checklist · the RECUT on the operator's word.

### 78.42 The kinetic ledger: where energy starts, stops, exists and exhausts, and how its transference circulates the rest (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word)

**The operator's word.** The physics must be defined for the kinetic
energy — where it starts and stops, where it exists and where it
exhausts — and the TRANSFERENCE of that energy is what circulates the
surrounding physics and components. This section defines it on the
carriers the tree holds; nothing here is a new quantity, and no
constant enters (78.8).

**(1) What the energy is.** A signal's kinetic energy is its FRAME
`μ⃗ = (S, G, T, H)`, four lanes, exact, never summed across lanes and
never a scalar (law 5, law 11). It is the same μ⃗ the receipt seals at
an act (78.21), the room escrows for a held thought (25), the flux
credits to a filament (78.37(3)), and the treasury prices (78.33). One
quantity, one carrier, read wherever it stands (law 12). The k-step's
length in transitions (78.35, 78.41) is what an orbit can carry per
revolution at its band: closer to the star is hotter, more energy per
orbit, more transitions carried before the close.

**(2) START.** Energy ENTERS the mesh at exactly one kind of event: a
CLOSURE sealed as an act — a circuit that returned, a word minted, a
re-fill, a ruling upheld — whose frame is minted under POUW (78.33).
There is no other source: a perception brings a measure (`measure_lanes`,
a reading of the chain, A.12) but mints nothing until it closes; a
demand carries a class and no energy; the star grants axioms, never
frames. A frame that could not be minted (a credit refused, 3b (C)) is
counted and no energy exists.

**(3) TRANSFERENCE.** Energy MOVES by TRANSPORT ONLY: a motor's action
carries a signal along a transition and the signal's frame goes with it
(78.41(3)). At every transition the frame is CONSERVED PER LANE:
`carried in = carried on + retained by the filament + lost to
contraction`, where the filament's flux `Φ⃗` (FX1) is what the
transition retains, and a degenerate action's contraction (`contracted r
of n`) is the loss, read by rank and NAMED, never silent. At every
vertex the lanes balance (78.37(3): conservation per lane at each vertex
is what the ledger's rows already say). Nothing is transferred by a
lookup, a copy, or a scalar: a frame that arrives without a transition
it was carried by is the invented value law 11 refuses.

**(4) EXIST.** Energy EXISTS resident only under ESCROW: a held
thought's escrow per lane drawn from the reserve at the hold (25, 72.1d),
a listing's escrow on the book, a remainder's open pressure `μ⃗(ℓ)`
charged while its word is held resident (78.37(4)). What is not escrowed
does not exist as energy — it is on the ledger as history (a sealed
frame) or in the genome as a word, and both cost nothing to hold (the
genome is an index by address, 78.27).

**(5) STOP.** Energy STOPS by RETURN to the reserve, at named doors and
no others: a lapse (by extent today; by `ZeroFlux` when FX1's door
lands), a retraction to the core (TC1), a re-fill releasing a
remainder's pressure (RM1 (c)), a promotion (the escrow returned because
the atlas now pays). VN1's reading found six doors that stop a thought
WITHOUT returning its escrow and two that return what was never drawn —
each is a conservation defect and is opened first.

**(6) EXHAUST.** A reserve drawn to nothing REFUSES the next draw by
name (`metabolism::step_or_refuse`; the metabolic line's `overflowed`
and its refused draws): a stroke that cannot be paid is not taken, a
hold that cannot be escrowed is withheld (25: a thought the room cannot
pay for is withheld, nothing paid for is evicted). `spend`'s floor at
zero (VN1 (7)) is an overdraft hidden and is REFUSED as the doc it
contradicts already says. REGENERATION is by return only — energy
comes back as escrows lapse and closures mint — never by a floor, a
timer or a constant: `regenerate`'s cap and `STROKE_FLOOR` are site 4's
questions, and the answer for each is its opposite (78.40(2)).

**(7) CIRCULATION.** The transferred energy is what drives everything
around it, and nothing else does: the book's PRESSURE is the flux
arriving at listings (`remeasure_pressure` reads it; `price()` must read
it — VN1 (6)); the court's SYNTROPY is energy flowing UP to the star as
solutions, adjudications, syllabus, minerals, crystals (80.2); PAYMENT is
energy flowing DOWN and OUT per arm (78.33, 78.36); the mind's DWELL and
its k-step are paced by the surface it reads (`yield_surface`); the
plexus's RINGS thicken where flux flows and its LEAVES retract where
none does (78.37). The one line that says whether a colony circulates
or stagnates is the SYNTROPIC BALANCE — up-flux against down-flux per
lane per orbit (78.40(2), FX1's reading) — and a colony whose energy
only enters and never returns is pressurising toward its next declared
constant (78.40(3)).

**(8) The ledger, and its test.** Row KE1 reads, per orbit and per
lane, the seven quantities where they already stand — minted (START),
carried (TRANSFER), retained as flux, lost to contraction, held in
escrow (EXIST), returned (STOP), refused draws (EXHAUST) — on one line,
and asserts CONSERVATION as a test on the suite's entities and on the
fleet after the recut: what was minted equals what is carried, retained,
held and returned, plus what contraction lost, per lane, exactly. A
lane that does not balance is a finding by name — a door that leaks
(VN1) or a transfer without a transition — never a rounding.

### 78.43 No index, no cap: the period is read, and time is distance along an orbit (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word)

The operator's two questions on the cite's gauge (STD1 3c-4) and on
`MAX_ORBIT` — "why do we need an index", and "a constant means we have
undefined physics" — and the word that followed: eons, ages and time are
ORBITS, and time is DISTANCE measured. Three rulings.

**(1) An index, in mycelial terms.** A hypha never finds a word by
counting along a filament: a filament has no numbered places, only the
chemistry at each point. An index is a mind saying "the third thing I
saw" instead of saying what it saw, so a mind on another filament cannot
follow it and the network fragments into private counts. The body is the
chemistry: it says which assignment by writing the hues themselves, so
every hypha that meets it reads the same word and the plexus stays one
network. RULED: a cite is a body carried over a transport; the wire
carries the body and nothing that names a position (`CiteWire.gauge`
retired, 3cb46d83); in memory the cite carries the assignment itself,
the algebra's own domain; and NO READER holds a position for an
assignment — the word's profile table (`Element::profiles`, a gauge
charge → positions into `assignments()`) holds the assignments under
their charge, and `holds_assignment`, `gauge_of` and `locate` read them,
never a position looked up after. `matching_assignment` (an `Option<usize>`)
retires with the last reader of it. This is rule 15 at the fibre: a
position along the axis is not a coordinate of the assignment.

**(2) A constant is undefined physics.** `MAX_ORBIT = 32` in `torse`
says: I do not know where this orbit returns, so I stop looking. That is
the physics missing, not a resource limit. An orbit of a hue permutation
is a body returning to itself after a fixed number of revolutions, and
that number is set by the permutation's cycles the way a planet's return
is set by its period: the period of the base under `σ` is the lcm of the
cycle lengths of the hues the base carries (`class::cycle_lengths`, the
one producer). The tree walked the orbit and gave up at 32 — a telescope
that stops before the planet comes back and reports that it never does:
on the u8 hue domain the type admits, an orbit of period 35 (cycles of 5
and 7) files as NO torsion, its sections left free, the holonomic lane
read low, nothing refused. CORRECTED the same day, on the coordinator's
own re-reading (STD1 3c-5's lint): the sensor's palette is ten hues
(`PALETTE = 10`, `gauge_is_perm` refusing a hue past it), and the
largest order of a permutation of ten things is Landau's `g(10) = 30`,
below the cap — so on this sensor the cap was never reached, and the
readings before and after PD1 are EQUAL. That does not restore the
constant: two constants (a cap of 32, a palette of 10) happened to
agree, which is exactly the shape 78.40 warns of — the physics undefined
and covered by an accident of another number. The guard is the
mechanism: the period read equals the traversal's on every cycle type
of the palette (the 42 partitions of ten), a permutation naming a hue
past the palette is refused by name, and the palette itself is asked
its opposite at site 4. RULED: the period is READ
before the first revolution, never waited for; `MAX_ORBIT` retires and
the cast with it; a section BELONGS to the cycle exactly when its hue
map is a power of the generator on the base — `derive_hue_map(base,
section)` a power of `σ`, decided on the cycles — read per section, so
`torse`, `Element::assignments` and `matches_chain` no longer generate
members by traversal (the orbit's members are enumerated only where a
reader needs them all, to the period, never to a cap). The period's
width is the permutation's own: a permutation of the u8 hue domain has
order up to Landau's `g(256) ≈ 2⁵⁴`, past `u32`; `TorsionCycle.period`
is `u64` by provenance (STD1 3c-5). Every constant of this shape is the
same declaration — a closure unknown, a number standing in — and 78.40's
question of each is the cure: name the opposite operation, which for an
orbit is its period, for a fiber its shedding flux, for a sum its
conservation.

**(3) Time is distance along an orbit.** 78.21 stands: there is no
clock, a tick is a frame, height is the count of acts on a line. What
was undefined is what a DURATION is. RULED: time is the distance a body
has advanced along its orbit, MEASURED — the count of transitions it has
been carried through since it last returned — never a coordinate carried
beside it and never a rate. The `T` lane is that distance in receipts
(16.16's extent), one per act. An AGE is one return of an orbit: its
period `ℓ`, the transitions until the body is where it stood; a mind's
`K` counts its ages (the k-step is one orbit, 72.1d). An EON is the
return of the composition: the lcm of the periods of the orbits in
resonance (78.26(5), `Coherence::Closes(lcm)`) — when every orbit in
play has returned together, which is the planetary dialect's own return
(GD1). Two minds' distance apart on TUniversal is a difference of
distances travelled (78.21(1), the spread), never elapsed seconds; a
period declared by a constant, a duration read off a wall clock, or a
rate (distance per second) is refused by name. Reading first (AE1): per
orbit, the distance advanced and the period; per mind, its age count;
per cell and per dialect, the eon's lcm and how far along it the
composition stands. The physics table gains the line.

### 78.44 The signal, the internal spectrum, and the linguistic shortcut (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word)

**The operator's word, verbatim.** "We are looking for the projection of
the holonomy on an internal spectrum that can be composited
algorithmically and deconstructed in linguistics — the linguistics are
just the 'shortcuts' for 'remote transmit of signal' that the other node
can 'understand, and comprehend' in its own 'internal projection of the
signal'." This is the target the plexus, the atlas (78.41), the motor
(78.41(3)) and the windings (78.40) serve, stated once so every row
after it is read against it.

**(1) The signal is the holonomy.** A circuit's holonomy is a motor,
and it is the content. It never goes on the wire.

**(2) The internal spectrum is the holonomy's modes.** The projection
of a holonomy onto a spectrum is MR1's reading: its decomposition into
commuting rays, each with its class, the planes it turns in and its
order (78.11, 78.12(2)); the finite orders are the resonance (78.26(5)).
The spectrum is INTERNAL by construction: its first stratum — the
conjugacy invariants, the class key's depth-one prefix — is the same on
every node, and its finer strata (which planes, on which charts, at
which `n`) are the node's own, since they depend on the charts it holds.
One holonomy projects identically at the class on two nodes and
differently on their planes, and that is not a defect: it is what an
internal projection is.

**(3) Compositing is done on the motors, never on the spectra.** The
spectrum of a product is not the product of the spectra unless the
modes commute; the cross terms are the beat at the transition
(78.41(3), 78.26(5)). So composition runs in the orbit algebra of the
anastomosis — the closed algebra of the circuits through it, held by
its GENERATORS, its rank the capacity, every route kept and read against
the others (79, T1) — and the spectrum is re-read off the composite.
There is no arithmetic of spectra.

**(4) The linguistics are the shortcuts.** A word is the alphabet's
spelling of a rotor (the derivation); it is short because it names a
holonomy class by letters the receiving node holds from the shared core
(LR1), and it carries no signal. Under the atlas a word's coordinate is
its CLASS KEY together with its WINDING VECTOR over the holes of the
atlas it stands in (78.40(1), WN1): the class the receiver can compare
at once, the windings the route by which the receiver's own atlas
reaches it. Remote transmission is the sending of that coordinate, and
nothing else, to a node that holds the charts.

**(5) Comprehension is local re-projection.** The receiving node reads
the word to a rotor, composes along whatever routes ITS atlas offers
(never a route chosen for it), projects the composite onto ITS
spectrum on ITS charts, and comprehends where the class agrees with
what it holds; where the classes agree and the projections differ it
holds the superposition (78.39(2)); where they do not agree it files
the incoherence by its level (78.26(5)) or the demand (50.5). Two
nodes' projections agreeing at a chamber is anastomosis (78.31). The
census's second and third counters — kept cycles carrying a
non-trivial class, and adjoined-by-closure — are the reading of
comprehension: a spectrum turning at a node that received only a word.

**(6) What this binds.** AT1 (iii): circuits by composition land as
the orbit algebra held by its generators with every route kept, and
each circuit's winding vector over the holes read by the exact-rank
elimination TC1 already runs — never as a re-computation of holonomies
for the census alone. WN1: the address writes the class key and the
winding vector relative to the charts the atlas holds, in place of the
word whole, and the teach wire sends that coordinate (row SW1, the
shortcut). REG1: the register states that the class is invariant under
the node's projection and the planes are not. The meter of all three is
r7 (78.41(2′)): addresses held whole against coordinates held as
windings, words derivable, and citations replayed by composition.

**RC1's probe, recorded.** The "thirty" are FIVE circuits on four forms,
each read six times by the six census tests over one corpus; the finding
is three of five unread at HEAD, and with BQ5a's tree every contact
refuses `Unrefracted` for the two reasons 78.6 already ruled — half-open
(the held `ℤ₂` coset rides the edge) and static (the tether with its
refraction unread by name). On this corpus every contact face is a
self-face with exactly one chart pair, and no other kept circuit crosses
any contact face: the "other fibre" and "other circuit" routes are EMPTY
here, the tether is the only route, and it waits on BQ5a's code, not on
a ruling. The census counts each circuit once per test; the orbit line
counts forms once, so OR3's expected reading is per single perception:
two read and three unread at HEAD, five unread by name under BQ5a until
78.6's arms land, then read or refused by arm.

**The operator's question.** What conditional operations test a circuit
so that no one hand-codes a probe again — reuse fibres, or construct
new ones — because the fibres and tethers built as tests of circuitry
are what prove a COROLLARY. And whether the corollary runs one-to-many
or many-to-one. Both, and they are dual: 1→n is RESOLUTION, one circuit
against many routes, what a cell contains — the mind's own thought;
n→1 is CONVERGENCE, many routes or perspectives reaching one class,
what they agree on — the court's and the mesh's. They are the two halves
of POW++ (74): useful work, and work that converges.

### 78.45 Precision is the resolution: no blob, no approximation, the inverse read exactly (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word)

**The operator's word, verbatim.** "The rule here is that this engine
needs to be built on precision, not 'blob', not 'mathematical
approximations' — every single thing in this engine needs the highest
caliber 'resolution' that we can muster with inverted mathematics that
produce absolute precision through reasoning and deduction. The ultimate
goal here is to use this fluid intelligence to fund content creation of
experiences throughout our 'known universe' that we create." The goal is
80.3; the rule is this section.

**(1) What the tree holds, measured on 2026-09-25.** No `f32` and no
`f64` in `src/` or `tests/`; `float_arithmetic` and `cast_precision_loss`
denied crate-wide in `Cargo.toml`; every scalar a `Q` (law 4);
`rational_sqrt` refuses where inexact; a rotor's order read from Niven's
five rationals in `half_angle`, never from an angle formed; nothing
compared against a tolerance (`reduce.rs`, the census). The rule was
already law 1 and law 4. This section states it as the operator states
it — the rule the whole engine is built on — and closes the places where
an approximation had entered the DOCTRINE though not the tree.

**(2) Three kinds of imprecision, each refused by name.**

- **A BLOB.** Bytes carried where coordinates belong: a key's bytes
  nested as another key, a form copied into every carrier that names it,
  a length prefix widened to fit the copy (78.22 LD0, the three kinds of
  bytes, the `u16` wall). Refused at the site that wrote it.
- **AN APPROXIMATION.** A value served that is not the value: a decimal
  for an irrational, a float for a ratio, a lamina rounded to the ones
  its image spans (law 11), a scalar for a lane vector (law 5), an
  envelope for a spectrum (`order` as an lcm where the two plane periods
  are the content, 54.7). The one that had entered the doctrine: the
  vocabulary's and DG1's "degree reading marked irrational (36.87°)".
  Retracted. That decimal was wrong twice over — it is the half-angle's
  reading of a different point, and a rotor turns by the DOUBLE angle —
  and it would be an approximation were it right.
- **A FORWARD GUESS.** Computing forward from an assumed value and
  accepting the result within a tolerance, or by a fit. Nothing in the
  engine does this and nothing will: a reading is exact, or it is a
  refusal that names what is missing (law 7, 78.9).

**(3) The resolution of a reading is exact deduction.** A reading serves
(a) the value, where it is exact over ℚ; (b) the exact fraction `t/ℓ`;
(c) the exact rational point; (d) where a position on a continuous scale
is asked of a point that has no exact mark, the SECTOR between two exact
marks that the point lies in, decided by comparison. The ℚ-PROTRACTOR is
the set of marks whose `cos²` is rational — Niven's set `{1, 3/4, 1/2,
1/4, 0}`, the same five rationals `half_angle` keys — that is 0°, 30°,
45°, 60°, 90°, 120°, 135°, 150°, 180° and their reflections; a rational
point is placed between two marks by comparing its `cos²` and its signs,
exactly. Finer marks are the `ℓ`-th roots of unity in `ℚ(ζ_ℓ)` (37.1,
Part VI): the reader names the resolution `ℓ` and the sector `k/ℓ` is
decided by exact comparison in that field. Worked, on the tree's own
letter: the (3,4,5) letter is the ray `3 + 4B`; its half-angle point is
(3/5, 4/5), `cos² = 9/25` outside Niven's set, so its order is infinite;
it turns by the double angle, whose point is `(9/25 − 16/25, 2·3·4/25)
= (−7/25, 24/25)`; `cos < 0`, `sin > 0`, `cos² = 49/625` lies between
`cos² 120° = 1/4` and `cos² 90° = 0`, so the turn lies strictly between
90° and 120°. That is the whole reading, and no decimal exists in it.
Resolution is raised by naming a larger `ℓ`, and every raise is exact:
PRECISION IS THE NUMBER OF EXACT MARKS, NEVER DIGITS AFTER A POINT.

**(4) Inverted mathematics.** The operator's phrase names the direction
the engine computes in: from the observed effect to the exact object that
produced it, by deduction, refusing where no exact object exists. Every
master already reads this way, and the phrase is now their common name:
a motor is known by its action and solved for exactly (78.41(3)); a
rotor's order is read from its class (15.3); an object is read back from
its key (M2's inverse, K6); a form's vertex is re-derived from its word
(law 12); a period is read as an lcm and never walked to a cap (78.43);
a constant is read from its provenance (78.8); a body's pose is the versor
between its shape and the gauge (law 11); a signal is comprehended by
re-projection on the receiver's own charts (78.44(5)). The inverse
problem is solved exactly or the residual is the demand (law 7); it is
never fitted, and a forward computation from a guessed value is (2)'s
third kind.

**(5) What this binds.** Law 4 carries the reading clause. The
vocabulary's turn and DG1 are corrected: an infinite-order turn is served
as its point and its sector, never a decimal. MU-STANDARDS 4.2 lists the
two lints that carry the rule and 4.4 the review item — a decimal
approximation of an irrational anywhere in the tree, in a value, a doc
line or a test name, is an approximation and returned. Every audit from
this date asks, beside 78.41(2′)'s three questions, a fourth: IS ANYTHING
SERVED THAT IS NOT EXACT. This is no row; the rule governs every row.

### 78.46 Lift and drag: the perturbed orbit as the summation of the physics (ruled 2026-09-25, the operator's word through the implementor; two clauses posed back to the operator)

**The operator's word.** "In orbit you have lift and drag … every orbit
should be slightly different based on the push/pull of the star/planet
alignment … the orbital mechanics are a summation of all physics we have
combined into one combinatorial definition." And, on the implementor's
matching of census strings to report AT1's acceptance: lift is a PHYSICS
COMPONENT — a combination of two axioms, constructed by the engine at
runtime, never asserted from outside by matching strings.

**(1) What the tree reads today is the unperturbed orbit.** A circuit's
holonomy is the closed product of its own overlaps' motors, one route at
a time (78.41(3), R4). Every neighbour's push and pull is switched off:
the two-body orbit. Two circuits reading identical holonomies is
therefore evidence that PERTURBATION IS ABSENT, not that anything about
them is equal, and no acceptance can be read on it — least of all by
matching printed lines (78.45(2), MU-STANDARDS 4.6). The identical
readings are the expected reading BEFORE (4)'s producer lands, and they
are served by name: "unperturbed".

**(2) The push and pull is a neighbour's generator, refracted to the
orbit.** Inside one anastomosis (R3: routes are compared inside one cell
and never across the form) the bodies act on one another through their
tethers `V = s_b s_a` (A.10) and a contact's transport is the refraction
`(θ_bθ_a⁻¹)·V` (A.16). A neighbouring circuit's holonomy, based at the
orbit's basepoint by its lasso (R5, T2), is a motor whose MODES (MR1) are
commuting rays, each turning in one plane by a turn (DG1); each mode's
plane is a bivector blade `B_n` with `B_n² ∈ ℚ*`. The orbit's own mode
is the blade `B_o`. Conjugation by `B_o` is an involution on bivectors
(`B_o²` is a central scalar), so every neighbouring generator splits
EXACTLY over ℚ into a part that commutes with the orbit and a part that
anticommutes with it:

```
B_∥ = ½ (B_n + B_o B_n B_o⁻¹)      B_o B_∥ = B_∥ B_o
B_⊥ = ½ (B_n − B_o B_n B_o⁻¹)      B_o B_⊥ = −B_⊥ B_o
```

- **DRAG is `B_∥`.** It acts in the orbit's own mode: it changes the
  RATE along the orbit — the phase and the period — and never the plane.
  Its readings the document already holds: the beat at the transition
  (78.26(5), 78.41(3)), resonance where the periods are commensurate
  (78.43: the eon), and what does not return in a period, which is
  recorded and never relaxed away — the dislocation on the word, the
  flux retained or lost to contraction on the kinetic ledger, per lane
  (A.8, 78.42). The two axioms drag combines: A.16 (the neighbour's
  action reaches the orbit through the contact's transport) with A.8
  (torsional persistence: the strain it leaves is moved or recorded).
- **LIFT is `B_⊥`.** Its content is the commutator `[B_o, B_n] = 2 B_o
  B_⊥`: a rotation in a plane that neither generator is (60.4, `[p, p]
  ⊂ k`, Thomas precession; 62's conjugate pair, which is well-formed
  exactly when its halves fail to commute). It TILTS the orbit's plane —
  the precession of the orbital elements (LC1), the eccentric offset the
  vocabulary's turn overlays on the orbit — and never its rate. The two
  axioms lift combines: A.16 (the same refraction) with the algebra's
  commutator law (60.4, 78.11's congruence by commutator, 78.39's
  openings as commutators). Lift is orthogonal to the motion and drag
  is along it, exactly as in a fluid, and the decomposition is the
  algebra's, not an analogy.

Neither is a scalar. Each is an exact bivector with an exact weight, and
a turn asked of either is read as DG1 reads a turn — the point and its
sector — off the ray `B_o B_n`, never a formed angle.

**(3) Alignment is the same decomposition read as a pair.** Two orbits
are ALIGNED where `B_⊥ = 0` (commuting modes: pure drag; where their
periods are commensurate they resonate, 78.43; their composite's spectrum
is then the arithmetic of the two, the one case 78.44(3) allows it),
ORTHOGONAL where `B_∥ = 0` (pure lift, the commutator whole), and in
general both, each part exact. No angle between orbits is formed and no
scalar "alignment" exists (law 5's shape: two readings, never one
number). THE STAR, answered by the operator 2026-09-25 (77.1(2)): "the
star is the axioms that provide the physics required for the planets to
allow their entities/mycelium-clients (kernels) to do their reasoning."
The star is the AXIOM REGISTER — the physics every planet is given
(`physics/axioms/`, 56, 72, 79); a PLANET is a hypha and the world it
hosts, its entities the mycelium-client kernels that reason on it (80's
planetary dialect is theirs). The coordinator's first reading — the star
as the court's syllabus, its minerals as generators in the orbit
algebra — is WITHDRAWN: the syllabus is the hardening path (80.2), not
the star. The axioms do not enter the orbit algebra as generators; they
are the LAWS every composite in it obeys — conservation per lane (78.42),
torsional persistence (A.8), refraction (A.16), the commutator law — so
a planet's alignment with its star is how its orbits stand under the
register, and the push and pull BETWEEN orbits is lift and drag, read
inside one anastomosis (2). Every planet shares the one star; 80.2's
"radius from the star" names no measure and is withdrawn.

**(4) The summation is the orbit algebra, and the perturbed orbit is
derived in it.** "A summation of all physics combined into one
combinatorial definition" is what 78.11 and 78.44(3) already rule: the
bracket-closed ℚ-algebra of the generators of EVERY circuit through the
anastomosis — the axioms not among them: they are the laws the composite obeys (3) — held by its generators, its
rank the capacity, every route kept (79, T1). A circuit's PERTURBED
holonomy is its own generator composed in that algebra with its
neighbours': its unperturbed motor, times the drag terms (commuting, the
rate), times the lift terms (the commutators, the tilt), the spectrum
re-read off the composite and never an arithmetic of spectra. It is
DERIVED at every stroke where the circuit is read — the census, the
observer's circuit line, the pivot's trial under pressure (78.7) — and
never stored (78.41(2′): the atlas holds the coordinate list, the
algorithms derive). Because every neighbour differs, every orbit reads
slightly differently — the operator's expectation — and where the algebra
holds one generator the reading is "unperturbed" by name. THE PRODUCER IS
AT1 (iii), the algebra by generators, which gains three readings: lift
and drag per (circuit, neighbour) pair inside one anastomosis, the
perturbed holonomy per circuit, and the sum as readings — never as a
scalar — into the mind's orbital elements per epoch (LC1). No row of its
own. POSED TO THE OPERATOR (b): whether lift's two axioms are A.16 with
the commutator law and drag's A.16 with A.8, as (2) pairs them, or two
others of the register.

**(4′) How the perturbed holonomy is composed (ruled 2026-09-25 on the
implementor's shape question; "times the drag terms, times the lift
terms" in (4) was loose and is replaced).** The terms `B_∥`, `B_⊥` are
bivectors and are READINGS; nothing turns them into versors. The
neighbour already has its versor — its holonomy — so the composite is
made of motors the engine holds, by the register's own theorems:

- **Per pair, T1 and C1(a).** For a circuit `o` and a neighbour `n` in
  one anastomosis, both based at one basepoint by their lassos (R5, T2),
  the PAIR COMPOSITE is `H(o, n) = H_n⁻¹ · H_o`, a versor product, exact.
  It is identity (one ray) exactly when the two routes agree; where they
  enclose 2-cells of the anastomosis T2 gives it as the ordered product of
  the lasso-conjugated curvatures. That is the perturbed holonomy of `o`
  against `n`, and LIFT and DRAG are its readings: the split of `n`'s mode
  blades against `B_o` (2), the drag read as the change of `o`'s turn in
  its own plane (`Turn` of the composite against `Turn` of `H_o`), the
  lift as the commutator `[B_o, B_n] ≠ 0`, the plane tilted.
- **The summation over all neighbours is the algebra, never one product.**
  A product over several neighbours needs an order, and no order is
  given: the orbit algebra held by its generators, its rank the capacity,
  IS the combination (78.11, 78.44(3)); the `n` pair composites give every
  pair by C1(a) (`H(i, j) = H_j⁻¹ H_i`) with no pairwise walk.
- **Refused:** a Cayley transform of each term (a versor invented from a
  reading, and the grouping a choice — 77(1)); factoring a neighbour's
  ray as `Ω_∥ · Ω_⊥` (no such factorisation exists in general, and where
  it does it re-derives what the pair composite already holds); lift and
  drag printed with no reader in the mind (77.1: costume).
- **Where the mind consumes it** (the first draft of this bullet,
  written the same day, is CORRECTED on the implementor's two readings,
  both right). (i) A VACUUM circuit's based holonomy is the identity ray,
  so its pair composite with `n` is exactly `ρ_n⁻¹`: filing it "curved
  by comparison" files `n`'s class a second time under another circuit —
  one fact on two carriers (law 12), no content gained. Withdrawn. What
  stands of it: a trivial circuit is KEPT beside the orbits as the
  reading it is, never dropped at the gate (law 7), and a cell's circuits
  read FLAT together where every pair composite is the identity (C1(b):
  the content is route-independent there). The new content of a pair is
  held where it already is: the product of two curved generators lies in
  the orbit algebra's bracket closure, and nothing is filed per pair.
  (ii) THE PIVOT'S TRIAL reads the pair composites by LAW 10'S CLOSURE
  RULE, which already says it — "the coordinate it acted on is zero, no
  other rose": a move that turns a pair composite which WAS the identity
  into a non-trivial one broke an agreement between routes that agreed,
  so another coordinate rose, and the trial refuses the move by name
  (`unclosed`, counted). A pair composite already non-trivial before the
  move does not refuse it — the literal reading "any non-trivial pair
  composite refuses" deadlocked every cell of two curved circuits
  (discharging either leaves the other's inverse) and is withdrawn.
  Every composite is checked against the register's laws (conservation
  per lane, A.8, A.16, the commutator law), a violation a counted refusal
  with its content. THE READING that accepts (iii): on the corpus, pivots
  refused `unclosed` that the unperturbed trial admitted, and the cells
  read flat and curved by their pair composites.

**(5) AT1 (i)+(ii)'s acceptance, re-stated; "lift" named apart.** The
coordinator's acceptance clause read "every circuit of the old basis
present as its per-frame lifts", using LIFT in the sheaf's sense — a
section carried to a frame — where the tree already has A.11's harmonic
lift (`blade::lift`, the single producer of the multipoles) and the
operator now names the physics component. That use is withdrawn: in this
document LIFT is the physics component of (2); A.11's producer is "the
